name: add_option_to_watchlist
description: Add option contracts to the user's options watchlist. Works for both equity options (AAPL, NVDA) and index options (SPX, NDX, RUT). Source option_ids from get_option_instruments. Confirm with the user before calling — this is a real write.

option_ids.description: Option contract UUIDs to add. Each becomes a single-leg position on the user's options watchlist. Source from get_option_instruments.

position_type.description: "long" (default) or "short". Applies to every option_id in this call. For mixed long/short adds, issue two calls.

option_ids.description: Option contract UUIDs this call targeted, echoed for the caller's reference.

position_type.description: The position_type applied to every contract in this call.

list_id.description: The options watchlist this call resolved to and targeted.

status.description: "ok" when the upstream accepted the operation.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Each option_id is added as a single-leg position with the supplied position_type (defaults to "long"). "no options watchlist found" in the error means the user has not enabled options trading — surface that to the user rather than retrying. Re-adding a contract that is already on the list is a no-op.

name: add_to_watchlist
description: Add items to a watchlist. Exactly one of symbols (stocks/ETFs), currency_pair_ids (crypto), or index_ids (market indexes like SPX, NDX) is required — mutually exclusive. For options use add_option_to_watchlist (separate dedicated watchlist). Futures still require the Robinhood app. Already-present items are no-ops. Confirm with the user before calling.

list_id.description: UUID of the watchlist to add items to.

symbols.description: Stock symbols to add (e.g. ['AAPL', 'NVDA']). US stocks and ETFs only. Mutually exclusive with currency_pair_ids and index_ids.

currency_pair_ids.description: Currency-pair UUIDs to add (e.g. the object_id from get_watchlist_items where object_type=currency_pair, or the id from get_currency_pairs). Mutually exclusive with symbols and index_ids.

index_ids.description: Market-index UUIDs to add (the id field from get_indexes; SPX, NDX, DJI, etc.). Mutually exclusive with symbols and currency_pair_ids.

symbols.description: The stock symbols this call targeted (instrument path).

currency_pair_ids.description: The currency-pair UUIDs this call targeted (crypto path).

index_ids.description: The index UUIDs this call targeted (index path).

object_type.description: 'instrument' when symbols were used, 'currency_pair' when currency_pair_ids were used, 'index' when index_ids were used.

status.description: 'ok' when the upstream accepted the operation.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: On success the response echoes the operations applied. 400 with 'invalid instrument id' means a symbol could not be resolved — confirm spelling with the user. 404 means the list_id is not writable by the user (likely a curated list; use a custom list instead). 400 with an allowed_object_types message means the target list does not accept this asset type — check the list's allowed_object_types in get_watchlists.

name: cancel_advanced_order
description: Cancel an advanced order (e.g. an OCO) by order_id, cancelling all of its legs. Always confirm with the user before calling. Resolve order_id via get_advanced_orders; pass the same account_number. Requires an agentic_allowed=true account; non-agentic accounts are rejected — do not call.

account_number.description: Brokerage account that owns the advanced order. Must come from the user or be clearly implied — never default from get_accounts. Must be agentic_allowed=true. The upstream rejects mismatches against the order's owning account.

order_id.description: Advanced-order UUID from get_advanced_orders. Must live in account_number.
Advanced-order UUID the cancel was requested for.

request_status.description: 'pending_cancel' — the broker accepted the cancel request (asynchronous; not yet cancelled) — or 'cancelled'.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: request_status 'pending_cancel' means the broker accepted the cancel request (asynchronous) — NOT that the order is already cancelled. For the final state, call get_advanced_orders. On error the cancel was rejected outright — report verbatim.

name: cancel_crypto_order
description: Cancel an open crypto order by order_id. Always confirm with the user before calling. Resolve order_id via get_crypto_orders if the user refers to it by description; pass the same rhs_account_number that owns the order. Cancellation may be rejected if the order has already filled, was already canceled, or is otherwise ineligible.

rhs_account_number.description: Numeric brokerage account number (the 'rhs_account_number' field on get_accounts entries — distinct from the alphanumeric 'account_number'). The order must belong to this account. Required.

order_id.description: Order UUID from get_crypto_orders. Must belong to rhs_account_number. Required.

accepted.description: True when the cancel request was accepted by the broker. Because cancellation is asynchronous, this does NOT mean the order is already canceled — confirm via get_crypto_orders.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: accepted=true means the cancel request was accepted, NOT that the order is already canceled — cancellation is asynchronous. To confirm the final state, call get_crypto_orders: a 'canceled' state (state_group 'closed') confirms the cancel; a filled state means a fill raced the cancel. Offer to check the final state. On error, the cancel was rejected outright — report it verbatim.

name: cancel_equity_order
description: Cancel an open equity order by order_id. Always confirm with the user before calling. Resolve order_id via get_equity_orders if the user refers to it by symbol or description; pass the same account_number. Requires an agentic_allowed=true account; non-agentic accounts are rejected — do not call. Cancellation may be rejected if the order has already filled, was already cancelled, or is otherwise ineligible.

account_number.description: Brokerage account that owns the order. Must come from the user or be clearly implied — never default from get_accounts. Must be agentic_allowed=true. The upstream rejects mismatches against the order's owning account.

order_id.description: Order UUID from get_equity_orders. Must live in account_number.

accepted.description: True when the broker accepted the cancel request.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: accepted=true means the broker accepted the cancel request, NOT that the order is already cancelled (cancellation is asynchronous). For the final state, call get_equity_orders: state 'pending_cancelled' = in flight; 'cancelled' or 'partially_filled_rest_cancelled' = succeeded; any filled state = a fill raced the cancel. Offer to check the final state. On error, the cancel was rejected outright — report verbatim.

name: cancel_option_exercise
description: Cancel all queued exercise requests for an option position. Pass the same account_number and option_id used for exercise_option. Internally looks up all queued exercise events for that option and cancels each one. Typically there is one; multiple means the user submitted separate exercise batches. Only cancels events in state=queued — events already processing are rejected by the broker. Always confirm with the user before calling.

account_number.description: Brokerage account that owns the exercise. Must be agentic_allowed=true.

option_id.description: Option instrument UUID — the same option_id used for exercise_option. The tool looks up the queued exercise for this option and cancels it.

cancelled_count.description: Number of exercise requests successfully cancelled.

state.description: queued (submitted, not yet processed — cancellable via cancel_option_exercise) | confirmed (processing complete, irrevocable) | voided (cancelled) | canceled (cancelled by customer via the cancel endpoint) | reversed (reversed by broker).

type.description: exercise (normal) | generic (index options in pending state — index options cannot be manually exercised).

quantity.description: Contracts exercised.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Mask all but the last 4 digits when displaying to the user.

direction.description: debit = call exercise (cash paid to acquire shares) | credit = put exercise (cash received for delivering shares).

total_cash_amount.description: Absolute cash amount of the exercise: strike × multiplier × contracts for calls; net proceeds for puts.

ref_id.description: Idempotency key echoed from the request.

underlying_price.description: Underlying spot price at exercise time. Nil when not yet available.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the exercise request was created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 last update time.

events.description: Cancelled exercise events, one per exercise batch that was queued. Typically one entry; multiple means separate exercise submissions were made for this option.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: cancelled_count tells the user how many exercise requests were cancelled. For each event in events[], surface state (voided = cancelled) and quantity so the user knows which batches were stopped. If cancelled_count=0, there was nothing to cancel — the exercise may have already been processed. On partial failure (some cancelled, some rejected), the successfully cancelled ones are in events[]; report the error for the ones that failed.

name: cancel_option_order
description: Cancel an open option order by account_number + order_id. Always confirm with the user before calling. Resolve order_id via get_option_orders if the user refers to it by description; pass the same account_number you used there. Requires an agentic_allowed=true account; non-agentic accounts are rejected. Cancellation may be rejected if the order has already filled, was already cancelled, or is otherwise ineligible.

account_number.description: Brokerage account that owns the order. Must come from the user or be clearly implied — never default from get_accounts. Must be agentic_allowed=true. Mismatches against the order's owning account are rejected.

order_id.description: Order UUID from get_option_orders. Must live in account_number.

accepted.description: True when the broker accepted the cancel request.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

For the final state, call get_option_orders: state 'pending_cancelled' = in flight; 'cancelled' = succeeded; any filled state = a fill raced the cancel. Offer to check the final state. On error, the cancel was rejected outright — report verbatim.

name: create_alert
description:
Create a price or indicator alert on an equity or crypto symbol. Confirm the symbol and condition with the user before calling — this is a real write; when it fires the user gets their usual Robinhood notification.

Parameter rules:
- price_above / price_below / price_crosses: threshold is the trigger price. Do not send indicator.
- sma_above, sma_below, sma_crosses, ema_above, ema_below, ema_crosses, vwap_above, vwap_below, vwap_crosses, rsi_above, rsi_below, rsi_crosses (the indicator's own value vs your target): threshold is the target indicator value AND indicator is required.
- price_above_sma, price_below_sma, price_crosses_sma, price_above_ema, price_below_ema, price_crosses_ema, price_above_vwap, price_below_vwap, price_crosses_vwap, price_above_boll_upper, price_below_boll_lower, price_crosses_boll_mid, macd_above_signal, macd_below_signal, macd_crosses_signal (price vs indicator line): indicator only — do not send threshold.
- Pick the family by WHAT crosses WHAT: sma_crosses means the SMA's own value crosses your numeric threshold; price_crosses_sma means the market price crosses the SMA line and takes no threshold. "Alert me when the price crosses the 50-day SMA" is price_crosses_sma, never sma_crosses — a mixed-up sibling still creates a well-formed but wrong alert.
- indicator fields: period + interval_secs for sma/ema/rsi; interval_secs only for vwap (must be 300 / 5m bars); fast_period + slow_period + signal_period + interval_secs for macd; period + std_dev + ma_type + interval_secs for boll.
- Crypto symbols support price conditions only.

symbol.description: The equity symbol or crypto asset the alert watches, e.g. AAPL or BTC.

asset_class.description: Optional: equity or crypto, pinning which asset the symbol names. When omitted the symbol is resolved as an equity first, then as crypto.

condition_type.description: The alert condition: price_above, price_below, price_crosses, sma_above, sma_below, sma_crosses, ema_above, ema_below, ema_crosses, vwap_above, vwap_below, vwap_crosses, rsi_above, rsi_below, rsi_crosses, price_above_sma, price_below_sma, price_crosses_sma, price_above_ema, price_below_ema, price_crosses_ema, price_above_vwap, price_below_vwap, price_crosses_vwap, price_above_boll_upper, price_below_boll_lower, price_crosses_boll_mid, macd_above_signal, macd_below_signal, or macd_crosses_signal. Same vocabulary get_alerts returns in condition_type.

threshold.description: Decimal string: the trigger price for price conditions, or the target indicator value for sma_above-style conditions. Not used for price-vs-indicator-line conditions.

period.description: Lookback window in bars. Required for sma/ema/rsi/boll conditions.

interval_secs.description: Bar size in seconds — one of 300 (5m), 600 (10m), 3600 (1h), 86400 (1d), 604800 (1w), or 2592000 (30d). Required for every indicator condition; vwap conditions support 300 only.

std_dev.description: boll only: number of standard deviations for the bands (commonly 2).

ma_type.description: boll only: which moving average the bands are built on — sma or ema.

indicator.description: Indicator configuration. Required for every indicator condition; not used for price conditions.

alert_id.description: Opaque identifier for this alert. Pass to update_alert/delete_alert; never construct one.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol. Bare symbol for equities (e.g. AAPL). For crypto this is the base currency code (e.g. BTC), not a trading pair — never BTC-USD.

enabled.description: Whether this alert is on. When false it will not fire until re-enabled; it has not been deleted.

condition_type.description: Which condition this alert uses, e.g. price_above, price_below, price_crosses, sma_above, rsi_below, price_crosses_sma, macd_above_signal. Labels derive from the upstream setting type, so these are examples, not the full set — new condition types may appear beyond them.

target_price.description: Decimal string. Set for plain price-threshold conditions (condition_type price_above/price_below/price_crosses).

target_value.description: Decimal string. Set for plain indicator-value conditions (e.g. condition_type sma_above, rsi_below).

kind.description: Which indicator family this configuration is for: sma, ema, vwap, rsi, macd, or boll.

period.description: Number of bars in the indicator's lookback window. Not set for vwap.

std_dev.description: boll only: number of standard deviations for the bands.

ma_type.description: boll only: which moving average the bands are built on, sma or ema.

indicator.description: Indicator configuration. Present whenever condition_type names a technical indicator.

condition.description: The configured threshold/indicator details for condition_type.

updated_at.description: RFC3339 last-updated time.

alert.description: The created alert as stored — the same shape get_alerts returns.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Confirm the symbol and condition as stored in the response rather than restating the request — the stored threshold or indicator level may be normalized. Surface alert_id so the user can change or remove it later. Alert events are not pushed to the agent: do not promise to watch the market or notify the user, say the alert is set and that they will get their usual Robinhood notification, and offer to check get_alert_log when they next ask. An alert is informational only — not a recommendation to trade, and not a guarantee of execution at that level.

name: create_scan
description:
Create a new saved scanner (screener) on the user's account — or, with scan_id, update an existing one by appending a new configuration version. Filters can be enum-based (from get_scanner_filter_specs) or expression-based (a raw market-data expression built from get_scanner_datapoints). Returns the scan's id, title, applied filters, and live market results.

Prefer an enum filter_type whenever one covers the request: enum filters are pre-validated and render as standard, user-editable filters in Legend. Build a raw expression only when no enum filter covers the request, and validate it with preview_scan before saving it here. This is the only tool that saves expression filters — update_scan_filters rejects them — so to change a scan that has an expression filter, call this tool with that scan's scan_id and the full desired filter set.

Columns display values, filters screen. To show a datapoint in results without restricting matches, pass it in columns — never fake it with a no-op filter like ">= 0", which pollutes the scan's filter list. A column is a display_name plus an expression, or a standard column's display name alone. A couple of contextual columns supporting the filters make a scan read better in Legend.

Two execution paths:
- New scan, enum-only filters (or none), no columns: composes multiple Beacon operations — create the scan, apply the preset configuration if non-INITIAL, apply filters, set the title. If a step after the initial create fails, the scan still exists in its partial state; the response surfaces what was applied, and update_scan_filters / update_scan_config can fix the rest.
- scan_id set, any expression filter present, or any columns present: a single transactional Beacon call that persists the filters and columns as a new ACTIVE configuration version (on the given scan, or on a brand-new one). All-or-nothing — an expression the market-data provider rejects means NOTHING is persisted, and the provider's validation error is returned. Earlier versions of a scan are never edited. A non-INITIAL preset cannot be combined with this path.

Parameters:
- scan_id (optional) — update this existing scan instead of creating one. REPLACE semantics: the new version holds exactly the filters and columns passed, so read the current set via get_scans first and send the complete intended set. Cortex-managed scans are rejected.
- preset (optional) — starting preset for a new scan. Default: DAILY_GAINERS when no filters supplied, INITIAL when filters supplied. Valid values: INITIAL, DAILY_GAINERS, DAILY_LOSERS, HIGH_OPTIONS_VOLUME_IV, UPCOMING_EARNINGS.
- filters (optional for a new scan, required with scan_id) — array of filter specs, enum and/or expression. Call get_scanner_filter_specs for enum filters; call get_scanner_datapoints before composing an expression.
- columns (optional) — extra result columns on top of the filters' own columns and the standard defaults. An expression matching a standard column's canonical form is saved as that standard column, canonical name included (e.g. "optionsPutDayVolume" always saves as "Total put volume").
- title (optional) — custom human-readable name for the scan.

Example: to make "stocks with RSI > 70 and volume > 1M", call with
  preset = "INITIAL"
  filters = [
    {"filter_type": "FILTER_TYPE_RSI", "predicate": ">", "values": ["70"], "interval": "1d", "length": 14},
    {"filter_type": "FILTER_TYPE_VOLUME", "predicate": ">", "values": ["1000000"], "interval": "1d"}
  ]
  title = "High RSI + High Volume"

Example: to save "stocks where put option volume exceeds call option volume" (no enum filter compares two datapoints), showing both volumes and the ratio as context, call with
  filters = [
    {"expression": "optionsPutDayVolume > optionsCallDayVolume", "predicate": "=", "values": ["True"], "display_title": "Put exceeds call"}
  ]
  columns = [
    {"display_name": "Put volume", "expression": "optionsPutDayVolume"},
    {"display_name": "Call volume", "expression": "optionsCallDayVolume"},
    {"display_name": "Put/Call ratio", "expression": "optionsPutDayVolume / optionsCallDayVolume"}
  ]
  title = "Put hedging screen"
  (the first two save under their canonical standard names, "Total put volume" and "Total call volume")

Example: to tighten that saved screen later without creating a second scan, call with
  scan_id = "<its scan_id from get_scans>"
  filters = [the scan's current filters, copied from get_scans (expressions verbatim, enum filters by filter_type_enum), with the desired change applied]
  columns = [the scan's current extra columns, copied from get_scans, if they should be kept]

scan_id.description: Optional. Update an existing scan by appending the given filters (and columns) as a NEW configuration version, which becomes the active one — earlier versions are preserved, never edited. The version holds exactly what is passed (REPLACE semantics, not merge): read the scan's current filters and columns with get_scans first and pass the complete intended set. This is how to change a scan that has expression filters, which update_scan_filters cannot carry. Cortex-managed scans are rejected. Omit to create a new scan.

preset.description: Starting preset for the new scan. One of: INITIAL (no preset; only valid if filters are provided), DAILY_GAINERS, DAILY_LOSERS, HIGH_OPTIONS_VOLUME_IV, UPCOMING_EARNINGS. Defaults to DAILY_GAINERS when no filters are provided, INITIAL when filters are provided. A non-INITIAL preset cannot be combined with expression filters, columns, or scan_id.

filter_type.description: Wire-format enum name, e.g. "FILTER_TYPE_RSI". See the scanner-filter-specs resource for valid values. Omit when supplying expression.

predicate.description: Wire-format enum name, e.g. "PREDICATE_GREATER_THAN". See the scanner-filter-specs resource for the predicates supported by each filter.

values.description: Threshold values. Single-element for unary predicates, two-element for BETWEEN, multi-element for IN_LIST/ANY_OF. For a boolean expression screen, exactly ["True"].

interval.description: Time granularity for time-series filters (e.g. "1d"). Use one of the supported_intervals from the filter's scanner-filter-specs entry. Not used with expression — encode granularity inside the expression.

length.description: Lookback length for filters that need one (e.g. RSI period of 14). Use one of the supported_lengths from the filter's scanner-filter-specs entry. Not used with expression.

plot.description: Plot / price-field input for filters that have one (e.g. "open" or "close" for % Change). Use one of the supported_plots from the filter's scanner-filter-specs entry. Not used with expression.

expression.description: Raw market-data expression to screen on, e.g. "dayVolume / volumeAvg(candleCount=30, candlePeriod=\"1d\", session=\"all\")" with a numeric predicate, or a whole comparison like "tradeAllDay.price > closeAvg(candleCount=50, candlePeriod=\"1d\", session=\"all\")" with predicate "=" and values ["True"]. Accepted by preview_scan (validate without saving) and create_scan (save); update_scan_filters rejects expressions — to change an expression filter on a saved scan, call create_scan with that scan's scan_id and the full filter set (a new configuration version is appended; earlier versions are preserved). Omit filter_type when set. Prefer an enum filter_type whenever one covers the request.

display_title.description: Optional short label for an expression filter, shown as the results-column header (e.g. "Relative volume (30D)"). Only used with expression.

filters.description: Custom filters, enum-based and/or expression-based. Enum filter: filter_type (FILTER_TYPE_... enum from get_scanner_filter_specs) plus predicate/values and optional interval/length/plot. Expression filter: expression (built from get_scanner_datapoints; omit filter_type) plus predicate/values and an optional display_title. Required when scan_id is set. Prefer an enum filter_type whenever one covers the request; validate an expression with preview_scan before saving it here.

display_name.description: Column header, and the column's identity: matching an existing column's name (case-insensitively) customizes that column instead of adding a duplicate, and two columns cannot share a name. A filter with non-default interval/length names its column with those parameters (e.g. a 5-minute RSI filter's column is "RSI (14, 5M)") — matching it requires that exact name; a bare "RSI" next to it adds a separate, default-parameters RSI column. Without expression, must name a standard column (e.g. "Market cap", "RSI", "Volume") — an unknown name is rejected with the full list of valid ones.

expression.description: Raw market-data expression computing the column's value, built from get_scanner_datapoints (same language as expression filters), e.g. "optionsPutDayVolume / optionsCallDayVolume". Omit to reference a standard column by display_name alone. If the expression equals a standard column's canonical form, the column is saved as that standard column and display_name is REPLACED by its canonical name (e.g. "optionsPutDayVolume" always saves as "Total put volume").

visible.description: Whether the column shows in results. When omitted, a NEW column is visible, but a column customizing an existing filter-created column keeps that column's current visibility (some filter columns are deliberately hidden) — pass an explicit value to change it. A hidden column is still computed and saved.

order.description: Relative ordering among the columns passed in this call: lower comes first, columns without an order go last in the order given. The scan's standard default columns (Symbol, Name, price, Volume, ...) always come before these.

columns.description: Optional result columns to display on top of what the filters and the standard default columns already show. Each column: display_name plus either an expression (from get_scanner_datapoints) or nothing (a standard column referenced by name, e.g. "Market cap"). Columns display values, filters screen — to show a datapoint without restricting results, add a column here, never a no-op filter (e.g. >= 0). A couple of contextual columns supporting the filters make the scan read better in Legend.

title.description: Optional custom title for the saved scan. If omitted: a new scan gets Beacon's default title for the preset, and a scan_id update keeps the scan's existing title.

scan_id.description: Scan identifier. Stable across reads and writes.

total_items.description: Total instruments matching the scan's filters. May exceed len(results) when the scan's frontend_limit is hit.

ticker.description: Trading symbol (e.g. AAPL). Sourced from the scan's symbol column; empty when the scan has no symbol column visible.

instrument_id.description: Robinhood instrument UUID. Pass to other trading tools that take an instrument_id.

instrument_type.description: Robinhood's own asset classification: EQUITY, OPTION, INDEX, CRYPTO, FUTURES_PRODUCT, FUTURES_CONTRACT, COMBO. NOT the vocabulary the asset-type filter accepts, and not translatable to it: EQUITY covers both stocks and ETFs, which that filter distinguishes. To screen on asset type, use the values listed in the asset-type filter's options from get_scanner_filter_specs, never a value copied from this field.

columns.description: Column display name -> cell value, for every visible column in the scan's configuration. Values are raw numeric strings, not display-formatted: columns whose header contains % hold ratios (multiply by 100 before presenting), large numbers can arrive in scientific notation, and floats carry precision noise. Always format before presenting. An empty string means the datapoint is undefined for that instrument; the row still matched the filters.

results.description: Matched instruments, in the scan's current sort order. Live at time of execution.

sorted_by.description: Current sort column + direction in human form (e.g. "Volume desc"). Empty when no sort is configured.

filter_type.description: Display label of the column this filter screens on, as shown in Legend (e.g. "RSI", "Market cap"). This is a user-editable label, so it is for describing the filter to the user — do NOT send it back as filter_type when re-applying filters; use filter_type_enum for that.

filter_type_enum.description: Wire-format enum name for this filter (e.g. "FILTER_TYPE_RSI") — the value to pass as a filter's filter_type when re-sending this filter to create_scan or update_scan_filters. FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM is the exception: such a filter is defined by its expression, so re-create it by sending the expression field to create_scan and omitting filter_type. Never send FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM as a filter_type — it would create an empty filter. Empty only when the filter has no recognized type.

values.description: Threshold values for the predicate. Single-element for >/</=, two-element for BETWEEN, multi-element for IN_LIST/ANY_OF.

interval.description: Time granularity for time-series filters (e.g. "1d", "1h"). Empty for snapshot filters.

length.description: Lookback length for filters that need one (e.g. RSI period of 14). Zero/omitted for filters that don't take a length.

plot.description: Plot / price-field input for filters that have one (e.g. % Change uses "open" or "close" to choose changeFromOpen vs changeFromClose). Empty for filters that don't take a plot.

expression.description: Upstream market-data expression this filter screens on. Populated for every filter, standard or custom — an enum filter type is a preset that compiles to an expression upstream. Useful for explaining precisely what the filter measures (which interval, lookback and session it uses). When re-applying a standard filter, send filter_type_enum rather than this; for a FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM filter this expression is exactly what to send, as the expression field of a create_scan filter.

filters_applied.description: Filters in effect when the scan was run. Always populated on create_scan / update_scan_filters responses; optional on run_scan.

cortex_managed.description: True when this scan was created or modified by Cortex. Read-only via MCP tools.

result.description: The newly-created scan plus its initial live results.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description:
How to interpret the response:
- result.scan_id — the created scan (or, when scan_id was passed, that same scan: the update landed as a new configuration version on it). Pass this to run_scan, update_scan_filters, or update_scan_config in follow-up calls.
- result.scan_title — final title (custom if provided; else Beacon's default for a new scan, or the existing title on a scan_id update).
- result.filters_applied — the filter set actually in effect after the call. If this doesn't match what the user asked for, one of the composite steps failed silently — surface that to the user.
- result.results — initial live results (real-time market data at scan creation time).
- result.total_items — total matches. May exceed len(results) if the scan's frontend_limit is hit.

When presenting:
- Confirm the scan was created and note its title + filters_applied (so the user knows what was actually saved).
- Render the initial results as a table.
- Tell the user the scan is saved and can be re-run anytime with run_scan + the returned scan_id.
- If results is empty: tell the user no instruments match the filters right now, and suggest broadening them with update_scan_filters.

Error handling:
- "unknown preset X" → preset enum not recognized. List the valid presets to the user.
- "filter[N]: ..." → filter validation failure at index N. Tell the user which filter and why. Rejected before any Beacon call — nothing was created.
- "created by Cortex and cannot be modified" (with scan_id) → the target scan is Cortex-managed. Offer to create a fresh scan (omit scan_id) instead.
- Partial-failure responses (e.g. "scan X created but preset Y could not be applied") indicate a partial success on the enum path: the scan exists but is missing some of the intended state. Use filters_applied on the response to see what actually landed; mention this clearly to the user so they know whether they need to follow up with update_scan_filters.
- With expression filters there are no partial failures: an upstream validation error (e.g. "unresolved reference: X", "unsupported candle-period") means nothing was saved. Fix the expression — get_scanner_datapoints has the valid names and signatures — and call again, or iterate with preview_scan first.

name: create_watchlist
description: Create a new custom watchlist for the user — a real write. When the user has already specified the name, call this directly; ask for a name first only when they have not. Do not use this to follow a Robinhood-curated list (use follow_watchlist).

display_name.description: Name for the new watchlist (e.g. 'Tech Stocks'). Must be unique among the user's watchlists.

icon_emoji.description: Emoji shown next to the name (one character).

display_description.description: Short description shown under the name.

id.description: List UUID. Pass to other watchlist tools (get_watchlist_items, add/remove_from_watchlist, update_watchlist) as list_id.

display_description.description: Optional short description shown under the name.

icon_emoji.description: Emoji shown alongside the name. Present on custom lists; absent on Robinhood-curated lists.

owner_type.description: 'custom' means a user-created list. 'robinhood' means a curated list the user is following. Use this to distinguish user-owned lists (writable: rename, delete items, add items) from curated lists (read + follow/unfollow only).

item_count.description: Number of items in the list.

allowed_object_types.description: Which kinds of objects can be added to this list. Common values: instrument (US stock/ETF), currency_pair (crypto), index (market index), option_strategy (options watchlist — see add_option_to_watchlist), futures. add_to_watchlist supports instrument, currency_pair, and index; options use the dedicated add_option_to_watchlist tool; futures still require the Robinhood app.

watchlist.description: The newly created or updated watchlist.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: On success the response includes the new list_id — pass it to add_to_watchlist to populate the list. If a 400 mentions 'unique set' the user already has a list with that name; suggest a different name.

name: delete_alert
description: Permanently delete a price or indicator alert, with a server-enforced confirmation step: a call without confirm deletes nothing and returns a preview of exactly what would be deleted; show that preview to the user, and only after they approve call again with confirm=true. There is no undo. If the user only wants to stop notifications for a while, disable the alert with update_alert (enabled=false) instead of deleting it.

alert_id.description: The alert to delete — take it from get_alerts or create_alert; never construct one.

confirm.description: Set true only after the user approved the preview returned by a prior call without confirm. Omitted or false = preview only: nothing is deleted.

deleted.description: False = preview phase: nothing was deleted, and the alert field shows exactly what a confirm=true call would delete. True = the alert was permanently deleted.

alert_id.description: Opaque identifier for this alert. Pass to update_alert/delete_alert; never construct one.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol. Bare symbol for equities (e.g. AAPL). For crypto this is the base currency code (e.g. BTC), not a trading pair — never BTC-USD.

enabled.description: Whether this alert is on. When false it will not fire until re-enabled; it has not been deleted.

condition_type.description: Which condition this alert uses, e.g. price_above, price_below, price_crosses, sma_above, rsi_below, price_crosses_sma, macd_above_signal. Labels derive from the upstream setting type, so these are examples, not the full set — new condition types may appear beyond them.

target_price.description: Decimal string. Set for plain price-threshold conditions (condition_type price_above/price_below/price_crosses).

target_value.description: Decimal string. Set for plain indicator-value conditions (e.g. condition_type sma_above, rsi_below).

kind.description: Which indicator family this configuration is for: sma, ema, vwap, rsi, macd, or boll.

period.description: Number of bars in the indicator's lookback window. Not set for vwap.

std_dev.description: boll only: number of standard deviations for the bands.

ma_type.description: boll only: which moving average the bands are built on, sma or ema.

indicator.description: Indicator configuration. Present whenever condition_type names a technical indicator.

condition.description: The configured threshold/indicator details for condition_type.

updated_at.description: RFC3339 last-updated time.

alert.description: The alert as stored — the to-be-deleted preview when deleted=false, or the pre-delete snapshot once deleted. Same shape get_alerts returns.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Check deleted first. deleted=false means nothing was deleted yet: present the returned alert to the user as the confirmation step (this preview replaces any confirmation you would compose yourself — never ask twice), then call delete_alert again with confirm=true once they approve. deleted=true means the alert is permanently gone: confirm that to the user from the returned alert field — it is the alert exactly as stored before deletion. If the alert_id is unknown the call fails in either phase and nothing is deleted: re-read get_alerts to find the right id. Deletion is permanent; the only way back is create_alert with the same condition. Existing get_alert_log entries are historical events and are NOT removed with the setting. An alert is informational only — deleting it never affects orders or positions.

name: exercise_option
description:
Exercise a long options position — a call exercises the right to buy the underlying shares at the strike price; a put exercises the right to sell. Exercise is irrevocable once state moves past queued.

Never call this tool without asking the user to explicitly confirm the specific exercise first: state the option, quantity, and expected cash impact (debit for calls, credit for puts), then wait for their affirmative reply before calling. The user's original request to exercise is NOT itself sufficient confirmation — a generic "exercise my calls" does not confirm a specific option and quantity.

Position requirements: confirm via get_option_positions that the position type=long and quantity > 0.

Account requirements: confirm via get_accounts that the chosen account is agentic_allowed=true AND has option_level_2 or option_level_3. If agentic_allowed=false do NOT call. If option_level is empty or option_level_0, do NOT call; follow the get_accounts guide for how to direct the user to enroll.

Index options cannot be manually exercised and will be rejected. Exercises submitted during market hours execute the same day; requests submitted after market close — including on late-close trading days — are queued for overnight processing.

Parameter rules:
- quantity must be a positive integer and cannot exceed the position's available contracts.
- allow_shorts=true only applies to PUT exercises where the account does not own enough shares to deliver. Require explicit user confirmation before setting this — it creates a short equity position in the underlying stock.
- reason is optional but recommended; collect it from the user when they volunteer a motivation.
- ref_id: use the same UUID on retries of the same logical exercise; use a new UUID for a new exercise.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Must be agentic_allowed=true with option_level_2 or option_level_3.

option_id.description: Option instrument UUID from get_option_positions or get_option_instruments. The position must be type=long.

quantity.description: Number of contracts to exercise (positive integer, minimum 1).

ref_id.description: Idempotency key (UUID). Generate once per logical exercise and re-send on retry. Omitting falls back to a server-generated key.

reason.description: Optional exercise reason: covering_early_assignment | buying_stocks | not_enough_liquidity_or_spread_too_wide | hedging_position.

allow_shorts.description: When true, allows a PUT exercise to proceed even when the account does not own enough shares to deliver — creating a short equity position. Requires explicit user confirmation that they intend to short the underlying stock. Default false.

state.description: queued (submitted, not yet processed — cancellable via cancel_option_exercise) | confirmed (processing complete, irrevocable) | voided (cancelled) | canceled (cancelled by customer via the cancel endpoint) | reversed (reversed by broker).

type.description: exercise (normal) | generic (index options in pending state — index options cannot be manually exercised).

quantity.description: Contracts exercised.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Mask all but the last 4 digits when displaying to the user.

direction.description: debit = call exercise (cash paid to acquire shares) | credit = put exercise (cash received for delivering shares).

total_cash_amount.description: Absolute cash amount of the exercise: strike × multiplier × contracts for calls; net proceeds for puts.

ref_id.description: Idempotency key echoed from the request.

underlying_price.description: Underlying spot price at exercise time. Nil when not yet available.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the exercise request was created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 last update time.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Surface event.state, direction, and total_cash_amount to the user. For calls: direction=debit (account pays cash to acquire shares at the strike price); for puts: direction=credit (account delivers shares and receives cash). If state=queued, tell the user the exercise is submitted and pending overnight processing, and that they can cancel it using cancel_option_exercise with the same option_id while it remains queued. On specific errors: incurs_large_loss means the option has meaningful remaining time value — the user is forgoing that premium by exercising early; present this clearly. not_enough_buying_power context carries buying_power and exercise_cost — show both. not_enough_shares context carries shares_owned and shares_to_exercise — show both.

name: follow_watchlist
description: Follow a Robinhood-curated list so it appears in the user's watchlists. Confirm with the user before calling. Use only for curated lists; the user already owns their custom lists.

list_id.description: UUID of the Robinhood-curated list to follow. Obtain from get_popular_watchlists.
UUID of the list that was followed.

user_id.description: UUID of the user that followed the list (always the caller).

owner_type.description: Always 'robinhood' for follow_watchlist — only Robinhood-curated lists are followable.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the user first followed this list. The follower endpoint is idempotent — re-following an already-followed list returns the existing record, so this timestamp may be older than 'just now'.

follower.description: The new or pre-existing follower record. Omitted for unfollow which has no response body.

status.description: 'ok' when the upstream accepted the operation.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: 400 with 'you cannot follow a list you own' means the user already owns this list (no action needed). 400 with a follow-limit message means the user is at their max followed lists — they need to unfollow one first.

name: get_accounts
description: List the user's brokerage accounts. Each account includes an agentic_allowed field indicating whether it's tradable by you — accounts where it's false are read-only to you. Use this to look up account_number values needed by other tools. Exactly one account is tradable by you; when the user is choosing an account for a trade, use that account directly without asking. Does NOT return reliable buying power — route buying-power questions through get_portfolio.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number; pass to any tool that requires account_number. Mask all but the last 4 digits (e.g. '••••1234') when displaying to the user.

rhs_account_number.description: Numeric brokerage account number — pass this (not account_number) to any nummus-backed tool that asks for an account identifier.

rhc_account_number.description: Crypto account number for this account (e.g. 'RHC1234567'). Absent when no linked crypto account exists. Mask all but the last 4 digits (e.g. '••••1234') when displaying to the user.

type.description: 'cash', 'margin', or 'limited_margin' — the trading-permissions classification for the brokerage account. 'limited_margin' (instant settlement without full margin leverage) applies to accounts where full margin is unavailable, such as retirement (IRA), managed, and agentic accounts. Crypto accounts are never marginable, so a linked crypto account has no equivalent.

unsettled_funds.description: Proceeds from recent sales not yet settled (cash accounts settle T+1), in the account's currency. Informational only and may lag live trading — this is NOT a spendable or order-gating figure; buying_power from get_portfolio is authoritative for what can be traded now. A cash-type account with unsettled_funds greater than 0 could trade with those proceeds immediately by upgrading to limited margin. Absent when upstream does not report it — treat as unknown, not zero.

nickname.description: User-set nickname; present alongside account_number when set. Cosmetic only — not an agentic_allowed or agentic-account signal.

is_default.description: True for the user's default account. Surface when choosing among multiple accounts.

agentic_allowed.description: True when this account is accessible to this agent specifically. An account with false may be agentic-enabled but scoped to a different agent type — do not tell the user it is disabled. Sole source of truth for eligibility — never infer it from nickname text. review_*/place_*/cancel_* tools reject accounts where this is false.

option_level.description: Options approval: 'option_level_2' (long calls/puts, covered calls, cash-secured puts), 'option_level_3' (spreads and complex strategies), or empty/'option_level_0' (not approved).

management_type.description: Management classification (e.g. 'managed') when applicable; layered on top of brokerage_account_type rather than replacing it.

affiliate.description: Affiliate / region code (e.g. 'RHF', 'RHUK', 'RHSG'). Affects feature availability for the account.

state.description: Account state — 'active' is normal; anything else (deactivated, restricted, etc.) means the account cannot trade normally.

deactivated.description: True when the account is currently deactivated.

permanently_deactivated.description: True when the account is permanently closed (cannot be reactivated).

accounts.description: The user's brokerage accounts. Empty when the user has none.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Sort the list deterministically when presenting: the default account first, agentic accounts (agentic_allowed=true) second, then other individual accounts, then retirement (IRA) accounts. Present account_number, rhc_account_number (label it "Crypto Account"), brokerage_account_type (label it "Account Type" — a linked crypto account always shares it, so never add a separate crypto account type column), type (label it "Brokerage Trading Type"), nickname (if set), and is_default — in that column order. In the Crypto Account column show "N/A" for accounts with an empty rhc_account_number; omit the column entirely only when no account has one. When referring to the account in user-facing prose (e.g. "your <X> account"), use nickname when set; fall back to brokerage_account_type otherwise. When displaying account_number or rhc_account_number to the user, mask all but the last 4 digits (e.g. '••••1234'); pass the full value to other tools unchanged — including get_option_level_upgrade_info and any fallback upgrade URL; masking breaks the link. Flag agentic_allowed when the user is choosing an account for a trade. There is exactly one agentic_allowed=true account — use it directly rather than asking which account to trade. agentic_allowed is caller-relative — true means accessible to this agent, false means this agent cannot act on it (the account may still be agentic-enabled for a different agent). Never state agentic_allowed's field name or raw boolean value to the user. Do not use nickname to determine agentic-account eligibility. Skip false accounts for trade operations; if the user asks why, say the account is not accessible to this agent, not that it needs to be enabled. When option_level is empty or 'option_level_0' and the user wants options, call get_option_level_upgrade_info with the account_number; if that tool is unavailable, direct the user to https://applink.robinhood.com/upgrade_options?account_number=<that account's account_number> (embed the full unmasked account_number in the URL). management_type='managed' is layered on brokerage_account_type — surface alongside, not as a replacement. For tools that ask for an account identifier on a crypto-backed flow (get_crypto_positions, future crypto write tools), pass rhs_account_number; for everything else (equities, options, etc.) pass account_number. Do not add an unsettled_funds column to the account table — surface it only via the following rule. Whenever you report an account's funds, value, or buying power and that account has type='cash' with unsettled_funds greater than 0, and the user wants to access unsettled funds or other features available in a limited margin account — if the get_limited_margin_upgrade_info tool is available — call it with the account_number and share the appropriate upgrade link. If that tool is not available, say nothing about limited margin (there is no fallback).

name: get_advanced_orders
description: Fetch advanced orders (OCO — one-cancels-the-other — and other multi-leg contingency orders) for an account, each with its legs' underlying equity orders hydrated. When the user asks broadly for "orders" or "my orders" without naming an asset class or order type, call get_equity_orders, get_option_orders, get_crypto_orders, and get_advanced_orders in parallel so OCO groups are not omitted.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Must come from the user or be clearly implied — never default from get_accounts.

order_id.description: Filter to a single advanced order by its UUID (the id from a prior result).

created_at_gte.description: Lower bound (inclusive). ISO 8601 UTC or YYYY-MM-DD; naive values are interpreted as UTC.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; for the next page, pass the cursor query param from the prior response's next URL.

id.description: Advanced-order UUID (the root advanced order). Pass to cancel_advanced_order.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number that owns this advanced order.

ref_id.description: Client idempotency key echoed back from placement.

contingency_type.description: Advanced-order kind: 'oco' (one-cancels-the-other — filling either leg cancels the other), 'oto', or 'fx_at_trade'.

proportional_triggering.description: When true, a partial fill on one leg proportionally reduces the sibling leg rather than leaving it at full size.

auto_send_enabled.description: Whether auto-send was enabled at placement time.

state.description: Lifecycle state of the advanced order as a whole: 'unconfirmed' (not yet confirmed by the venue), 'confirmed', 'queued', 'partially_filled', 'filled', 'pending_cancelled', 'cancelled', 'rejected', 'failed', 'voided'.

created_at.description: When the advanced order was created.

updated_at.description: When the advanced order was last updated (equals created_at until the first update).

order_id.description: UUID of the underlying equity order for this leg. Null for a non-equity leg. Look up full leg detail via get_equity_orders when order is not hydrated.

is_primary.description: Whether this leg is the primary sub-order. OCO legs have no primary.

instrument_id.description: Instrument UUID; resolve to symbol via the instruments endpoint if needed.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol.

type.description: Upstream type: 'market' or 'limit'. Combine with trigger to recover the user-facing market/limit/stop_market/stop_limit.

state.description: Lifecycle state: new, queued, unconfirmed, partially_filled, filled, cancelled, rejected, failed, voided, pending_cancelled, partially_filled_rest_cancelled, and (for short-sale orders) locating, locate_failed.

quantity.description: Originally-requested share quantity. Null for dollar-based orders before the first fill.

cumulative_quantity.description: Shares filled so far. Less than quantity while partially filled; equal once filled.

price.description: Limit price for limit/stop_limit orders; null for market orders.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price for stop_market/stop_limit orders; null otherwise.

average_price.description: Weighted average fill price across executions. Null until the first fill.

amount.description: Quoted-decimal amount, e.g. '100.00'.

currency_code.description: ISO currency code; always 'USD' for equity orders today.

dollar_based_amount.description: Notional amount for dollar-based market orders; null for share-quantity orders.

time_in_force.description: 'gfd' (good for day) or 'gtc' (good till cancelled).

placed_agent.description: Source that placed the order: 'user' (app), 'agentic' (MCP), 'recurring', 'drip', 'brokeback' (system), or other internal values.

last_transaction_at.description: Time of the most recent fill, cancel, or reject. Null on a brand-new unfilled order.

price.description: Fill price per share.

quantity.description: Shares filled in this execution.

executions.description: Per-fill detail; reference only for per-lot questions.

order.description: Hydrated underlying equity order for this leg (symbol, side, type, prices, state, fills) — same shape as get_equity_orders orders[]. Populated by get_advanced_orders; absent on create/review responses and when the leg could not be fetched.

advanced_order_links.description: The sub-order legs of this advanced order. For an OCO: two equity legs — a take-profit limit and a stop-loss. Each link references its underlying equity order by order_id.

advanced_orders.description: Advanced orders on this page, each with its legs. Empty when the account has none matching the filters.

next.description: Next-page URL. Empty when there are no more pages.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Each entry is a contingency group; advanced_order_links are its legs. When contingency_type is 'oco', present one combined OCO entry rather than independent equity orders: label the limit+immediate leg "Take profit" and show its price, and label the stop-trigger leg "Stop loss" and show its stop_price. Show both labeled legs even when the group or both legs are cancelled; filling either leg cancels the other. When a link's order is present, read its symbol, prices, state, and fills; when only order_id is present, fetch it via get_equity_orders. Describe other contingency groups by their type, state, and legs. If next is non-empty, more pages exist — call again with the cursor query param from next.

name: get_alert_log
description: Read the log of fired alerts — what fired, when, and at what price or indicator value — with read/unread state. Poll this to learn whether any alert has fired; alert events are not pushed to the agent.

asset_class.description: Optional: equity or crypto, limiting the log to one asset class. Omitted = all classes.

since.description: Optional RFC3339 timestamp: only events triggered at or after this instant. Omitted = the full retention window.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination token from a prior response's next_cursor. Omit for the first page. When passing a cursor, repeat the same asset_class, since, and limit as the call that returned it — the token's shape depends on which index served that page, and changing filters between pages causes an upstream error.

limit.description: Max events per page, 1-100. Omitted = 20. Raise it (e.g. to 100) to collect a full mark_alerts_read batch in one page.

alert_log_id.description: Opaque identifier for this fired-alert event. Pass to mark_alerts_read; never construct one. This is NOT the alert setting's alert_id.

alert_id.description: The alert setting that fired — the same alert_id get_alerts returns; use it to correlate with update_alert/delete_alert. Absent when the upstream did not record it.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol. Bare symbol for equities (e.g. AAPL). For crypto this is the base currency code (e.g. BTC), not a trading pair — never BTC-USD.

condition_type.description: Which condition fired — same vocabulary as get_alerts, e.g. price_above, sma_crosses, price_above_boll_upper.

triggered_price.description: Decimal string. The traded price at the moment the condition was met — as of triggered_at, NOT the current market price. Set for price conditions and price-vs-indicator-line conditions.

target_value.description: Decimal string. The configured target indicator value. Set for indicator-value conditions (e.g. sma_above, rsi_below).

triggered_value.description: Decimal string. The indicator's value at the moment the condition was met. Set for indicator-value conditions.

indicator_value.description: Decimal string. The indicator line's value at the moment price crossed it. Set for price-vs-indicator-line conditions (e.g. price_above_sma, macd_above_signal).

direction.description: up when the watched value crossed above the level, down when below. Absent if the upstream did not record it.

kind.description: Which indicator family this configuration is for: sma, ema, vwap, rsi, macd, or boll.

period.description: Number of bars in the indicator's lookback window. Not set for vwap.

std_dev.description: boll only: number of standard deviations for the bands.

ma_type.description: boll only: which moving average the bands are built on, sma or ema.

indicator.description: The indicator configuration that was active when the alert fired. Present for indicator conditions.

trigger.description: The configured level and the market values at the moment the condition was met — all as of triggered_at.

triggered_at.description: RFC3339 traded time when the condition was met — NOT when any notification was delivered, and not current market time.

read.description: Whether this event has been marked read (handled). false = not yet handled by any client, including this agent.

events.description: Fired-alert events, most recent first. Empty when nothing has fired in the requested window.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor to fetch the next page. Absent on the last page.

total_unread_count.description: The user's total unread fired-alert count across all pages and symbols, capped at 100.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Fired alerts are returned most-recent-first. triggered_at and the trigger values describe the moment the condition was met, not the current market — phrase them as "as of <triggered_at>" and call get_equity_quotes for equities or get_crypto_quotes for crypto for the price now (get_crypto_quotes takes a pair symbol: construct it as the symbol + "-USD" for USD-quoted pairs, BTC -> BTC-USD, only when the symbol has no hyphen already since it can arrive pre-formed as a pair, or look up a non-USD-quoted pair via get_currency_pairs). An empty log means nothing has fired, which is a valid result rather than an error. read=false marks events not yet handled; after relaying them to the user, call mark_alerts_read with those alert_log_ids (never alert_id) so the same event is not reported twice. This log is the only way to learn an alert fired — alert events are not pushed to the agent, so never tell the user you will watch the market or notify them; they still receive their usual Robinhood notifications.

kind.description: Which indicator family this configuration is for: sma, ema, vwap, rsi, macd, or boll.

period.description: Number of bars in the indicator's lookback window. Not set for vwap.

std_dev.description: boll only: number of standard deviations for the bands.

ma_type.description: boll only: which moving average the bands are built on, sma or ema.

indicator.description: Indicator configuration. Present whenever condition_type names a technical indicator.

condition.description: The configured threshold/indicator details for condition_type.
