alerts.description: The user's configured alerts. Empty when the user has none set.

next_cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page. Omitted when there are no more alerts.

alert_limit_reached.description: Only present when filtering by symbol: true when that asset is already at its per-asset alert cap, so creating another alert on it would be rejected. Absent on unfiltered calls — absence does not mean there is headroom.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Alerts are returned grouped by symbol (alphabetically), newest-created first within each symbol. An empty alerts list means the user has no alerts set — a valid result, not an error. Pass alert_id to update_alert or delete_alert; never construct one. Equity alerts carry a bare symbol (AAPL) and crypto alerts the base currency code (BTC, never BTC-USD) — route to get_equity_quotes for equities or get_crypto_quotes for crypto when the user asks how close an alert is to firing, since no live price is included here; get_crypto_quotes takes a pair symbol, so construct it as the symbol + "-USD" for USD-quoted pairs (BTC -> BTC-USD) — append "-USD" only when the symbol has no hyphen already, since it can arrive pre-formed as a pair — or look up a non-USD-quoted pair via get_currency_pairs. Surface enabled=false before telling the user an alert is watching the market.

name: get_crypto_account_onboarding_info
description: Get the link a user opens to sign the crypto agreement and open a crypto account. Call when the user wants to trade crypto but has no crypto account.

already_onboarded.description: True when the user already has at least one crypto account — onboarding_url is empty and no signup is needed. False when they have none and should open the link to sign up.

onboarding_url.description: Link for the user to sign the crypto agreement and open a crypto account. The user must log in to their Robinhood account at the link to sign. Present it as a tappable link; never call it programmatically. Empty when already_onboarded is true.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: If already_onboarded is true, the user already has a crypto account, so no new signup is needed — do NOT present a link (the signup link cannot create or re-activate an account when one already exists). Tell them they already have a crypto account; do not claim it is active or ready to trade. If they say they still cannot trade crypto, their account may be deactivated, which is a separate reactivation flow this tool does not cover — direct them to Robinhood support rather than the link. Otherwise, send onboarding_url to the user as a tappable link, and tell them they must log in to their Robinhood account at the link to review and sign the crypto user agreement. After they sign, their crypto account(s) are provisioned — this tool does not create the account or sign on the user's behalf. Signing provisions crypto accounts for all of the user's eligible brokerage accounts, so a user who has an agentic brokerage account also gets an agentic crypto account. Once the user confirms they have finished, call get_accounts again with a fresh request to pick up the new crypto account before retrying; do not reuse a prior get_accounts result, as the account does not exist until the user completes this flow.

name: get_crypto_orders
description:
List crypto order history for an account — newest first. Open and closed orders, including fills, cancellations, and rejections. Pass order_id to retrieve a single order by UUID.

Filtering tips:
- Prefer narrow queries: combine state (or state_group), symbol, and/or created_at_gte for specific questions.
- created_at_gte: interpret relative times in the user's timezone, convert to UTC before sending.
- updated_at_gte: useful when polling for order fills or state transitions.
- symbol triggers a symbol→currency_pair_id lookup; omit it if you don't need it.

When the user asks broadly for "orders" or "my orders" without naming an asset class or order type, call get_equity_orders, get_option_orders, get_crypto_orders, and get_advanced_orders in parallel so OCO groups are not omitted.

For requests spanning all accounts, re-fetch the account list with get_accounts first — a list from earlier in the conversation may be missing newly created accounts.

rhs_account_number.description: Numeric brokerage account number (the 'rhs_account_number' field on get_accounts entries — distinct from the alphanumeric 'account_number'). Required.

order_id.description: Filter to a single order by UUID. The response shape is unchanged (results[] with at most one entry); empty when the order does not belong to the account.

state.description: Filter by single state: queued, confirmed, partially_filled, filled, canceled, rejected, failed, voided. For open-vs-closed shortcuts, use state_group instead.

state_group.description: Filter by state group: 'open' or 'closed'. Quick shortcut — 'open' covers queued/confirmed/partially_filled, 'closed' covers filled/canceled/rejected/failed/voided. Mutually exclusive with state.

symbol.description: Filter by crypto symbol (e.g. 'BTC', 'ETH', or 'BTC-USD'). Triggers a symbol→currency_pair_id lookup before the orders call.

created_at_gte.description: Lower bound (inclusive) on created_at. ISO 8601 UTC; naive values are interpreted as UTC.

updated_at_gte.description: Lower bound (inclusive) on updated_at. ISO 8601 UTC. Useful for polling for fills — each state transition bumps updated_at.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; for the next page, pass the cursor query param from the prior response's next URL.

rhs_account_number.description: Echo of the brokerage account number this page was queried with. Every order in results belongs to this account — when querying multiple accounts in parallel, attribute orders using this echo, not memory of which call was which.

crypto_account_number.description: Crypto account number (e.g. 'RHC1234567') these orders belong to. Present THIS as the account to the user — not the brokerage account number used to look it up. When absent, refer to the account as the user's linked crypto account.

ref_id.description: Client-supplied idempotency key from order placement. Useful for reconciling agent-placed orders against records the agent kept.

account_id.description: Crypto account UUID this order belongs to. Matches the account_id on get_crypto_positions rows.

currency_pair_id.description: Pair UUID (e.g. BTC-USD). Pass to get_crypto_quotes for current price, or match against get_currency_pairs.id.

currency_code.description: Asset currency code (e.g. 'BTC', 'ETH'). Useful for grouping orders by coin without joining against get_currency_pairs.

type.description: 'market', 'limit', 'stop_loss', or 'stop_limit'. 'stop_loss' is a stop-triggered market order — despite the name it applies to buy stops too; the equity/option tools call the same concept 'stop_market'. ALWAYS call these by their app names when speaking to the user, including when listing what types are supported: 'stop_loss' is a 'stop order' and 'stop_limit' a 'stop limit order'; the raw values are tool inputs only.

state.description: Raw lifecycle state: new, queued, unconfirmed, confirmed, partially_filled, filled, canceled, rejected, failed, voided. Combine with derived_state for clearer end-state classification.

derived_state.description: Normalized lifecycle classification, e.g. 'open' / 'closed' / similar shorthand the upstream computes from raw state + fills. Prefer over state for user-facing summaries.

state_group.description: 'open' or 'closed' — the headline answer to 'is this order still working?'.

time_in_force.description: 'gtc' (good till canceled), 'gfd' (good for day), 'ioc' (immediate or cancel), 'gfw' (good for week), 'gfm' (good for month).

quantity.description: Originally-requested asset quantity. On dollar-based orders the server derives it at placement: from the quote for market and from the stop price for stop_loss (treat those as estimated until fills confirm them), and from the limit price for limit/stop_limit (exact at placement).

cumulative_quantity.description: Total asset quantity filled so far. Less than quantity while partially filled; equal once filled.

canceled_quantity.description: Quantity that was canceled before fill (only populated on partial-fill-then-cancel paths).

price.description: Order price (interpretation depends on type — limit price for limit; for stop_loss it is the collared worst-case execution bound, NOT the trigger, which lives in stop_price; for market it is the raw quote side-price on a preview_crypto_order response — the same price the app displays, NOT collared — but the collared worst-case execution bound on placed orders; stablecoin pairs are never collared, so their preview and placed prices both carry the raw quote). Use limit_price / stop_price for the unambiguous fields.

limit_price.description: Limit price for limit / stop_limit orders. Null for market / stop_loss.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price for stop_loss / stop_limit orders. Null for market / limit.

average_price.description: Volume-weighted average fill price across executions. Null until the first fill.

entered_price.description: Price the user originally entered (pre-collaring). Different from limit_price after server-side collaring adjusts the order.

rounded_executed_notional.description: Total notional filled so far in the quote currency, rounded to 2 decimals.

price.description: Reported fill price per unit asset (e.g. USD per BTC). For the price the user actually paid after venue adjustments, use effective_price.

effective_price.description: Per-unit price after venue fees or price adjustments are applied — closer to the user's realized fill economics than price.

quantity.description: Asset quantity filled in this execution.

notional.description: effective_price * quantity, rounded to 2 decimals where applicable.

exchange_name.description: Routing venue name. Treat as informational; do not surface unless the user asks about routing.

executions.description: Per-fill detail. Reference for per-execution timing or price questions; for headline 'what did this fill at?' use average_price.

initiator_type.description: Source that placed the order: 'api_trading', 'trading_view', 'recurring', 'paycheck', 'rh_assistant', 'agentic_trading' (when nummus adds that enum value), or one of the internal crypto-specific values. Tells the user whether they placed this order via app, API, recurring buy, or an agent.

speculative.description: True when the order was created as a speculative pre-trade check (no upstream side effect). Should always be false on real placed orders; populated read-only by upstream.

updated_at.description: Last server-side state update (UTC) — fill, cancel, reject, etc.

canceled_at.description: When the cancel was acknowledged. Null when the order has not been canceled.

routing.description: How the order is routed for execution. Present verbatim as the routing line item; absent when routing information is unavailable.

rounded_estimated_notional_with_estimate.description: Estimated total cost (buy) or net proceeds (sell) in the quote currency, with ONLY the estimated fee already included. It does NOT include any additional taxes or deductions.

rounded_uncollared_estimated_notional_wi.description: Same as rounded_estimated_notional_with_estimated_fee but before price collaring. Null when collaring does not apply.

rounded_executed_notional_with_fee.description: Notional actually executed so far only including fees without netting additional taxes, in the quote currency. Grows as fills come in; 0 before the first fill. For the executed figure net of all taxes and fees use net_rounded_executed_notional.

total_executed_notional.description: Total executed notional so far only including fees without netting additional taxes. Null until there are fills.

net_rounded_estimated_notional.description: Estimated total cost (buy) or credit (sell) net of ALL taxes and fees. On a preview, present this as the estimated total cost or credit line item alongside the separate estimated_fee value. Never subtract the fee or taxes from it again. Null when an order has fills.

net_rounded_executed_notional.description: Executed total cost (buy) or credit (sell) net of ALL taxes and fees — the definitive amount actually debited or credited. Null before the first fill. Grows as fills come in. Never subtract the fee or any taxes from it again.

fee_structure.description: How the fee was computed (e.g. a fixed percentage or a volume-tiered rate).

fee_amount.description: Fee amount in the quote currency (USD).

fee_ratio.description: Rate this fee was computed at, when applicable.

fee_data.description: This fee's amount, type, and rate.

fees.description: Itemized fee breakdown for exchange-routed orders. Empty or absent when the order carries no itemized fees.

withholding_rate.description: Withholding rate preformatted as a percent (e.g. '24%'), aggregated across the federal and any state portion. Print verbatim. Absent when no rate is available.

estimated_withholding_amount.description: Estimated USD to be withheld from this sell's proceeds. Present only while cumulative_quantity is 0. Exactly one of this and total_withholding_amount is ever present, so read the one that is there.

total_withholding_amount.description: Actual USD withheld from proceeds across fills so far (final once fully filled). Present only once cumulative_quantity is positive. Exactly one of this and estimated_withholding_amount is ever present, so read the one that is there.

tax_withholding.description: Backup withholding on this sell order's proceeds. Present only when withholding applies (sell orders for subject users; never on IRA accounts) — when absent, do not mention withholding. amount and withholding_rate are the display-ready figure and percent.

fee.description: Fee for this order in the quote currency (USD on USD-quoted pairs) — an estimate before any fill; once filled, the amount collected on fills so far (final when fully filled). Absent when the order carries no itemized fees (typical of Market Maker Routing) — treat absence as no fee data, not a $0 charge.

fee_rate.description: Rate this order's fee was computed at, preformatted: the bare percent on single-rate fee pricing (e.g. '0.95%'), suffixed with the liquidity outcome on maker/taker-priced accounts — e.g. '0.05% maker', '0.1% taker', or '0.07% blended' for orders filled partly maker and partly taker. Absent when no fee rate applies.

results.description: Crypto orders on this page, newest first. Empty when the cursor has no rows.

next.description: Next-page URL. Empty when there are no more pages.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: For the headline answer to "is this order still working?", use state_group ('open' vs 'closed'); raw state has finer granularity if the user asks why. For the fill price the user cares about, use average_price (VWAP across fills). cumulative_quantity vs quantity tells "how much filled?"; canceled_quantity only appears on partial-fill-then-cancel paths. Asset symbol is currency_code; pair UUID is currency_pair_id. For current market, call get_crypto_quotes with the pair symbol (construct as currency_code + "-USD" for USD-quoted pairs, or look up via get_currency_pairs) — get_crypto_quotes takes the symbol, NOT currency_pair_id. initiator_type tells how the order was placed (app / API / recurring / agent) — surface it when the agent didn't place this order. Per-fill executions[] are omitted from list responses to keep the page sized for an agent's context window; pass order_id to retrieve a single order with executions populated. Present currency_code, side, type (ALWAYS translated to the app's name: stop_loss = "stop order", stop_limit = "stop limit order" — never show the raw stop_loss/stop_limit values to the user), state, quantity (or cumulative_quantity when partially filled), average_price once filled, backup withholding on a sell whenever tax_withholding is present, created_at, and id when cancellation may follow; suppress other fields unless asked. When presenting multiple orders, add a Fee column when any order on the page carries fee or fee_rate — the fee value verbatim (label it estimated when the order has no fills yet), with the fee_rate value appended verbatim in parentheses when present, e.g. '$1.23 (0.05% maker)' or '$1.23 (0.95%)' — fee_rate carries its own maker/taker/blended qualifier, never re-derive or re-label it; an order with fee_rate but no fee shows the bare rate; '-' for orders with neither; omit the column entirely when no order on the page has either. For a single order, state the fee and rate the same way when present. Backup withholding: show whichever of tax_withholding.estimated_withholding_amount / total_withholding_amount is present (exactly one ever is), labeled "Estimated backup withholding" for the estimate and "Backup withholding" for the total, with the tax_withholding.withholding_rate value appended verbatim in parentheses, e.g. '$23.88 (24%)'; on a partially filled order phrase the total as withheld so far — never as final, and never compute an estimate for the remainder. When presenting multiple orders, add a Withholding column only when at least one order on the page carries tax_withholding, with '-' for orders that do not; when none does, do not mention withholding at all. Answer total cost/credit questions from whichever net_* field the order carries, never from rounded_executed_notional / rounded_estimated_notional_with_estimated_fee / total_executed_notional — those are gross of taxes like backup withholding and will overstate a subject order. An order with no tax_withholding has no withholding — never raise the subject for it or show it as $0. Every order on this page belongs to the account echoed in rhs_account_number / crypto_account_number — when querying several accounts in parallel, attribute each order from its own response's echo, never from memory; identify the account to the user by crypto_account_number.

name: get_crypto_positions
description: List open crypto positions for a specific brokerage account. Returns asset, quantity, transferable amount, and cost-basis breakdown.

rhs_account_number.description: Numeric brokerage account number (the 'rhs_account_number' field on get_accounts entries — distinct from the alphanumeric 'account_number'). Required.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; for the next page, pass the cursor query param from the prior response's next URL.

account_id.description: Brokerage account UUID this position belongs to.

type.description: 'cryptocurrency' for crypto assets, 'fiat' for cash currencies.

currency.description: Asset currency this position holds. Use currency.code as the asset symbol.

currency_pair_id.description: UUID of the canonical pair quoted against USD (e.g. BTC-USD). Pass in the currency_pair_ids array to add_to_watchlist / remove_from_watchlist. For current price call get_crypto_quotes with the pair SYMBOL (construct as currency.code + "-USD"), not this UUID. Empty when no such pair exists for this asset (rare).

quantity.description: Total quantity held in asset units (e.g. BTC), net of pending withdrawal holds only. For the amount the user can actually sell right now, use 'quantity_transferable'.

quantity_transferable.description: Quantity available to sell or transfer right now — net of open sell orders, pending withdrawals, quarantine, and any other holds. This is the correct field for 'how much can I sell?', including for crypto purchased on instant funds. Strictly ≤ 'quantity'.

quantity_held_for_sell.description: Quantity locked by open outgoing sell orders.

direct_quantity.description: Quantity attributable to direct buys (excludes transfers and rewards).

direct_cost_basis.description: Total cost basis for direct_quantity (units of the quote currency, typically USD).

cost_bases.description: Direct-purchase cost basis. Tracks only the portion of the position that came from buys — quantity acquired via transfer, reward, or fork is not represented here, so sum(direct_quantity) can be less than the holding's quantity. Multiple entries appear after forks/splits (e.g. BCH/BSV).

results.description: Open crypto positions on this page. Empty when the cursor has no rows.

next.description: Next-page URL. Empty when there are no more pages.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Sellable quantity: use `quantity_transferable`, not `quantity` — `quantity_transferable` is the amount available to sell right now (already nets out open sell orders, pending withdrawals, holds, quarantine, and instant-funds restrictions); `quantity` only subtracts pending withdrawals. The two are equal in the common case but diverge when there are open sells or unsettled instant buys. Asset name comes from currency.code; for current price, call get_crypto_quotes with the pair symbol (construct as `currency.code + "-USD"` for USD-quoted pairs, or look up via get_currency_pairs) — note that get_crypto_quotes takes the symbol, NOT currency_pair_id. For per-unit average buy price, sum direct_cost_basis and sum direct_quantity across all cost_bases entries (multi-entry rows appear after forks like BCH/BSV) and divide — the average only covers direct purchases. When sum(direct_quantity) is materially less than quantity, the rest came from transfers, rewards, or forks with no captured cost basis; surface that the average buy price applies only to a subset of the units. The intraday_* fields isolate today's portion when the user asks about today specifically. Suppress cost_bases when not asked. No market price here — for current value or P&L, multiply the get_crypto_quotes result by quantity.

name: get_crypto_quotes
description: Get real-time bid/ask/mark prices plus the previous close for one or more crypto pair symbols (e.g. BTC-USD).

symbols.description: One or more crypto pair symbols (e.g. 'BTC-USD', 'ETH-USD'). Hyphenated and unhyphenated forms are both accepted on input; the response symbol field comes back unhyphenated.

timezone.description: Optional IANA timezone name (e.g. 'America/New_York', 'America/Los_Angeles') that anchors the previous-close (open_price) day boundary to the user's local midnight and sets the timezone the response timestamps (bid_time, ask_time, updated_at) are rendered in. Pass ONLY when the user's timezone is known from context — do NOT guess it, infer it from language, or default it. When omitted, the previous close is anchored to midnight US Eastern and timestamps are rendered in US Eastern. Must be a valid IANA name — not an abbreviation ('PST'), a UTC offset ('-08:00'), or 'Local'.

rhs_account_number.description: Optional numeric brokerage account number (the 'rhs_account_number' from get_accounts). When supplied, bid/ask/mark and the previous close are priced on this account's execution routing — the venues its orders actually fill at — and the applied routing is echoed in routing. When omitted, prices use the caller's own routing (it is set at the user level, so any of their crypto accounts yields the same routing). A caller with no crypto account, or an account that cannot be resolved, receives market-maker-routed pricing.

symbol.description: Crypto pair symbol returned by upstream in unhyphenated form (e.g. 'BTCUSD'). To cross-reference with get_currency_pairs.symbol (which is hyphenated, e.g. 'BTC-USD'), strip the hyphen from that field or insert one before the last 3 characters of this one.

id.description: Currency-pair instrument UUID. Pass in the currency_pair_ids array to add_to_watchlist / remove_from_watchlist — no separate get_currency_pairs call needed just to get the UUID. Also matches get_currency_pairs.id and the currency_pair_id on get_crypto_positions rows.

bid_price.description: Highest current buy-order price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable — do NOT present zero as a price.

bid_time.description: Timestamp of bid_price, rendered in the request timezone (the get_crypto_quotes 'timezone' parameter; US Eastern when not supplied). Present when the upstream included side timestamps; otherwise absent.

ask_price.description: Lowest current sell-order price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

ask_time.description: Timestamp of ask_price, rendered in the request timezone (the get_crypto_quotes 'timezone' parameter; US Eastern when not supplied). Present when the upstream included side timestamps; otherwise absent.

mark_price.description: Reference midpoint computed from bid and ask. Zero when both sides of the book are unavailable.

open_price.description: Previous close — the reference midpoint (same bid/ask-mid basis as mark_price) at the midnight day boundary of the request timezone (the get_crypto_quotes 'timezone' parameter; US Eastern when not supplied). Crypto trades continuously, so this boundary price is the prior day's close. Resets daily; NOT a last-trade price.

routing.description: Execution routing these prices are quoted on, matching the routing on get_crypto_orders rows. bid_price, ask_price, mark_price, and open_price are all priced on this routing. Absent when routing information is unavailable.

updated_at.description: Time this snapshot was last refreshed, rendered in the request timezone (the get_crypto_quotes 'timezone' parameter; US Eastern when not supplied) — the same zone that anchors open_price. Use to judge freshness — when stale, phrase as 'as of <time>' rather than 'current'.

results.description: One entry per requested symbol with live market data. Empty if no symbol resolved.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Current price: prefer mark_price when both sides of the book are populated; if mark_price is zero, fall back to the most recent of bid_time / ask_time and quote the side that updated last. Drop bid or ask when zero — the book is unavailable on that side. Use updated_at to judge freshness; if it is more than a few seconds stale, phrase as "as of <time>" rather than "current". open_price is the previous close — in continuous crypto the midnight boundary price is the prior day's close. That boundary is midnight in the request timezone (the 'timezone' parameter), or US Eastern when none is supplied; response timestamps carry that same timezone's offset, so quote "as of" times in it directly. For change vs the previous close, compute (mark_price - open_price) / open_price. The response symbol comes back unhyphenated (e.g. 'BTCUSD'); the canonical form from get_currency_pairs is hyphenated ('BTC-USD') — strip the hyphen to cross-reference. bid/ask/mark reflect the execution routing reported in routing: the supplied account's routing when rhs_account_number was given, otherwise the caller's user-level routing (market maker routing when the caller has no crypto account). This is informational; place_order routing is selected per account at order time.

name: get_currency_pairs
description: List Robinhood-supported crypto currency pairs (e.g. BTC-USD, ETH-USD), including any with an active trading halt. Catalog-only coins that Robinhood does not offer are excluded. Use this to discover symbols and per-pair order constraints before calling get_crypto_quotes or referencing positions.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; for the next page, pass the cursor query param from the prior response's next URL.

limit.description: Maximum number of pairs to return on this page (clamped to [1, 700]). Defaults to 25 to keep the response sized for an agent's context window; raise it when the user wants the full catalog and is OK with a larger response.

id.description: Currency-pair UUID. Pass to get_crypto_quotes via the symbol field, or match against the currency_pair_id on get_crypto_positions rows.

symbol.description: Canonical hyphenated symbol (e.g. 'BTC-USD'). Note: get_crypto_quotes returns the unhyphenated form (e.g. 'BTCUSD') in its symbol field; strip the hyphen here to cross-reference.

display_symbol.description: Display-only override for the symbol (rarely set). When empty, treat symbol as the display value.

type.description: 'cryptocurrency' or 'fiat'.

asset_currency.description: The asset side of the pair (e.g. BTC in BTC-USD).

type.description: 'cryptocurrency' or 'fiat'.

quote_currency.description: The quote side of the pair (typically USD).

tradability.description: Pair-level eligibility: 'tradable' (both sides open), 'buy_only', 'sell_only', 'untradable', or 'limited'. Resolved for the authenticated user across all their account types; per-account-type detail is in tradability_by_account_type.

tradability_by_account_type.description: Per-account-type tradability override (key e.g. 'individual', 'ira_roth', value as in tradability). Empty when only the headline applies.

display_only.description: True when the pair is shown for discovery but cannot be ordered.

min_order_size.description: Minimum order quantity in asset units (e.g. 0.00000001 BTC).

max_order_size.description: Maximum order quantity in asset units.

min_order_quantity_increment.description: Quantity step size — order quantities must be a multiple of this value.

min_order_price_increment.description: Limit-price step size — prices must be a multiple of this value.

min_order_quote_amount.description: Minimum order notional in the quote currency (USD). Null for unauthenticated callers or pairs without a notional floor.

market_orders_only.description: True when only market orders are accepted on this pair (no limit / stop variants).

type.description: Currency-pair type (typically 'cryptocurrency').

halted.description: True when this pair has an active halt in one or more regions right now. Convenience flag for halted_regions being non-empty. Derived from the /halts/summary/ endpoint at call time; distinct from tradability, which reflects standing eligibility rather than a live halt event.

halted_regions.description: Region codes where this pair currently has an active halt (e.g. ['NY','TX']). The sentinel 'ALL' denotes a global halt that applies to every region. Omitted when the pair is not halted. A region-scoped entry may be one-sided (e.g. sell-only) — do not assume the pair is fully suspended.

results.description: Robinhood-supported currency pairs on this page, including pairs with an active halt (halted=true). Catalog-only coins not offered by Robinhood are excluded. Empty when the cursor has no rows.

next.description: Next-page URL. Empty when there are no more pages.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Render pairs as a markdown table with columns: Symbol | Name | Pair ID | Min Order | Max Order | Min Increment | Min Price Increment | Min Notional | Mkt Only | Restrictions | Halted. Formatting: Symbol → symbol; Name → asset_currency.name (e.g. 'Aave', not the full pair name); Pair ID → id truncated to the segment before the first '-'; Min Order → min_order_size; Max Order → max_order_size with comma separators; Min Increment → min_order_quantity_increment; Min Price Increment → '$' + min_order_price_increment; Min Notional → '$' + min_order_quote_amount, or '—' when null; Mkt Only → 'Yes'/'No' from market_orders_only; Restrictions → halted_regions joined by ', ' ('ALL' = a global halt), or 'None' when empty; Halted → 'True' when halted else '—'. When Halted is True the pair has a live halt in the listed regions — it may be one-sided (e.g. sell-only) and should not be assumed freely orderable. Only Robinhood-supported pairs are listed; catalog-only coins Robinhood does not offer are already excluded.

name: get_earnings_calendar
description: List earnings reports scheduled across the market over a date window (up to 31 days), optionally limited to high-market-cap names. Returns one entry per report event — estimated/actual EPS, report date and timing (am/pm), and company-verification status. Use this for market-wide discovery ("what large-caps report this week?"). For a specific known ticker, use get_earnings_results instead. Read-only.

start_date.description: Window anchor, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today (US/Eastern) when omitted.

days.description: Window length in days, measured from start_date. Defaults to 7. Positive = forward window (e.g. 7 = the next 7 days, inclusive of start_date); negative = look-back window (e.g. -7 = the 7 days ending at start_date). Must be a non-zero value between -31 and 31 — windows wider than 31 days are rejected.

filter.description: Optional result filter. Set to 'high_market_cap' to limit the calendar to high-market-cap names (market cap over $1B) — useful for 'what large-caps report this week' style questions. Omit for all names.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol the earnings event belongs to.

estimate.description: Expected (estimated) EPS for the quarter. Null when no estimate is available for this quarter.

actual.description: Reported EPS for the quarter. Null for upcoming quarters (not yet reported) — pair with report.date to tell the two apart.

eps.description: Estimated and actual earnings per share for the quarter. Both sides may be null — see field docs.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD report date. Present whenever the parent report block is non-null — use the parent's null/non-null state, not this field, to detect 'no scheduled event'.

timing.description: 'am' (before market) or 'pm' (after market). Null when timing is not yet known — only distinguishes before/after market, not an exact time.

verified.description: True when the company has confirmed the report date. False when the date is tentative (not yet company-confirmed).

report.description: Report scheduling — date, am/pm timing, company-verification flag. Null when upstream has no scheduled event for this quarter yet.

results.description: Earnings report events in the window, one per company-quarter, sorted ascending by report date. Empty array when no reports fall in the window.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Each entry is one company's report event within the window, sorted ascending by report date. The window spans days from start_date (positive = forward, negative = look-back). Distinguish "upcoming" from "already reported" by eps.actual: null means not yet reported. When report.verified is false, present the date as tentative rather than confirmed. An empty results array means no reports fall in the window (with filter=high_market_cap, no high-market-cap names do) — not an error. This tool does NOT return an "expected move" — pair with options data for implied-volatility-based moves.

Use this for earnings-timing questions ("does AAPL report this week?"), EPS surprise analysis, and screening for upcoming earnings risk on a specific stock. For market-wide earnings calendar queries across many symbols, use get_earnings_calendar. Read-only.

symbol.description: Stock symbol to look up (one symbol per call). Exact-ticker match — no name or partial-ticker resolution. Lowercase and whitespace-padded input is normalized to uppercase-trimmed before forwarding. Returns the trailing up to 8 quarters of earnings for the symbol.
Ticker symbol the earnings event belongs to.

actual.description: Reported EPS for the quarter. Null for upcoming quarters (not yet reported) — pair with report.date to tell the two apart.

eps.description: Estimated and actual earnings per share for the quarter. Both sides may be null — see field docs.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD report date. Present whenever the parent report block is non-null — use the parent's null/non-null state, not this field, to detect 'no scheduled event'.

timing.description: 'am' (before market) or 'pm' (after market). Null when timing is not yet known — only distinguishes before/after market, not an exact time.

verified.description: True when the company has confirmed the report date. False when the date is tentative (not yet company-confirmed).

report.description: Report scheduling — date, am/pm timing, company-verification flag. Null when upstream has no scheduled event for this quarter yet.

guide.description: Entries are sorted ascending — historical quarters first, most recent / upcoming quarter last. name: get_equity_analyst_ratings

symbol.description: The requested ticker, in canonical uppercase form.

num_buy_ratings.description: Number of covering analysts rating the symbol Buy.

num_hold_ratings.description: Number of covering analysts rating the symbol Hold.

num_sell_ratings.description: Number of covering analysts rating the symbol Sell.

high_price_target.description: Highest individual analyst price target across covering analysts. Absent when price-target data is unavailable, even if the ratings counts are present.

low_price_target.description: Lowest individual analyst price target across covering analysts. Absent when price-target data is unavailable, even if the ratings counts are present.

mean_price_target.description: Average analyst price target across covering analysts. Absent when price-target data is unavailable, even if the ratings counts are present.

updated_at.description: When the most recent contributing analyst report was last revised (RFC3339). Absent when no report backs the current ratings.

ratings.description: Analyst price targets and ratings breakdown. Absent means no analyst coverage for this symbol.

results.description: Per-symbol analyst ratings, positionally aligned to the requested symbols (same order).

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: results is positional — aligned one-to-one with the requested symbols, in order. A null ratings means that symbol has no analyst coverage — either it could not be resolved to a tradable instrument, or it has too few contributing analysts to report — surface it as "no analyst coverage for X" rather than as an error. Price targets can be absent even when the ratings counts are present (they are gated independently); present that as "price targets not available" rather than implying zero coverage.

symbols.description: One or more stock symbols (max 10 per call). Exact-ticker match — no name or partial-ticker resolution. Lowercase and whitespace-padded input is normalized to uppercase-trimmed before forwarding.

One of 'regular' (regular trading hours), 'trading' (regular + post-market), 'extended' (pre-market + regular + post-market), '24_5' (24-hour, 5-day-trading-week). Does not affect valuation fields. overnight_volume only populates when bounds=24_5. Defaults to 'regular' when omitted.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol.

overnight_volume.description: Overnight session share volume. Null unless bounds=24_5 was requested; treat null as 'not applicable to this session', not 'no overnight trades'.

bounds.description: Session-bounds tag the data was computed over (e.g. '24_5' = 24-hour, 5-day-trading-week).

market_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD trading date the snapshot is 'as of'.

average_volume.description: Trailing 52-week average daily share volume (the unqualified name reflects the upstream contract).

high_52_weeks.description: Highest price over the trailing 52 weeks.

high_52_weeks_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD date the trailing-52-week high was set.

low_52_weeks.description: Lowest price over the trailing 52 weeks.

low_52_weeks_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD date the trailing-52-week low was set.

float.description: Publicly tradable share count (excludes insider / restricted holdings).

market_cap.description: Market capitalization in USD. Null for delisted or zero-share-outstanding instruments.

pb_ratio.description: Price-to-book ratio. Null for instruments with non-positive book value or no book-value data.

pe_ratio.description: Price-to-earnings ratio (TTM). Can be negative when earnings are negative. Null for recent IPOs or non-equity instruments.

dividend_yield.description: Trailing 12-month dividend yield as a percentage (1.85 means 1.85%). Null for non-dividend-paying instruments.

dividend_per_share.description: Most recent declared dividend amount per share. Present only for dividend-paying instruments.

distribution_frequency.description: How often the dividend is paid (e.g. 'quarterly', 'monthly', 'annual'). Present only for dividend-paying instruments.

payable_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD date the next dividend will be paid. Null for non-dividend stocks.

ex_dividend_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD next ex-dividend date — buy before this date to receive the upcoming dividend. Null for non-dividend stocks.

record_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD date of record for the next dividend. Present only for dividend-paying instruments.

thirty_day_sec_yield.description: 30-day SEC yield as a percentage (1.85 means 1.85%). Present primarily for bond funds; absent for individual stocks.

description.description: Short company description in the caller's preferred language.

financial_status_indicator.description: Short code from the listing exchange flagging listing-deficiency status (e.g. 'CC0' = no deficiency, 'D' = deficient, 'E' = delinquent). Pair with financial_status_description for the human-readable form.

financial_status_description.description: Human-readable form of financial_status_indicator. Empty when the indicator is the 'no deficiency' value.

results.description: One entry per resolved symbol, in upstream order. Empty if no symbol resolved. Symbols that did not resolve (delisted, invalid, non-equity) are NOT placeholder-null'd here — they appear in not_found instead so the whole call doesn't fail.

not_found.description: Requested symbols that the upstream could not resolve (delisted, invalid, non-equity). Returned in canonical uppercase form. Absent / null when every requested symbol resolved.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Symbols that did not resolve (delisted, invalid, non-equity) appear in not_found instead of results; surface them to the user as "no data for X" rather than ignoring them. Present nulls as "not applicable" rather than zero. Pair financial_status_indicator with financial_status_description — never surface the indicator code alone.

name: get_equity_historicals
description:
Get OHLCV bars for one or more equity symbols across an explicit time range. Use this for charting, "recent activity" questions, and backtesting. The server auto-selects an interval when one is not provided. If the bar's interpolated field is true, bar was synthesized to fill a gap and carry no new information.

Parameter rules:
- interval is optional; when omitted, the server auto-selects an interval that targets ~2,500 bars across the requested range. Provide an explicit interval only when you need a specific granularity.
- interval values are fixed; the server does NOT aggregate intermediate bars. For a custom interval (e.g. 3-minute), request the next-finer fixed interval and aggregate client-side.
- bounds defaults to 'regular' (RTH only). Use 'extended' or '24_5' only when the user explicitly asks about extended-hours activity.
- adjustment_type defaults to 'split' (split-adjusted, the right default for backtesting). Use 'none' for raw prices, 'all' for split + dividend adjustment.
- If the range would produce more bars than the upstream allows at the explicitly requested interval, narrow the range or coarsen the interval — the call is rejected before reaching upstream. The cap does not apply when interval is auto-selected.

symbols.description: One or more stock symbols (uppercase). Up to 10 per call.

start_time.description: Start of the range (RFC3339 UTC, e.g. '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'). Required.

end_time.description: End of the range (RFC3339 UTC). Optional — when omitted, defaults to the current time.

interval.description: Bar interval. Optional — when omitted, the server picks an interval that targets ~2,500 bars across the requested range. Intraday: 15second, 30second, minute, 5minute, 10minute, 30minute, hour, 4hour. Interday: day, week, month, 3month, 6month, year, 5year, 10year, 20year, 50year. Note: the 1-minute bar is named 'minute' (not '1minute').

adjustment_type.description: Corporate-action adjustment: 'none' (raw prices), 'split' (default; right for backtesting), or 'all' (split + dividend; intraday only).

symbol.description: Ticker symbol.

interval.description: Bar interval. Echoes the request when one was supplied; otherwise reports the server-auto-selected interval.

bounds.description: Session bounds echoed from the request.

begins_at.description: Start of the bar (RFC3339 UTC). Bars are left-edge labeled.

open_price.description: First trade price in the bar.

close_price.description: Last trade price in the bar. NOT the official settled close; for that use get_equity_quotes closes[].

high_price.description: Highest trade price in the bar.

low_price.description: Lowest trade price in the bar.

volume.description: Share volume in the bar. Zero for interpolated bars.

session.description: Wire-format session: 'reg' (regular hours), 'pre' (pre-market), or 'post' (after-hours). Empty/absent when the bar's session is unknown.

interpolated.description: True when the bar was synthesized to fill a gap (no trades occurred). OHLC values are forward-filled from a nearby bar; volume is zero.

bars.description: Bars in ascending time order. Empty if no trading activity in the window.

results.description: One entry per requested symbol that resolved upstream.

not_found.description: Requested symbols that did not resolve (delisted, invalid, or non-equity). Absent when every requested symbol resolved.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Bars are left-edge labeled in UTC; convert to the user's timezone for presentation. Treat interpolated=true bars as gap-fill — they carry no new info and should usually be hidden in charts and ignored for analytics. close_price on the most recent bar is NOT the official settled close — use get_equity_quotes for that. For a multi-bar move, compute return from the first bar's open_price to the last bar's close_price; do not aggregate intermediate interpolated bars. When bounds='regular' the bar series covers only regular trading hours — gaps between trading sessions are not zero-filled, they are simply absent. When the request omitted interval, the 'interval' field on each result reports what the server auto-selected.

name: get_equity_news

name: get_equity_orders
description:
Fetch equity orders for an account — list mode (newest first; open and closed, including fills, cancellations, rejections) or single-order mode by passing order_id. When the user asks broadly for "orders" or "my orders" without naming an asset class or order type, call get_equity_orders, get_option_orders, get_crypto_orders, and get_advanced_orders in parallel so OCO groups are not omitted.

Filtering tips:
- Prefer narrow queries: combine state, symbol, and/or created_at_gte for specific questions (e.g. "my filled AAPL orders this week") — the per-page cap is fixed.
- created_at_gte: interpret relative times in the user's timezone, convert to UTC before sending.
- symbol forces a symbol→instrument lookup; omit it if you don't need it.

symbol.description: Filter to one symbol (triggers a symbol→instrument lookup before the orders call).

symbol.description: Ticker symbol.

type.description: Upstream type: 'market' or 'limit'. Combine with trigger to recover the user-facing market/limit/stop_market/stop_limit.

quantity.description: Originally-requested share quantity. Null for dollar-based orders before the first fill.

cumulative_quantity.description: Shares filled so far. Less than quantity while partially filled; equal once filled.

price.description: Limit price for limit/stop_limit orders; null for market orders.

currency_code.description: ISO currency code; always 'USD' for equity orders today.

dollar_based_amount.description: Notional amount for dollar-based market orders; null for share-quantity orders.

time_in_force.description: 'gfd' (good for day) or 'gtc' (good till cancelled).

placed_agent.description: Source that placed the order: 'user' (app), 'agentic' (MCP), 'recurring', 'drip', 'brokeback' (system), or other internal values.

last_transaction_at.description: Time of the most recent fill, cancel, or reject. Null on a brand-new unfilled order.

price.description: Fill price per share.

quantity.description: Shares filled in this execution.

Mention placed_agent when it is not 'user'. Recover the user-facing order type from type+trigger or from price/stop_price. Present symbol, side, type, state, quantity (or dollar_based_amount), cumulative_quantity when partially filled, price for limit orders, average_price once filled, last_transaction_at (or created_at), and id when cancellation may follow; suppress other fields unless asked.

name: get_equity_positions

symbol.description: Ticker symbol.

quantity.description: Total shares held, including today's fills. Negative for short positions.

intraday_quantity.description: Portion of quantity filled today (upstream is timezone-aware).

average_buy_price.description: Average cost per share as shown in the Robinhood app; reflects partial sells. Omitted for positions still reconciling.

shares_available_for_sells.description: Shares the user can sell right now (server-computed after subtracting holds).

shares_held_for_sells.description: Shares locked by open outgoing sell orders.

shares_held_for_stock_grants.description: Shares held for settlement of stock grants / unsettled inbound fills.

shares_held_for_options_events.description: Shares earmarked for an upcoming options exercise/assignment.

shares_held_for_asset_transfer.description: Shares locked by an outgoing asset transfer (e.g. ACATS-out).

shares_pending_from_options_events.description: Shares pending from an options exercise/assignment, not yet booked into quantity.

type.description: 'long' (positive quantity), 'short' (negative), 'boxed' (both, rare), or 'empty' (zero).

positions.description: Open equity positions on this page. Empty when the cursor has no rows.

next.description: Next-page URL. Empty when there are no more pages.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Sellable shares: use shares_available_for_sells, not quantity. Yesterday's quantity = quantity - intraday_quantity. average_buy_price is the average cost per share shown in the Robinhood app (it already reflects partial sells) — use it as the user's average cost; it may be omitted for positions still reconciling. No market price here — for current value or PnL, call get_equity_quotes and multiply by quantity. Present symbol, quantity, average_buy_price, and type when not 'long'; suppress other fields unless asked.

name: get_equity_price_book
description: Get a real-time bid/ask order book (Level 2) snapshot for one or more equity symbols (max 4), showing the ladder of price levels and resting share size on each side. Use to read supply/demand depth before entering or exiting a position.

symbols.description: One or more stock symbols, max 4 per call.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol this book is for.

updated_at.description: Time the snapshot was taken.

price.description: Limit price at this level, as a decimal string.

quantity.description: Aggregate shares resting at this price level.

asks.description: Ask (sell-side) levels, ascending by price (best/lowest ask first). Empty when the book is unavailable.

price.description: Limit price at this level, as a decimal string.

quantity.description: Aggregate shares resting at this price level.

bids.description: Bid (buy-side) levels, descending by price (best/highest bid first). Empty when the book is unavailable.

books.description: One order-book snapshot per successfully fetched symbol, in request order. A symbol that failed appears in errors instead.

symbol.description: Requested symbol that could not be returned.

error.description: Why this symbol's book is unavailable: it did not resolve to an equity, the market is closed, or the snapshot request failed.

errors.description: Per-symbol failures. A symbol appears here or in books, never both. Empty when every requested symbol succeeded.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Each book in books is one symbol's snapshot: asks are sell-side levels (lowest/best ask first) and bids are buy-side levels (highest/best bid first), so the inside market is asks[0] vs bids[0]. quantity is the resting share size at a level — a level with outsized size relative to its neighbors is a wall (support on the bid side, resistance on the ask side). A requested symbol appears in books OR in errors, never both: surface anything in errors (a symbol that did not resolve to an equity, or whose book was unavailable because the market is closed) rather than implying its book was empty. An empty asks or bids array means no resting liquidity on that side right now, not an error.

name: get_equity_quotes

last_trade_price.description: Most recent regular-hours trade (9:30-16:00 ET). Stays frozen at the closing print after the close until the next open; not the official settled close.

last_non_reg_trade_price.description: Most recent pre-market / after-hours / overnight trade. Null during regular hours or when the symbol does not trade in the current session.

venue_last_non_reg_trade_time.description: Timestamp of last_non_reg_trade_price. Reveals which non-regular session the trade came from.

adjusted_previous_close.description: Prior-day close adjusted for splits, dividends, and mergers.

previous_close.description: Raw prior closing print — not corporate-action adjusted and not the official settled close.

previous_close_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD trading date that previous_close corresponds to. Null for symbols that have never had a settled close.

bid_price.description: Highest current buy-order price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

ask_price.description: Lowest current sell-order price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

has_traded.description: False for instruments that have never traded; price fields are meaningless when false.

state.description: Instrument listing state — 'active' is normal; other values (inactive, delisted, unlisted) mean the instrument is not in normal trading state.

quote.description: Live market data for this symbol.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD trading date for this close. May be earlier than the requested date when interpolated.

price.description: Official settled close price. Null when the upstream has no close (rare).

interpolated.description: True when the requested date had no session and the price came from an earlier date.

close.description: Official settled close from the most recent completed session. Absent when closes_error is set, or when this symbol had no close in an otherwise-successful closes batch.

results.description: One entry per symbol resolved from /quotes/, in upstream order, each carrying the live quote and (when available) the official prior-session close. Empty if no symbol resolved.

closes_error.description: Populated when the closes lookup is skipped or fails tool-wide (e.g. too many symbols, upstream timeout, no previous_close_date). Per-symbol gaps surface as a missing close on the affected result, not here.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Each entry in results pairs the live quote with the official prior-session close for the same symbol. Current price: pick whichever of quote.last_trade_price / quote.last_non_reg_trade_price has the more recent timestamp, then verify that timestamp is recent before calling it "current" — otherwise phrase as "as of <time>". Daily change uses quote.adjusted_previous_close. "Yesterday's close" uses results[].close.price (official settled close); when a result is missing close — either closes_error is set tool-wide, or this symbol had no close in an otherwise-successful batch — fall back to quote.previous_close and tell the user the official close lookup is unavailable. Drop bid/ask when zero. Surface has_traded=false or any non-'active' state before quoting a price.

name: get_equity_tax_lots
description: List the open tax lots for one equity holding in an account — each lot is a separate acquisition with its own quantity, cost basis, acquisition date, and long/short-term status.
