description: List options positions for an account. Returns open and closed (zero-quantity) positions. Pass nonzero=true for "what options do I have" / "show me my positions" — the common case.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Must come from the user or be clearly implied — never default from get_accounts.

nonzero.description: True to return only currently-open positions; omit/false to include closed ones.

type.description: 'long' or 'short'.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; for the next page, pass the cursor query param from the prior response's next URL.

option_id.description: Option instrument UUID. Pass to get_option_instruments to look up strike/expiration/type.

type.description: 'long' (bought) or 'short' (sold/written).

quantity.description: Net contracts held; zero means closed.

average_price.description: Signed cost basis per contract; negative on credit-received short positions.

intraday_average_open_price.description: Average open price across today's fills.

intraday_quantity.description: Contracts opened in the current session; resets daily.

opened_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the current open of this position began (resets on close+reopen). Prefer this over the underlying record's created_at when telling the user when they opened the position.

positions.description: Option positions on this page. Empty when the cursor has no rows.

next.description: Next-page URL. Empty when there are no more pages.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Surface chain_symbol, type, quantity, average_price, and expiration_date. Look up strike/option_type (call/put) via get_option_instruments with option_id when needed. Warn the user about any non-zero pending_* quantities. When next is non-null, extract the cursor query param and call this tool again.

name: get_option_quotes
description: Get real-time quotes for one or more option contracts by instrument UUID, plus the official prior-session close for each.

instrument_ids.description: Option instrument UUIDs. Above 20, quotes still return but closes is omitted with closes_error set.

instrument_id.description: UUID of the option contract; the canonical match key against closes[].instrument_id.

ask_price.description: Lowest current sell-side price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

bid_price.description: Highest current buy-side price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

break_even_price.description: Underlying price at which the position breaks even at expiration (strike +/- premium).

adjusted_mark_price.description: Mark adjusted for corporate actions on the underlying. Use against historical cost basis.

mark_price.description: Mid-market fair value — canonical current price for valuation.

high_fill_rate_buy_price.description: Upper bound of the likely fast-fill range for a buy.

low_fill_rate_buy_price.description: Lower bound of the likely fast-fill range for a buy.

high_fill_rate_sell_price.description: Upper bound of the likely fast-fill range for a sell.

low_fill_rate_sell_price.description: Lower bound of the likely fast-fill range for a sell.

previous_close_price.description: Quote-derived prior close — best-effort, not the official settled close.

previous_close_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD trading date that previous_close_price corresponds to.

delta.description: Sensitivity of option price to a $1 move in the underlying.

gamma.description: Rate of change of delta per $1 move in the underlying.

rho.description: Sensitivity to a 1% change in interest rates.

theta.description: Daily time decay ($/day); negative for long positions.

vega.description: Sensitivity to a 1% change in implied volatility.

open_interest.description: Outstanding contracts not yet closed or expired.

chance_of_profit_long.description: Model probability the long side ends in profit at expiration, decimal.

chance_of_profit_short.description: Model probability the short side ends in profit at expiration, decimal.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the quote refresh.

quote.description: Live market data for this option contract.

instrument_id.description: UUID of the option contract; the canonical match key against quotes[].instrument_id.

symbol.description: Underlying ticker. NOT unique — many contracts share a symbol.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD date this close corresponds to. May be earlier than the requested date when interpolated.

price.description: Official settled close price. Null when the upstream has no close (rare; usually illiquid expired contracts).

interpolated.description: True when the close came from a different date than requested (illiquid contract with no print on the requested day).

close.description: Official settled close from the most recent completed session. Absent when closes_error is set, or when this contract had no close in an otherwise-successful closes batch.

results.description: One entry per requested contract, in upstream quote order, each carrying the live quote and (when available) the official prior-session close. Empty if no instrument_id resolved.

closes_error.description: Populated when the closes lookup is skipped or fails tool-wide (e.g. too many contracts, upstream timeout, no previous_close_date). Per-contract gaps surface as a missing close on the affected result, not here.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Each entry in results pairs the live quote with the official prior-session close for the same option contract. Current price: use quote.mark_price (adjusted_mark_price when comparing against historical cost basis); verify quote.updated_at is recent before calling it 'current' — otherwise phrase as 'as of <updated_at>'. 1D P&L per contract: (quote.mark_price - close.price) × multiplier × position_quantity (multiplier is typically 100; use trade_value_multiplier from get_option_positions for adjusted contracts). Prefer results[].close.price (official settled close) over quote.previous_close_price; when a result is missing close — either closes_error is set tool-wide, or this contract had no close in an otherwise-successful batch — fall back to quote.previous_close_price and tell the user the official close lookup is unavailable. When close.interpolated is true, surface close.date — the price is not from the requested day. Drop bid/ask when zero.

name: get_option_watchlist
description: List the single-leg option contracts on the user's options watchlist. Use this instead of get_watchlist_items for the options watchlist — get_watchlist_items returns a generic shape that drops the option-specific title and the upstream rejects it with 400 anyway. Works for both equity options (AAPL, NVDA) and index options (SPX, NDX, RUT). Multi-leg strategies (verticals, condors, etc.) that may exist in the user's watchlist from app-side order placement are not shown — direct the user to the Robinhood app to view those.

id.description: Opaque UUID handle for this watchlist item. Same value upstream calls object_id.

name.description: Human-readable position title, e.g. "Long Call AAPL Jan 2026 $200". Surface to the user verbatim.

option_ids.description: Option contract UUIDs in this strategy. Always length 1 — only single-leg strategies are surfaced. Pass to get_option_quotes, review_option_order, place_option_order, or remove_option_from_watchlist.

expiration_date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the contract's expiration.

items.description: Items on the user's options watchlist. Empty when the watchlist exists but is empty.

list_id.description: The options watchlist this call resolved to.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Surface name to the user — it is the human-readable position title (e.g. "Long Call AAPL Jan 2026 $200"). option_ids[0] is the contract id to pass to get_option_quotes, review_option_order, place_option_order, or remove_option_from_watchlist. If the user mentions a multi-leg strategy (vertical, iron condor, etc.) they have in their watchlist and you don't see it here, tell them this tool only shows single-leg items and to check the app. "no options watchlist found" in the error means options trading is not enabled for this account.

name: get_pnl_trade_history
description: Get a customer's per-trade realized profit & loss — a chronological, paginated list of closed/realizing trades (equities, options, crypto, prediction markets) with symbol, side, quantity, price, and realized gain/loss. This is the same data behind the app's PnL hub ("Realized profit & loss"). Read-only. Trades only. Use get_realized_pnl for aggregate/bucketed totals.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number (the rhs_account_number from get_accounts). Obtain it from get_accounts.

span.description: Preset window: week (default), month, 3month, ytd, or all. Wormhole offers preset spans only (no arbitrary date range).

symbol.description: Optional single stock symbol filter (trimmed + uppercased). Omit for all symbols; one symbol per call.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor. Omit for the first page.

account_number.description: The account the trades are for (echoed).

span.description: The span window actually used (defaults to week).

timestamp.description: RFC3339 time the trade closed (the realizing event).

symbol.description: Instrument symbol traded.

quantity.description: Shares/contracts, decimal string.

price.description: Execution (close) price, decimal string.

realized_gain.description: Realized profit/loss on this closing trade, decimal string in the account currency.

trades.description: Closed/realizing trades in the window, most-recent-first. Empty when there were none.

next_cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page; empty when there are no more trades.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: trades are returned most-recent-first. Each entry is a closed/realizing trade with the realized gain/loss on it. price is the execution (close) price. The window is a preset span (not an arbitrary date range); default is the last week. Paginate with cursor: pass next_cursor from the previous response for the next page; an empty next_cursor means there are no more trades. An empty trades list means there were no realized trades in the window — a valid result, not an error. To filter more than one symbol, call once per symbol. Treat figures as informational, not a tax document or tax/performance advice.

name: get_politician_trades
description: Get disclosed trading activity of US politicians from Tip Ranks. Use when the user asks about politician/congressional trades - either for a specific stock ("which politicians traded NVDA?") or a specific politician. Data comes from public STOCK Act disclosures; amounts are ranges, not exact values, and disclosures lag the actual trade by up to 45 days.

politician_name.description: Full or partial name of a US politician, e.g. 'Nancy Pelosi'. Case-insensitive. Optional when equity_symbol is provided.

equity_symbol.description: One active US equity ticker, e.g. NVDA. Exact ticker only; lowercase and surrounding whitespace are normalized. Optional when politician_name is provided.

party.description: Political party, e.g. DEMOCRAT, REPUBLICAN, INDEPENDENT.

asset_type.description: EQUITY, CRYPTO, OPTION, or UNSPECIFIED. When UNSPECIFIED, the disclosure didn't identify the instrument clearly enough for symbol to be populated — that's expected, not an error.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol of the traded instrument.

min.description: Lower bound of the disclosed trade-size range, in USD.

max.description: Upper bound of the disclosed trade-size range, in USD.

amount_range.description: Disclosed trade-size range — never present as an exact figure.

disclosure_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD date the trade was made public. Can lag transaction_date by up to 45 days.

trades.description: Disclosed trades matching the request, most recent first. Empty when no disclosures match.

has_more.description: True when older disclosed trades exist beyond what's returned here; this tool does not page through the full history.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Each entry is one disclosed transaction. Always display the source (Tip Ranks) as attribution. transaction_date is when the trade occurred; disclosure_date is when it was made public - this lag can be up to 45 days, so treat entries as historical information, not a real-time signal, and do not imply the information is more recent than it is. Amounts are disclosed ranges - never present them as exact figures. Do not present politician trades as a recommendation or endorsement.

name: get_popular_watchlists
description: Discover Robinhood-curated lists the user can follow (e.g. '100 Most Popular', 'Daily Movers'). Use to find a list_id, then pass it to follow_watchlist.

display_name.description: Human-readable list name (e.g. '100 Most Popular', 'Daily Movers').

item_count.description: Number of items in the list.

is_badged.description: True for newly-published curated lists. Worth surfacing as 'new' when listing options for the user to follow.

lists.description: Robinhood-curated lists available for the user to follow.

next.description: Cursor URL for the next page when more results exist. Absent on the last page.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: For 'this list is new' surfacing, use is_badged. The response is paginated — if next is non-null there are more lists; call again with the cursor from next.

name: get_portfolio
description: Get the account's portfolio market value breakdown by asset type and buying power. Use for "how much is my account worth?", "what's my portfolio breakdown?", "how much do I have in options?", and "how much can I spend / afford?" questions.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Obtain from get_accounts.

total_value.description: Total portfolio value across all asset types. The default 'account value' to show the user.

equity_value.description: Value of stock and ETF positions.

futures_value.description: Value of futures positions (includes RHD cost basis).

cash.description: Available cash (includes early access from pending deposits).

pending_deposits.description: Deposits in transit, not yet settled.

currency.description: Currency all values are denominated in (e.g. USD).

buying_power.description: Authoritative spendable figure used to gate order placement. For margin-enabled accounts it already includes available margin leverage; for cash and leverage-disabled accounts it equals the cash-only figure.

unleveraged_buying_power.description: Buying power ignoring margin leverage. Typically <= buying_power. Negative when the account is in deficit — new positions cannot be opened until the deficit is cleared.

intraday_buying_power.description: Buying power for intraday leverage, when applicable; null when the account does not have intraday margin enabled.

off_intraday_buying_power.description: Buying power outside the intraday-leverage window; null when not applicable.

buying_power.description: Real-time buying power from the broker.
Authoritative spendable figure for crypto buys (cash-only; excludes equity margin leverage).

crypto_buying_power.description: Spendable buying power for crypto buys. Cash-only (crypto is not marginable), so it excludes the equity margin leverage that buying_power may include — quote this for 'how much can I spend on crypto'. Omitted when unavailable or when the caller is not in the crypto experiment.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Show total_value as "account value" or "portfolio value". The breakdown fields show how value is distributed across asset types. Zero-value fields mean the user has no holdings in that asset class — omit them from display unless the user explicitly asks. For "how much cash do I have?" use the cash field. buying_power is the real-time authoritative spendable figure from the broker; quote buying_power.buying_power as the primary affordability answer with buying_power.display_currency. For "how much can I spend on crypto?" quote crypto_buying_power.buying_power instead — crypto is cash-only (not marginable), so the top-level buying_power may overstate it; crypto_buying_power is omitted when unavailable. crypto_value reflects the user's crypto holdings value. On a cash account, recently sold proceeds that have not yet settled are not spendable and are not included in buying_power; that unsettled amount is reported as unsettled_funds by get_accounts (not here), so if you do not already have the account's unsettled_funds, call get_accounts to check it. Whenever you report buying power or account value for a type='cash' account whose unsettled_funds is greater than 0, and the user wants to access unsettled funds or other features available in a limited margin account — if the get_limited_margin_upgrade_info tool is available — call it with the account_number and share the appropriate upgrade link. If that tool is not available, say nothing about limited margin (there is no fallback).

name: get_realized_pnl
description: Get a customer's realized profit & loss for an account over a time window — per-bucket realized gain ($ and %) and the number of closing trades, plus window totals. Read-only. Aggregate, bucketed numbers only (not individual trades). Use for post-trade analysis like "how did my last 90 days of trades do?".

account_number.description: Brokerage account number (the rhs_account_number from get_accounts). Obtain it from get_accounts.

span.description: Preset window: day, week, month, 3month, year, or all. Defaults to 3month ('last 90 days'). Mutually exclusive with start_date/end_date.

start_date.description: Custom window start, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive — interpreted at midnight in timezone (default US Eastern). Use with end_date instead of span; must be on or before end_date and not in the future.

end_date.description: Custom window end, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive — the entire end_date is covered (through 23:59:59 in timezone). Use with start_date instead of span; an end_date beyond today returns data through the present.

asset_classes.description: Filter to one or more of equity, option, crypto. Omit for all asset classes available on the account.

display_currency.description: Currency for returned amounts. Currently USD only; defaults to USD.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for bucket day-boundaries (e.g. America/New_York). Defaults to the account timezone (US Eastern).

account_number.description: The account the realized profit and loss is for (echoed).

window.description: The window actually used — the span name, or 'start_date..end_date' for a custom range.

display_currency.description: Currency the amounts are denominated in.

start_time.description: RFC3339 start of the bucket window (inclusive).

end_time.description: RFC3339 end of the bucket window.

realized_gain.description: Realized profit/loss in the bucket, decimal string in display_currency. Null when the bucket's realized profit and loss is not meaningful (e.g. all lots are transfers with no cost basis) — present it as 'n/a', not 0.

rate_of_realized_gain.description: Bucket realized return as a percentage, decimal string (e.g. '10' = 10%). Null for transfer-only buckets with no cost basis — the same condition that nulls realized_gain; present as 'n/a', not 0.

number_of_trades.description: Count of closing/realizing trades in the bucket.

data_points.description: Realized-profit-and-loss buckets in ascending time order. Empty when there were no closing trades in the window.

total_returns.description: Total realized profit and loss across the window, decimal string in display_currency. '0' when the window had no closing trades.

total_rate_of_return.description: Total realized return across the window as a percentage, decimal string.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: This is realized profit & loss only — gains/losses from positions closed within the window; it excludes unrealized profit and loss on open positions. data_points are buckets in ascending time order. A window with no closing trades returns empty data_points with zero totals — that is a valid result ("no realized trades in this window"), not an error. When a bucket's realized_gain and rate_of_realized_gain are null (a transfer-only bucket whose lots had no cost basis, e.g. transfers), present them as "n/a" — do not render them as $0 / 0%. These are aggregate numbers; for individual trade records use the separate realized profit and loss (trade history) tool. Treat figures as informational, not a tax document or tax/performance advice.

name: get_scanner_datapoints
description:
List the market-data datapoints available for building raw expressions: functions (with signatures) and fields, each with a category and description. Expressions serve two purposes — filters (screen on the expression's value) and columns (display it in results) — on preview_scan, create_scan and update_scan_config. Call this before constructing one; do not guess datapoint names or signatures.

For filters, use expressions only for screens no enum filter covers: check get_scanner_filter_specs first, and prefer an enum filter_type whenever one fits. For columns, a standard column referenced by display_name alone needs no expression at all.

Scoping a scan to a set of instruments is done here, not with an enum filter: the descriptive category's symbol field restricts a scan to named tickers or to an index's members. See the guide for the exact predicates.

Requires a category, since the full catalog is too large to return at once. Pass "technical", "price_volume", "fundamental", "options", "volatility", "quote" or "descriptive"; the response lists every category with a description so you can pick a different one if needed.

category.description: Which part of the catalog to return. One of: technical (chart studies - rsi, macd, adx, bollinger, pivots), price_volume (prices, changes, moving averages, volume), fundamental (marketCap, peRatio, eps, dividends, sector, earnings dates), options (options volume and open interest on the underlying), volatility (implied and realized volatility, IV rank), quote (bid/ask, sizes, spread), descriptive (symbol, type, listing, date arithmetic). Also accepts "function" or "field" to slice by kind instead, or any category name from a previous response. Required - the full catalog is too large to return at once.

name.description: Identifier to use inside an expression, e.g. "rsi", "fundamental.marketCap". Case-sensitive.

kind.description: "function" takes arguments and must be called with parentheses; "field" is referenced bare.

signature.description: The callable form to copy, e.g. rsi(candleCount: number, candlePeriod: CandlePeriod, session: Session = "all"): number. An argument type in UpperCamelCase (CandlePeriod, TimePeriod, Session) has a fixed set of legal values listed in argument_types; a value not in that set is rejected by the market-data provider. A trailing = shows the default, which may be omitted from the call.

value_type.description: Type the datapoint evaluates to: "number" or "string". Compare a number datapoint against numeric values only.

examples.description: Worked expressions using this datapoint, safe to copy and adapt. Present on a minority of datapoints.

datapoints.description: The datapoints in the requested category. Empty when the category matched nothing — read categories and call again.

name.description: Category name as it appears on a datapoint.

description.description: What this category covers, naming representative datapoints in it.

datapoint_count.description: How many datapoints this category holds — an indication of how large the response will be.

aliases.description: Values accepted for the category parameter to select this category.

categories.description: Every category in the catalog, always returned in full so a wrong category can be corrected without another failed call.

name.description: Type name as it appears in a signature, e.g. "CandlePeriod".

argument_names.description: Argument names that take this type, e.g. ["candlePeriod"].

values.description: The only legal values. Pass one of these verbatim (quoted inside the expression); anything else is rejected upstream.

note.description: Guidance for arguments that are easy to confuse — read this before choosing a value.

argument_types.description: Legal values for the named argument types that appear in signatures. A signature says candlePeriod: CandlePeriod; this says what CandlePeriod may be.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description:
Build an expression by copying a signature and filling its arguments: rsi(candleCount: number, candlePeriod: CandlePeriod, session: Session = "all") becomes rsi(candleCount=14, candlePeriod="1d", session="all"). Arguments are passed by name, string values are quoted, and an argument shown with a default may be omitted.

An argument type in UpperCamelCase has a fixed value set in argument_types — using a value outside it fails upstream, so check there rather than inferring. Read the note on CandlePeriod and TimePeriod before choosing: candlePeriod is the size of each candle, timePeriod is how far back to look, and confusing them silently changes what the screen measures.

Some screens are composed rather than looked up: comparing two datapoints puts the whole comparison in the expression with predicate "=" and values ["True"] — "put volume exceeds call volume" is optionsPutDayVolume > optionsCallDayVolume, "price above its average" is tradeAllDay.price > closeAvg(...). Prefer that boolean form over dividing (optionsPutDayVolume / optionsCallDayVolume > 1): a division silently drops every instrument whose denominator is zero, which here are the most put-skewed names — the ones the screen exists to find. Composition is also the fallback when an enum filter covers the screen but not your variant — e.g. relative volume has an enum filter (FILTER_TYPE_RELATIVE_VOLUME), so only compose dayVolume / volumeAvg(...) for a lookback missing from its supported_lengths.

Scoping the universe to specific instruments uses the symbol field with a LIST predicate rather than a comparison, and the expression is the bare word symbol:
- named tickers — predicate ANY_OF, values the tickers ("only AAPL and MSFT" is expression symbol, predicate ANY_OF, values ["AAPL", "MSFT"]).
- members of an index — predicate IN_LIST, values index CODES, not tickers ("S&P 500 stocks" is expression symbol, predicate IN_LIST, values ["SP500"]). Several codes union: ["SP500", "NDX"] means in either index.
The two predicates are not interchangeable, and mixing them up fails in opposite ways: IN_LIST with a ticker is rejected upstream ("list name 'AAPL' does not exist"), while ANY_OF with an index code returns zero rows and no error at all. Valid index codes: SP100, SP400, SP500, SP500_SecIndicies, SP500_SecIndustrIndicies, SP600, DJI, NDX, NDXT25, Russell1000, Russell2000, Russell3000, RussellMidcap, RussellMicrocap, HGX, HXC, OSX, RUF, SOX, UTY, XAU, S5C. There is no code for the Nasdaq Composite: "COMP" resolves upstream but collides with the Compound (COMP) crypto symbol, so avoid it. A user's own watchlist or positions cannot be used as a scope.

The same expressions work as result COLUMNS (the columns parameter of preview_scan, create_scan and update_scan_config): a column displays the expression's value without screening on it. A boolean-comparison filter reads best with its operands as columns (e.g. the put-exceeds-call screen showing both volumes); the division that is wrong as a filter is fine as a column, where a zero denominator only blanks a cell instead of dropping the row.

Always validate an expression with preview_scan before saving it to a scan.

name: get_scanner_filter_specs
description:
List every valid scanner filter type and how to use it. Call this before constructing filters for create_scan or update_scan_filters — do not guess filter_type names.

This tool takes no parameters.

filter_type.description: Wire-format enum name, e.g. "FILTER_TYPE_RSI". Pass this in filter payloads.

display_name.description: Human-readable name as shown in Legend, e.g. "RSI".

filter_group.description: Category bucket: POPULAR, TECHNICAL, FUNDAMENTAL, OPTION, or PRICE_VOLUME.

value_type.description: Expected value format: DECIMAL, INTEGER, DATETIME, or STRING.

unit_type.description: Value unit: DOLLAR, PERCENTAGE, or PLAIN. PERCENTAGE filters take DECIMAL values: 0.05 means 5%, so send 0.05 and never 5 (which reads as 500% and silently matches nothing). Same convention as the Legend UI, which converts percent input to decimals before sending.

supported_predicates.description: Symbolic predicates valid for this filter (e.g. ">", "<", "BETWEEN").

supported_lengths.description: Lookback lengths the filter accepts (e.g. [9, 14, 21, 50] for RSI). Empty when the filter has no length input.

supported_intervals.description: Time granularities the filter accepts (e.g. ["1m", "5m", "1h", "1d"]). Empty when the filter has no interval input.

supported_plots.description: Plot / price-field values the filter accepts (e.g. ["open", "close"] for % Change). Empty when the filter has no plot input.

options.description: The complete set of values this filter accepts, for filters that take a value from a fixed vocabulary rather than a threshold (asset type, sector). Send one of these verbatim in the filter's values: they are case-sensitive, and a value outside the set is rejected. Empty for threshold filters, whose values are numbers.

filter_specs.description: Every valid scanner filter type: wire-format enum name, category, value format, supported predicates/intervals/lengths/plots, and the enumerated options a vocabulary filter accepts.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description:
Match filter_type exactly, including suffixes (e.g. percent-change filters use FILTER_TYPE_PERCENT_CHANGE_FROM_CLOSE, not FILTER_TYPE_PERCENT_CHANGE). If a filter's supported_intervals is non-empty, pass an interval — omitting it is the leading cause of an otherwise-valid filter returning no results. Use supported_predicates symbols exactly (e.g. ">", "BETWEEN").

No enum filter scopes a scan to particular instruments: to restrict it to named tickers or to an index's members, use an expression filter on the symbol field (get_scanner_datapoints, descriptive category) rather than concluding it cannot be done.

If a filter has options, its values must come from that list verbatim — it is the filter's complete vocabulary, and anything else is rejected. Do not infer these values from scan results: the instrument_type field in results is Robinhood's classification, which is coarser than the asset-type filter's (its EQUITY spans both STOCK and ETF), so a value copied from there screens for nothing.

Filters with unit_type PERCENTAGE take DECIMAL values: 0.05 means 5%. A whole-percent number silently matches nothing — "implied volatility above 80" is values ["0.8"], because ["80"] reads as 8000% and returns zero rows with no error. This applies to every PERCENTAGE filter (implied and historical volatility, IV rank, the margins, return on assets/equity, % change, gap).

name: get_scans
description:
List the authenticated user's saved scanners (also called screeners). A scan is a saved set of filters and columns that filters the market for instruments matching specific criteria (e.g. "RSI > 70 and Volume > 1M"). The user creates these in Legend or via the create_scan tool.

Returns one entry per scan with its id, title, active filters, configured columns, sort order, and a flag indicating whether the scan is managed by Cortex (Legend's AI agent). Cortex-managed scans are read-only via MCP — they can be run with run_scan but not modified with update_scan_filters or update_scan_config.

This tool takes no parameters.

scan_id.description: Unique scan identifier. Pass this to run_scan, update_scan_filters, or update_scan_config.

title.description: Human-readable name the user gave the scan.

filter_type.description: Display label of the column this filter screens on, as shown in Legend (e.g. "RSI", "Market cap"). This is a user-editable label, so it is for describing the filter to the user — do NOT send it back as filter_type when re-applying filters; use filter_type_enum for that.

filter_type_enum.description: Wire-format enum name for this filter (e.g. "FILTER_TYPE_RSI") — the value to pass as a filter's filter_type when re-sending this filter to create_scan or update_scan_filters. FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM is the exception: such a filter is defined by its expression, so re-create it by sending the expression field to create_scan and omitting filter_type. Never send FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM as a filter_type — it would create an empty filter. Empty only when the filter has no recognized type.

values.description: Threshold values for the predicate. Single-element for >/</=, two-element for BETWEEN, multi-element for IN_LIST/ANY_OF.

interval.description: Time granularity for time-series filters (e.g. "1d", "1h"). Empty for snapshot filters.

length.description: Lookback length for filters that need one (e.g. RSI period of 14). Zero/omitted for filters that don't take a length.

plot.description: Plot / price-field input for filters that have one (e.g. % Change uses "open" or "close" to choose changeFromOpen vs changeFromClose). Empty for filters that don't take a plot.

expression.description: Upstream market-data expression this filter screens on. Populated for every filter, standard or custom — an enum filter type is a preset that compiles to an expression upstream. Useful for explaining precisely what the filter measures (which interval, lookback and session it uses). When re-applying a standard filter, send filter_type_enum rather than this; for a FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM filter this expression is exactly what to send, as the expression field of a create_scan filter.

filter_summary.description: Active filters applied to this scan, one entry per filter. Empty when the scan uses only preset defaults.

column_count.description: Number of visible columns configured on this scan. Equals the number of columns entries with visible true.

display_name.description: Column header as shown in Legend, e.g. "% Change". This is the value other scanner tools take when they reference a column.

visible.description: False for a column configured on the scan but hidden from the results table. Hidden columns still appear here but their values are absent from scan results.

order.description: Zero-based position of this column in the results table.

expression.description: Upstream market-data expression this column computes, e.g. dayVolume or fundamental.marketCap. Populated for every column, standard or custom — a named column is a preset that compiles to an expression upstream. Read-only explanatory detail: reference a column by display_name, never by this.

columns.description: Every column configured on this scan, visible or not, in configuration order. Use the display_name values here as the sorting_column argument to update_scan_config — that argument matches on display name and is case-sensitive.

sorting.description: Current sort column + direction in human form (e.g. "Volume desc"). Empty when no sort is configured.

cortex_managed.description: True when this scan was created or modified by Cortex (Legend's AI agent). Cortex-managed scans can be read but not modified via MCP tools.

scans.description: List of the user's saved scans, newest first. Empty when the user has no saved scans.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description:
How to interpret the response:
- scans is an array, newest first. Empty when the user has no saved scans — offer to create one with create_scan if they ask.
- filter_summary on each scan describes the active filters. Use filter_type (e.g. "RSI"), predicate, values and optional interval/length to tell the user what the scan does. To re-send a filter to update_scan_filters or create_scan, copy filter_type_enum — not filter_type, which is a user-editable column label and will be rejected.
- A filter whose filter_type_enum is FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM is defined by its expression. update_scan_filters cannot carry it over; to change a scan that has one, use create_scan with that scan's scan_id and the full intended filter set, passing the filter's expression in the expression field (the scan gets a new configuration version; earlier versions are preserved).
- cortex_managed: true means the scan was created or modified by Cortex inside Legend. Tell the user it's read-only via MCP if they ask to modify it. Suggest creating a fresh scan via create_scan as the alternative.
- columns lists every configured column, hidden ones included; column_count counts only the visible ones. When the user asks to re-sort a scan, take update_scan_config's sorting_column verbatim from a columns[].display_name — never guess it.
- Columns are writable: to add, remove or reorder a scan's extra columns (the ones beyond its filters' own and the standard defaults), call update_scan_config with the complete intended columns list — it keeps the scan's filters, expression filters included, without re-sending them. Each entry here carries the display_name and expression to copy from.
- sorting describes the scan's current sort (e.g. "Volume desc"). Mention it when summarizing how results would be ordered.
- Use scan_id (not title) when calling run_scan, update_scan_filters, or update_scan_config.

When presenting scans to the user:
- Render as a numbered list with the title prominent and a short summary of filters.
- Mark Cortex-managed scans clearly so the user knows they're read-only here.
- If the user wants to see results, ask which scan and call run_scan with that scan_id.

name: get_sec_filing
description: Read an SEC filing's table of contents or a specific section's text. Use get_sec_filing_index to find a filing_id first.

section.description: Section identifier from the table of contents (the id field). Omit to get the full table of contents; provide to get a specific section's text.

filing_id.description: Filing identifier, echoed from the request.

form_type.description: SEC form type of this filing, e.g. '10-K'.

id.description: Slugified section identifier. Pass as the section param to get_sec_filing to retrieve this section's text.

title.description: Section heading text as it appears in the filing.

level.description: Heading depth: 1 = top-level part, 2 = item, 3 = sub-item.

sections.description: All sections in the filing, in document order. Pick a section id and call get_sec_filing again with that id to read the text.

table_of_contents.description: Table of contents for the filing. Populated when no section is requested. Pick a section id from sections and call get_sec_filing with it to read the text.

filing_id.description: Filing identifier, echoed from the request.

form_type.description: SEC form type of this filing, e.g. '10-K'.

section_id.description: Section identifier, echoed from the request.

content.description: Full markdown text of the section. May be several thousand tokens for narrative sections like MD&A.

section.description: The requested section's text and metadata. Populated only when a section id was provided.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: When section is omitted, table_of_contents is populated and section is absent — pick a section id and call get_sec_filing again with that id. When section is provided, section is populated and table_of_contents is absent. Section content can be several thousand tokens for narrative sections (e.g. MD&A); prefer fetching one section at a time. If the filing has not yet been processed or the section id did not match, an error will be returned.

name: get_sec_filing_facts
description: Get reported facts tagged under specific GAAP concept names in one or more SEC filings — financial figures (revenue, net income, assets, debt) and disclosures (e.g. debt schedules, related-party transactions, subsequent events) alike. Use get_sec_filing_index to find filing_ids first.

filing_ids.description: Filing identifiers to fetch facts for (1-3), from get_sec_filing_index. Default to a single filing_id — most questions are answered by periods already embedded in one filing (10-Ks carry ~3 fiscal years, 10-Qs carry current + prior-year). Pass more than one only when the question needs data a single filing structurally can't have, e.g. a trend longer than 3 years, or confirming a disclosed subsequent event landed in the next filing.

concepts.description: GAAP concept names to fetch (1-10) — covers numeric line items (e.g. NetIncomeLoss, Assets, Revenues) and disclosure text blocks (e.g. ScheduleOfDebtTableTextBlock) alike. Guess common names directly; only call get_sec_filing_facts_catalog first if a guess comes back with no matching facts.

filing_id.description: Filing identifier this fact was reported in, from get_sec_filing_index.

concept.description: GAAP taxonomy concept name, e.g. NetIncomeLoss, Assets. Echoed from the request.

entity.description: Filer identifier (CIK) this fact was reported under.

period.description: Reporting period as reported: either a single date (instant, e.g. balance-sheet items) or a start/end date range (duration, e.g. income-statement items).

axises.description: Dimension breakdown for this fact, e.g. ['ProductOrServiceAxis: HardwareMember']. Empty means this is the undifferentiated total for the concept and period — prefer it as 'the total' when both a totals row and axis-sliced rows exist.

decimals.description: Reported precision as a power of 10, e.g. -6 means rounded to the nearest million. Absent for text-valued facts. The same concept can appear at different precisions across facts in one filing (e.g. -6 vs -7) — don't assume uniform precision when doing raw arithmetic across multiple rows.

value.description: Numeric value as reported, a decimal string. Absent when this fact is text-valued — see char_value instead.

char_value.description: Text value as reported (e.g. footnote/disclosure text-block content). Empty when this fact is numeric-valued — see value instead. A populated value can still be just a section heading rather than a narrative; don't assume any non-empty text is informative. Substantial disclosures (e.g. debt schedules) can run to several thousand tokens — fetch text-block concepts deliberately, not as part of a broad speculative batch.

unit.description: Unit of the numeric value, e.g. USD, shares. Absent for text-valued facts.

start_date.description: Start of the reporting period. Absent for instant (point-in-time) facts, e.g. balance-sheet items.

end_date.description: End of the reporting period, or the instant date for point-in-time facts.

facts.description: Matching fact rows, one per filing/concept/period/axis combination found. Empty when none of the requested concepts exist for the requested filings.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Fetch known synonym/near-duplicate concept pairs together and cross-check for divergence — they can legitimately disagree (e.g. NetIncomeLoss with ProfitLoss, Revenues with RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax). Not every similarly-named pair is the same failure mode: some are inconsistent tagging of the same thing (reconcile to one number, or flag the divergence if it's large); others are deliberately different scopes (e.g. DebtCurrent/LongTermDebt exclude finance leases, while LongTermDebtAndFinanceLeasesCurrent/LongTermDebtAndFinanceLeasesNoncurrent include them and will consistently run a few percent higher) — present those separately with what each includes rather than collapsing them into one number. A requested concept with no matching rows in the response simply does not exist for that filing — diff the concepts you requested against the concepts actually present before answering, and call get_sec_filing_facts_catalog if a load-bearing concept came back missing rather than answering off a partial set. Report a concept as not available rather than force-fitting a value that doesn't semantically match the question.

name: get_sec_filing_facts_catalog
description: List the distinct GAAP concept names tagged in an SEC filing, with their reporting periods and dimension breakdowns. Use this only after a direct get_sec_filing_facts guess comes back empty, or for open-ended "what's unusual/notable" questions — most common financial questions should guess concept names directly rather than calling this first.

filing_id.description: Filing identifier to catalog, from get_sec_filing_index.

concept_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on concept name, e.g. 'Debt'. Omit to return all concepts.

axis_name_in.description: Only return concepts broken down by at least one of these dimension names. For 'what's unusual/notable in this filing' questions, try named-entity axes like SubsequentEventTypeAxis, BusinessAcquisitionAxis, RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis, LegalEntityAxis, or MajorCustomersAxis before falling back to an unfiltered call. Omit to skip this filter.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Omit for the first page; to fetch the next page, pass the value from the prior response's next_offset field.

concept.description: GAAP taxonomy concept name available for this filing. Pass to get_sec_filing_facts's concepts param to fetch its values.

is_text_block.description: True when this concept holds narrative/disclosure text rather than a number — expect char_value, not value, on the fetched fact.

period.description: Reporting period as reported: either a single date (instant) or a start/end date range (duration), matching the period field on get_sec_filing_facts rows.

start_date.description: Start of the period. Absent for instant (point-in-time) periods.

end_date.description: End of the period, or the instant date for point-in-time periods.

periods.description: Distinct reporting periods this concept was tagged for in this filing.

axis_names.description: Dimension names this concept is broken down by in this filing, e.g. ['ProductOrServiceAxis']. Empty means only an undifferentiated total exists for this concept.

concepts.description: Distinct concepts tagged in this filing, matching any filters applied.

count.description: Total number of concepts matching the request, across all pages.

next_offset.description: Present only when more concepts remain. Pass as the offset param on the next call to page through the rest.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: If a filtered call (concept_contains or axis_name_in) returns nothing relevant, retry once without filters before giving up. If the unfiltered catalog still has nothing relevant, say clearly that it isn't available in this filing rather than guessing further. When a question spans multiple filings, call this tool once per filing_id — GAAP tagging can differ year to year, so one filing's catalog shouldn't be assumed to apply to another. Page size is set upstream and not fixed — always pass next_offset back exactly as returned rather than guessing an increment, and stop once a response has no next_offset.

name: get_sec_filing_index
description: List a company's SEC filings, optionally filtered by form type and date. Use this to find a specific annual report (10-K), quarterly report (10-Q), or material event disclosure (8-K).

symbol.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL. Exact match — no partial or name-based lookup. Lowercase input is normalized to uppercase.

form_type.description: One or more SEC form types to filter by, e.g. ['10-K'] or ['10-K','10-Q']. Omit to return all form types.

since.description: Earliest filing date to include, ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. Omit to return filings from all dates.

until.description: Latest filing date to include, ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. Omit to return filings up to the most recent.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor. Omit for the first page; to fetch the next page, pass the value from the prior response's next field.

symbol.description: The requested ticker, in canonical uppercase form.

filing_id.description: Unique identifier for this filing. Pass to get_sec_filing to read its content.

form_type.description: SEC form type, e.g. '10-K' (annual report), '10-Q' (quarterly report), '8-K' (current report / material event).

description.description: Human-readable label for the form type, e.g. 'Annual Report'.

date_filed.description: Date the filing was submitted to the SEC, YYYY-MM-DD.

filings.description: Filings matching the request, most-recent-first. Empty when no filings match the filters.

next.description: Pagination cursor for the next page. Empty when there are no more results.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: If next is non-empty, more filings are available — call this tool again with the cursor value from next to fetch the next page. Results are most-recent-first. When the question doesn't need more than the most recent filing's own embedded history (most questions), use the first result rather than filtering further. When the question needs data spanning further back than one filing embeds — a multi-year trend beyond ~3 years, a specific past quarter, confirming a disclosed subsequent event's follow-through in the next filing — widen since/until and select up to 3 of the returned filings covering the needed span, then pass all of their filing_ids to get_sec_filing_facts. If a query with specific filters (form_type, since/until) returns no filings, retry once with the filters loosened (drop form_type, or widen/drop the date range) before giving up; if it's still empty, say clearly that no matching filing was found rather than guessing from an unrelated one.

name: get_watchlist_items
description: List the items in a watchlist. Items may be stocks/ETFs, crypto pairs, futures, indexes — distinguished by object_type. For the options watchlist, use get_option_watchlist instead — this tool returns a generic shape that drops the strategy-specific fields and the upstream rejects it with 400 anyway. Does not return live prices; call get_quotes with the symbol(s) for that.

list_id.description: UUID of the watchlist whose items to fetch. Obtain from get_watchlists or get_popular_watchlists.

object_id.description: UUID of the underlying instrument / currency pair / futures contract / index. Pass to remove_from_watchlist (via symbol — the tool resolves it back to this id internally) to remove this item.

object_type.description: What kind of asset this item references: 'instrument' (US stock/ETF), 'currency_pair' (crypto), 'futures' (futures contract), 'index' (market index), 'option_strategy' (options watchlist only), 'tokenized_stock'. Different object types are surfaced differently in the app.

symbol.description: Human-readable ticker (e.g. 'AAPL' for instrument, 'BTC-USD' for currency_pair). May be empty for futures items if the upstream lookup failed.

has_futures_contracts.description: True when at least one item is a futures contract. Mention to the user when surfacing items so they know which rows are futures.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: For instruments (object_type=instrument) the symbol is the ticker — pass to get_quotes for prices. For crypto (currency_pair), symbol is the pair (BTC-USD). The has_futures_contracts flag at the top tells you whether any futures items are present — futures behavior is different (the object_id is the active contract, not the product). When presenting to the user, lead with symbol + object_type; omit object_id unless asked.

name: get_watchlists
description: List the user's watchlists, including both user-created custom lists and Robinhood-curated lists the user follows. Use to look up list_id values for other watchlist tools.

id.description: List UUID. Pass to other watchlist tools (get_watchlist_items, add/remove_from_watchlist, update_watchlist) as list_id.

display_description.description: Optional short description shown under the name.

icon_emoji.description: Emoji shown alongside the name. Present on custom lists; absent on Robinhood-curated lists.

owner_type.description: 'custom' means a user-created list. 'robinhood' means a curated list the user is following. Use this to distinguish user-owned lists (writable: rename, delete items, add items) from curated lists (read + follow/unfollow only).

item_count.description: Number of items in the list.

allowed_object_types.description: Which kinds of objects can be added to this list. Common values: instrument (US stock/ETF), currency_pair (crypto), index (market index), option_strategy (options watchlist — see add_option_to_watchlist), futures. add_to_watchlist supports instrument, currency_pair, and index; options use the dedicated add_option_to_watchlist tool; futures still require the Robinhood app.

watchlists.description: One entry per watchlist the user has created or follows.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Distinguish lists by owner_type: 'custom' lists are writable (add_to_watchlist, remove_from_watchlist, update_watchlist); 'robinhood' lists are read-only and managed via follow_watchlist / unfollow_watchlist. When the user picks a list to act on, prefer matching by display_name and confirm before destructive actions.

name: mark_alerts_read
description:
Mark fired alerts as read so already-handled events are not reported to the user twice. Call it after relaying fired alerts from get_alert_log.

Parameter rules:
- Provide exactly one of alert_log_ids or all_through.
- alert_log_ids marks specific events; all_through marks every event triggered at or before that instant, across ALL symbols — not only the ones just discussed.

alert_log_ids.description: Fired-alert event ids from get_alert_log's alert_log_id (never alert_id). At most 100 per call — the server enforces the exact cap and rejects oversized batches naming the current limit.

all_through.description: RFC3339 timestamp: mark every event triggered at or before this instant as read, across all symbols. Set it to the triggered_at of the newest event you relayed so later events stay unread. Never a future timestamp — the upstream rejects it, and one would silently suppress unread state for alerts that have not fired yet.

marked.description: Always true on a non-error result — acceptance only, not confirmation that anything changed. The upstream silently no-ops unknown, foreign, or already-read ids and never reports how many events changed state; re-read get_alert_log's total_unread_count to confirm.

scope.description: 'alert_log_ids' when specific fired events were marked, 'all_through' when a watermark was used.

alert_log_id_count.description: How many alert_log_ids were sent (events scope only) — the request size, not a changed-state count.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: This only clears the unread marker used to track which events have been handled — it does not delete events or change any alert setting, so do not describe it to the user as turning an alert off. The response confirms acceptance only — no count of cleared events is available; re-read get_alert_log's total_unread_count if a number is needed. Call this only after the fired alerts have actually been relayed to the user. Marking all with all_through clears every unread event across all symbols triggered at or before that instant, not only the ones just discussed.

name: place_advanced_order
description:
Place an OCO (one-cancels-the-other) equity order with real money: a take-profit limit leg and a stop-loss leg on the same symbol, side, and quantity, where filling one cancels the other. Requires an agentic_allowed=true account; non-agentic accounts are rejected — do not call.

Workflow: by default call review_advanced_order first, present both legs and any alerts, and get explicit user confirmation before calling this tool. Idempotency: pass a fresh UUID as ref_id on the first call and re-send the same ref_id on transient retries.

OCO rules:
- Both legs use the same symbol, side, and quantity.
- take_profit_limit_price and stop_loss_stop_price are required and must differ.
- For a sell OCO (protecting a long): take_profit_limit_price must be ABOVE stop_loss_stop_price. For a buy OCO (covering a short): stop_loss_stop_price must be ABOVE take_profit_limit_price.
- time_in_force defaults to gtc. market_hours must be regular_hours (the only session OCO supports) — omit it or pass regular_hours explicitly.
- take_profit_limit_price and stop_loss_stop_price must each be at least 0.25% away from the current market price, and at least $0.10 apart from each other, or the order will be rejected — don't propose prices tighter than that.

name: place_crypto_order
description:
Place a real crypto order with real money. Parameters mirror preview_crypto_order plus the optional ref_id. Requires an agentic-enabled crypto account.

Workflow: by default call preview_crypto_order first, present the estimated cost/credit and any validation errors, and get explicit user confirmation before calling this tool. Skip the preview only when the user has very explicitly asked to bypass it — a generic "place this order" is NOT a bypass.

Idempotency: pass a fresh UUID as ref_id on the first call for each logical order, and re-send the SAME ref_id on retries of transient failures. Use a new ref_id only when the user wants a new order.

Parameter rules:
- Provide exactly one of quantity or dollar_amount; dollar_amount works with every type.
- limit_price is required for limit and stop_limit; stop_price is required for stop_loss and stop_limit.
- symbol is resolved to a currency pair before placement; pass a bare asset symbol (e.g. 'BTC') or a pair ('BTC-USD').
- tax_lots (specified-lot selling, sell only): first call get_crypto_tax_lots for the symbol (optionally with strategy + quantity), then pass tax_lots as {open_lot_id, quantity} pairs whose quantities sum to the order quantity. Omit for the default disposal. Quantity-based sells only; check selection_state first. Lot quantities take at most 8 decimal places, and the order quantity must be a multiple of the pair's min_order_quantity_increment (see get_currency_pairs); an off-increment quantity is rejected before placement because the lot quantities would no longer match it. Lot availability is verified when the order is placed, so a preview can pass and the place can still be rejected — e.g. a lot was used by another order, its available quantity changed, or specified-lot selling is no longer enabled for the asset.
- Accounts that require trade approval may not be able to carry a specified-lot sell; if the error mentions TAX_LOT_APPROVALS_DISABLED, tell the user and offer to retry without tax_lots (default disposal).

rhs_account_number.description: Numeric brokerage account number (the 'rhs_account_number' field on get_accounts entries — distinct from the alphanumeric 'account_number'). Must be an agentic-enabled crypto account. Required.

symbol.description: Crypto symbol (e.g. 'BTC', 'ETH', or 'BTC-USD'). Resolved to a currency pair before the order is placed. Required.

type.description: 'market', 'limit', 'stop_loss', or 'stop_limit'. Required. 'stop_loss' is a stop-triggered market order — despite the name it applies to buy stops too; the equity/option tools call the same concept 'stop_market'. ALWAYS call these by their app names when speaking to the user, including when listing what types are supported: 'stop_loss' is a 'stop order' and 'stop_limit' a 'stop limit order'; the raw values are tool inputs only. A user asking for a 'stop loss', 'stop order', or 'stop market' order means this stop_loss type — do not ask which stop type (but a limit price given alongside the trigger makes it stop_limit); ask only when the phrasing names no type, e.g. a bare 'stop' or 'protect my position'.

quantity.description: Asset quantity to trade (e.g. amount of BTC). Provide exactly one of quantity or dollar_amount. Crypto is measured in coins/units, not shares — when speaking to the user, including order confirmations, NEVER call a crypto quantity 'shares' ('shares' is equity terminology); state the amount of the asset, e.g. '0.001542 ETH'.

dollar_amount.description: USD notional (e.g. '100.00'). Valid with every order type. Provide exactly one of quantity or dollar_amount. For market, quantity is derived server-side: a buy is sized at the current market price — the same sizing as the app — so the typical debit is ~dollar_amount, with a worst case up to ~1% more if the price moves before execution (the buy collar); a sell is likewise sized at the current market price, so the typical credit is ~dollar_amount, with a worst case up to ~5% less if the price moves before execution (the sell collar). For stop_loss, quantity is derived from dollar_amount at stop_price (the trigger price) when the order is placed, not the live quote — the triggered market order executes near the trigger, so the typical fill notional is ~dollar_amount, with a worst case up to the collar worse (a higher debit for buy stops, a lower credit for sell stops). For limit and stop_limit, quantity is derived from dollar_amount at limit_price when the order is placed — fills execute at the limit price or better, so a buy's debit is capped at dollar_amount (no collar buffer; on fee-priced accounts fee rounding can add at most one cent) and a sell's credit is at least the derived quantity's worth at the limit, minus any fee. On fee-priced accounts a buy's quantity is sized from the fee-netted amount so the total debit targets dollar_amount, and a sell's fee is deducted from the credit.

limit_price.description: Limit price; required for limit and stop_limit.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price; required for stop_loss and stop_limit.

time_in_force.description: Allowed values depend on type. market and limit: 'gtc' (good till canceled) only — market orders execute immediately so a bounded duration does not apply, and limit orders are always for 90 days; omit this field or pass 'gtc' for both. stop_loss and stop_limit: 'gtc' (good for 90 days), 'gfd' (good for day), 'gfw' (good for 7 days), or 'gfm' (good for 30 days). If omitted, defaults to gtc for market and limit, and gfd for stop_loss and stop_limit. 'ioc' is NEVER supported for crypto orders.

Omit for the default. Sell only; quantity-based orders only (not dollar_amount); at most 50 lots; only when get_crypto_tax_lots reports selection_state 'enabled'.

guide.description: The order has been submitted — not necessarily filled. Describe it with state. Tell the user the order was placed, summarize side, type (ALWAYS the app's name: stop_loss = "stop order", stop_limit = "stop limit order" — never show the raw values to the user), quantity (or dollar amount) phrased as an amount of the asset (e.g. '0.001542 ETH') and never as 'shares', any limit/stop prices, and the estimated fee — from estimated_fee, shown even when 0, with the fee_rate value appended verbatim in parentheses when present, e.g. '$1.23 (0.5% maker)' or '$1.23 (0.35%)', or the fee_context value appended verbatim in parentheses when fee_rate is absent and fee_context is present, e.g. '$0 (asset not eligible for fee tiers)' (never re-derive, re-label, or reword either parenthetical; none when both are absent). When tax_withholding is present, give the backup withholding as its own line in the confirmation: show whichever of tax_withholding.estimated_withholding_amount / total_withholding_amount is present (exactly one ever is), labeled "Estimated backup withholding" for the estimate and "Backup withholding" for the total, with the tax_withholding.withholding_rate value appended verbatim in parentheses, e.g. 'Estimated backup withholding: $23.88 (24%)'; never mention withholding when tax_withholding is absent. State the total from whichever net_* field the order carries — labeled estimated for net_rounded_estimated_notional, final (or "so far" while cumulative_quantity is below quantity) for net_rounded_executed_notional — never from rounded_estimated_notional_with_estimated_fee, which is net of the fee only and will overstate a withholding-subject sell; if neither net total is present, give no total figure. Remind them it may not have filled yet and can be checked or canceled via id. For orders entered by dollar_amount, quantity is derived at placement — from the live quote for market orders (a buy is sized at the market price like the app: debit typically ~the dollar_amount, worst case up to ~1% more; a sell likewise sized at the market price: credit typically ~the dollar_amount, worst case up to ~5% less), from the stop price for stop_loss orders (typical fill notional ~the dollar_amount, worst case up to the collar worse), from the limit price for limit and stop limit orders. For market and stop_loss present the derived quantity as estimated until the order fills; for limit and stop_limit the derived quantity is exact at placement and a buy's total is capped at the requested amount. On fee-priced accounts a sell's fee is deducted from the credit. For orders entered by quantity, the amount is exact. Identify the account by the crypto_account_number returned in the response, not by the brokerage account number the tool was called with. When tax_lots were provided, say the order sells the specified lots; otherwise do not mention lots. On error, the order was NOT placed — report the error verbatim.

name: place_equity_order
description:
Place a real equity order with real money. Parameters mirror review_equity_order plus the optional ref_id. Requires an agentic_allowed=true account; non-agentic accounts are rejected — do not call.

Workflow: by default call review_equity_order first, present the estimated cost and any alerts, and get explicit user confirmation before calling this tool. Skip review only when the user has very explicitly asked to bypass it (e.g. "skip the review", "just place it, don't review") — a generic "place this order" is NOT a bypass.

Idempotency: pass a fresh UUID as ref_id on the first call for each logical order, and re-send the SAME ref_id on retries of transient transport failures. Use a new ref_id only when the user wants a new order.

Parameter rules:
- If the user has not specified type, ask. For immediate fills with price protection, prefer a marketable limit at the current ask over a plain market.
- Outside regular hours, only limit orders execute. For an immediate fill during extended or overnight/24-hour sessions, place a limit order (a marketable limit at the current ask) with market_hours set to that session — not a market order. Market and stop orders are regular_hours-only; placed after hours as regular_hours they queue for the next regular open.
- Provide exactly one of quantity or dollar_amount, and take the value from the user — if they did not say how much, ask. Never substitute a default such as 1 share or $100. dollar_amount requires type=market (server computes shares from last_trade_price).
- Fractional shares: only on type=market with market_hours=regular_hours, eligible accounts, up to 6 decimal places, no short sells.
- limit_price required for limit/stop_limit; stop_price required for stop_market/stop_limit.
- Fractional and dollar-based orders only place in regular_hours; the tool rejects them in other sessions.
- tax_lots (specified-lot selling, sell only): to sell specific lots, first call get_equity_tax_lots for the symbol, then pass tax_lots as {open_lot_id, quantity} pairs whose quantities sum to the order quantity. Omit for default (FIFO) cost basis. US accounts only; not allowed with dollar_amount, stop orders, all_day_hours, or fractional limit orders.

symbol.description: Stock symbol.

type.description: 'market', 'limit', 'stop_market', or 'stop_limit'.

quantity.description: Number of shares. Decimals (fractional) allowed for market + regular_hours only.

dollar_amount.description: USD notional (e.g. '100.00'). Only valid with type=market.

limit_price.description: Limit price; required for limit or stop_limit.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price; required for stop_market or stop_limit.

time_in_force.description: 'gfd' or 'gtc'. Default: gfd.

market_hours.description: 'regular_hours' (default, 9:30–16:00 ET), 'extended_hours' (pre-/post-market), or 'all_day_hours' (the 24 Hour Market / overnight session). extended_hours and all_day_hours execute limit orders only — market, stop_market, and stop_limit are regular_hours-only and are rejected if tagged to another session.

To sell specific tax lots instead of the default FIFO cost basis, pass the exact lots as {open_lot_id, quantity} objects, where open_lot_id comes from get_equity_tax_lots and the quantities sum to the order quantity. Omit for default FIFO. Sell only; at most 30 lots; US accounts only. Not allowed with dollar_amount, stop_market/stop_limit, all_day_hours, or fractional-share limit orders.

name: place_option_order
description:
Place a real options order with real money.

Workflow: by default call review_option_order first, present the alerts, fees, collateral, and quote, and get explicit user confirmation before calling this tool. Skip review only when the user has very explicitly asked to bypass it (e.g. "skip the review", "just place it, don't review") — a generic "place this order" is NOT a bypass.

Capability: single-leg options orders — Level 2 strategies (covered calls, cash-secured puts, long calls and puts). Multi-leg spreads (Level 3 strategies) are supported on option_level_3 accounts.

Account requirements: confirm via get_accounts that the chosen account is agentic_allowed=true AND has option_level_2 or option_level_3. If agentic_allowed=false do NOT call. If option_level is empty or option_level_0, do NOT call; follow the get_accounts guide for how to direct the user to enroll.

Alert handling: pre-trade alerts surface only in review_option_order. After the user has acknowledged the reviewed alert, call this tool with the same parameters.

Idempotency: pass a fresh UUID as ref_id on the first call for each logical order, and re-send the SAME ref_id on retries of transient transport failures. Use a new ref_id only when the user wants a new order.

To find option_id: get_option_chains → get_option_instruments filtered by expiration_date/strike_price/type.

Parameter rules:
- Multi-leg leg layouts — vertical spread: two legs, same expiration, different strikes, opposite sides. Calendar: two legs, same strike, different expirations. Iron condor: four legs, a put spread plus a call spread. Roll: close the leg you hold (position_effect 'close', side opposite the position) plus open the replacement ('open').
- Get the net price from the user rather than inferring it from individual leg quotes.
- Multi-leg is not available on cash or retirement accounts through this tool.
- type: 'limit' (default), 'market', 'stop_limit', 'stop_market'. price for limit/stop_limit; stop_price for stop_market/stop_limit.
- market, stop_market, and stop_limit are single-leg only. market and stop_market are also regular_hours, GFD only. stop_market is sell-to-close only with stop_price below the current ask.

Not currently supported anywhere (including the Robinhood apps):
- combo orders. At Robinhood, "combo" specifically means a stock-option combo: one option leg paired with 100 shares of the underlying equity. In broader industry use, "combo" without qualifier sometimes refers to multi-leg option structures.

position_effect.description: 'open' (new position) or 'close' (existing position). To close a long use sell; to close a short use buy.

ratio_quantity.description: Contracts for this leg per unit of the order's quantity. Defaults to 1, which is what standard spreads, condors, calendars, and rolls use. Must be 1 on a single-leg order; across legs the ratios must be in lowest terms (1:2, not 2:4).

legs.description: 1 to 4 legs, all on the same underlying and each a different contract. Several legs are filled together as one strategy. Should match the legs the user reviewed.

direction.description: Net direction of the whole order: 'debit' (you pay the net premium) or 'credit' (you receive it). Required with 2 or more legs; for one leg it is derived from that leg's side, so omit it.

type.description: 'limit' (default), 'market', 'stop_limit', or 'stop_market'. Should match the type the user reviewed. Only 'limit' is available with 2 or more legs.

quantity.description: Positive integer contract count. With several legs it counts whole strategies — each leg fills quantity × its ratio_quantity contracts.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price per contract. Required for stop_limit/stop_market; must be omitted for limit/market.

time_in_force.description: 'gfd' (default) or 'gtc'. Market orders must be 'gfd'.

market_hours.description: 'regular_hours' (default), 'regular_curb_hours', or 'regular_curb_overnight_hours'. Non-limit-immediate orders only place in regular_hours. CURB requires an index chain with extended_hours_state='enabled'.

direction.description: 'debit' (you pay) or 'credit' (you receive) on the overall order.
