Summarize chain_symbol, opening_strategy or closing_strategy, quantity, price, direction; remind the user it may not have filled and that they can check status or cancel via id. Source chain_symbol from the response directly. On error, the order was NOT placed; report the error verbatim. CURB-rejection errors mean market_hours is incompatible with the chain or the CURB session is closed — suggest 'regular_hours' or waiting for the session.

name: preview_crypto_order
description:
Simulate a crypto order without placing it — returns the transient order shape with the estimated cost/credit and fees resolved, plus any pre-trade validation errors. Call this by default before place_crypto_order unless the user has very explicitly asked to skip the preview. Requires an agentic-enabled crypto account.

Parameter rules:
- Provide exactly one of quantity or dollar_amount; dollar_amount works with every type.
- limit_price is required for limit and stop_limit; stop_price is required for stop_loss and stop_limit.
- symbol is resolved to a currency pair before the preview; pass a bare asset symbol (e.g. 'BTC') or a pair ('BTC-USD').
- tax_lots (specified-lot selling, sell only): first call get_crypto_tax_lots for the symbol (optionally with strategy + quantity), then pass tax_lots as {open_lot_id, quantity} pairs whose quantities sum to the order quantity. Omit for the default disposal. Quantity-based sells only; check selection_state first. Lot quantities take at most 8 decimal places, and the order quantity must be a multiple of the pair's min_order_quantity_increment (see get_currency_pairs); an off-increment quantity is rejected before the preview because the lot quantities would no longer match it. Lot availability is verified when the order is placed, so a preview can pass and the place can still be rejected — e.g. a lot was used by another order, its available quantity changed, or specified-lot selling is no longer enabled for the asset.

rhs_account_number.description: Numeric brokerage account number (the 'rhs_account_number' field on get_accounts entries — distinct from the alphanumeric 'account_number'). Must be an agentic-enabled crypto account. Required.

symbol.description: Crypto symbol (e.g. 'BTC', 'ETH', or 'BTC-USD'). Resolved to a currency pair before the preview. Required.

type.description: 'market', 'limit', 'stop_loss', or 'stop_limit'. Required. 'stop_loss' is a stop-triggered market order — despite the name it applies to buy stops too; the equity/option tools call the same concept 'stop_market'. ALWAYS call these by their app names when speaking to the user, including when listing what types are supported: 'stop_loss' is a 'stop order' and 'stop_limit' a 'stop limit order'; the raw values are tool inputs only. A user asking for a 'stop loss', 'stop order', or 'stop market' order means this stop_loss type — do not ask which stop type (but a limit price given alongside the trigger makes it stop_limit); ask only when the phrasing names no type, e.g. a bare 'stop' or 'protect my position'.

quantity.description: Asset quantity to trade (e.g. amount of BTC). Provide exactly one of quantity or dollar_amount. Crypto is measured in coins/units, not shares — when speaking to the user, including order confirmations, NEVER call a crypto quantity 'shares' ('shares' is equity terminology); state the amount of the asset, e.g. '0.001542 ETH'.

dollar_amount.description: USD notional (e.g. '100.00'). Valid with every order type. Provide exactly one of quantity or dollar_amount. For market, quantity is derived server-side: a buy is sized at the current market price — the same sizing as the app — so the typical debit is ~dollar_amount, with a worst case up to ~1% more if the price moves before execution (the buy collar); a sell is likewise sized at the current market price, so the typical credit is ~dollar_amount, with a worst case up to ~5% less if the price moves before execution (the sell collar). For stop_loss, quantity is derived from dollar_amount at stop_price (the trigger price) when the order is placed, not the live quote — the triggered market order executes near the trigger, so the typical fill notional is ~dollar_amount, with a worst case up to the collar worse (a higher debit for buy stops, a lower credit for sell stops). For limit and stop_limit, quantity is derived from dollar_amount at limit_price when the order is placed — fills execute at the limit price or better, so a buy's debit is capped at dollar_amount (no collar buffer; on fee-priced accounts fee rounding can add at most one cent) and a sell's credit is at least the derived quantity's worth at the limit, minus any fee. On fee-priced accounts a buy's quantity is sized from the fee-netted amount so the total debit targets dollar_amount, and a sell's fee is deducted from the credit.

limit_price.description: Limit price; required for limit and stop_limit.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price; required for stop_loss and stop_limit.

time_in_force.description: Allowed values depend on type. market and limit: 'gtc' (good till canceled) only — market orders execute immediately so a bounded duration does not apply, and limit orders are always for 90 days; omit this field or pass 'gtc' for both. stop_loss and stop_limit: 'gtc' (good for 90 days), 'gfd' (good for day), 'gfw' (good for 7 days), or 'gfm' (good for 30 days). If omitted, defaults to gtc for market and limit, and gfd for stop_loss and stop_limit. 'ioc' is NEVER supported for crypto orders.

open_lot_id.description: open_lot_id of the open tax lot to sell, from get_crypto_tax_lots.

quantity.description: Units to sell from this lot as a decimal string; at most the lot's quantity_available (or exactly quantity_to_sell from a strategy result).

tax_lots.description: Optional specified-lot selection for a SELL order. To sell specific tax lots instead of the default disposal, pass {open_lot_id, quantity} objects where open_lot_id comes from get_crypto_tax_lots and the quantities sum to the order quantity. Omit for the default. Sell only; quantity-based orders only (not dollar_amount); at most 50 lots; only when get_crypto_tax_lots reports selection_state 'enabled'.

ref_id.description: Client-supplied idempotency key from order placement. Useful for reconciling agent-placed orders against records the agent kept.

account_id.description: Crypto account UUID this order belongs to. Matches the account_id on get_crypto_positions rows.

currency_pair_id.description: Pair UUID (e.g. BTC-USD). Pass to get_crypto_quotes for current price, or match against get_currency_pairs.id.

currency_code.description: Asset currency code (e.g. 'BTC', 'ETH'). Useful for grouping orders by coin without joining against get_currency_pairs.

type.description: 'market', 'limit', 'stop_loss', or 'stop_limit'. 'stop_loss' is a stop-triggered market order — despite the name it applies to buy stops too; the equity/option tools call the same concept 'stop_market'. ALWAYS call these by their app names when speaking to the user, including when listing what types are supported: 'stop_loss' is a 'stop order' and 'stop_limit' a 'stop limit order'; the raw values are tool inputs only.

state.description: Raw lifecycle state: new, queued, unconfirmed, confirmed, partially_filled, filled, canceled, rejected, failed, voided. Combine with derived_state for clearer end-state classification.

derived_state.description: Normalized lifecycle classification, e.g. 'open' / 'closed' / similar shorthand the upstream computes from raw state + fills. Prefer over state for user-facing summaries.

state_group.description: 'open' or 'closed' — the headline answer to 'is this order still working?'.

time_in_force.description: 'gtc' (good till canceled), 'gfd' (good for day), 'ioc' (immediate or cancel), 'gfw' (good for week), 'gfm' (good for month).

quantity.description: Originally-requested asset quantity. On dollar-based orders the server derives it at placement: from the quote for market and from the stop price for stop_loss (treat those as estimated until fills confirm them), and from the limit price for limit/stop_limit (exact at placement).

cumulative_quantity.description: Total asset quantity filled so far. Less than quantity while partially filled; equal once filled.

canceled_quantity.description: Quantity that was canceled before fill (only populated on partial-fill-then-cancel paths).

price.description: Order price (interpretation depends on type — limit price for limit; for stop_loss it is the collared worst-case execution bound, NOT the trigger, which lives in stop_price; for market it is the raw quote side-price on a preview_crypto_order response — the same price the app displays, NOT collared — but the collared worst-case execution bound on placed orders; stablecoin pairs are never collared, so their preview and placed prices both carry the raw quote). Use limit_price / stop_price for the unambiguous fields.

limit_price.description: Limit price for limit / stop_limit orders. Null for market / stop_loss.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price for stop_loss / stop_limit orders. Null for market / limit.

average_price.description: Volume-weighted average fill price across executions. Null until the first fill.

entered_price.description: Price the user originally entered (pre-collaring). Different from limit_price after server-side collaring adjusts the order.

rounded_executed_notional.description: Total notional filled so far in the quote currency, rounded to 2 decimals.

price.description: Reported fill price per unit asset (e.g. USD per BTC). For the price the user actually paid after venue adjustments, use effective_price.

effective_price.description: Per-unit price after venue fees or price adjustments are applied — closer to the user's realized fill economics than price.

quantity.description: Asset quantity filled in this execution.

notional.description: effective_price * quantity, rounded to 2 decimals where applicable.

exchange_name.description: Routing venue name. Treat as informational; do not surface unless the user asks about routing.

executions.description: Per-fill detail. Reference for per-execution timing or price questions; for headline 'what did this fill at?' use average_price.

initiator_type.description: Source that placed the order: 'api_trading', 'trading_view', 'recurring', 'paycheck', 'rh_assistant', 'agentic_trading' (when nummus adds that enum value), or one of the internal crypto-specific values. Tells the user whether they placed this order via app, API, recurring buy, or an agent.

speculative.description: True when the order was created as a speculative pre-trade check (no upstream side effect). Should always be false on real placed orders; populated read-only by upstream.

updated_at.description: Last server-side state update (UTC) — fill, cancel, reject, etc.

canceled_at.description: When the cancel was acknowledged. Null when the order has not been canceled.

routing.description: How the order is routed for execution. Present verbatim as the routing line item; absent when routing information is unavailable.

rounded_estimated_notional_with_estimate.description: Estimated total cost (buy) or net proceeds (sell) in the quote currency, with ONLY the estimated fee already included. It does NOT include any additional taxes or deductions.

rounded_uncollared_estimated_notional_wi.description: Same as rounded_estimated_notional_with_estimated_fee but before price collaring. Null when collaring does not apply.

rounded_executed_notional_with_fee.description: Notional actually executed so far only including fees without netting additional taxes, in the quote currency. Grows as fills come in; 0 before the first fill. For the executed figure net of all taxes and fees use net_rounded_executed_notional.

total_executed_notional.description: Total executed notional so far only including fees without netting additional taxes. Null until there are fills.

net_rounded_estimated_notional.description: Estimated total cost (buy) or credit (sell) net of ALL taxes and fees. On a preview, present this as the estimated total cost or credit line item alongside the separate estimated_fee value. Never subtract the fee or taxes from it again. Null when an order has fills.

net_rounded_executed_notional.description: Executed total cost (buy) or credit (sell) net of ALL taxes and fees — the definitive amount actually debited or credited. Null before the first fill. Grows as fills come in. Never subtract the fee or any taxes from it again.

fee_structure.description: How the fee was computed (e.g. a fixed percentage or a volume-tiered rate).

fee_amount.description: Fee amount in the quote currency (USD).

fee_ratio.description: Rate this fee was computed at, when applicable.

fee_data.description: This fee's amount, type, and rate.

fees.description: Itemized fee breakdown for exchange-routed orders. Empty or absent when the order carries no itemized fees.

withholding_rate.description: Withholding rate preformatted as a percent (e.g. '24%'), aggregated across the federal and any state portion. Print verbatim. Absent when no rate is available.

estimated_withholding_amount.description: Estimated USD to be withheld from this sell's proceeds. Present only while cumulative_quantity is 0. Exactly one of this and total_withholding_amount is ever present, so read the one that is there.

total_withholding_amount.description: Actual USD withheld from proceeds across fills so far (final once fully filled). Present only once cumulative_quantity is positive. Exactly one of this and estimated_withholding_amount is ever present, so read the one that is there.

tax_withholding.description: Backup withholding on this sell order's proceeds. Present only when withholding applies (sell orders for subject users; never on IRA accounts) — when absent, do not mention withholding. amount and withholding_rate are the display-ready figure and percent.

order.description: Transient preview of the order — same shape as a placed order (get_crypto_orders results), with estimated cost/credit and fees resolved. No order was placed; id and lifecycle fields are not meaningful.

fee_rate.description: Rate the estimated fee was computed at, preformatted: the bare percent on single-rate fee pricing (e.g. '0.35%'), suffixed with the liquidity role on maker/taker-priced accounts (e.g. '0.05% maker', '0.1% taker'). Absent when no fee rate applies to this order.

estimated_fee.description: Estimated fee for this order in USD. 0 when no fee applies to this order. The estimated total cost already includes this fee — never add them together or annotate the total with it.

fee_context.description: Why no fee rate applies to this order even though the account trades with fee pricing, preformatted for display (e.g. 'asset not eligible for fee tiers'). Only ever present when fee_rate is absent; absent when no explanation applies.

crypto_account_number.description: Crypto account number the order is previewed against. Present THIS as the account to the user — not the brokerage account number used to look the account up. When absent, refer to the account as the user's linked crypto account.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: This tool does NOT place the order — it returns a preview for the user to review. Present the preview as a table with exactly these rows, in this order: 1) side; 2) asset — symbol and pair, e.g. DOGE (DOGE-USD); 3) order type — ALWAYS the app's name: stop_loss = "stop order", stop_limit = "stop limit order"; never show the raw stop_loss/stop_limit values to the user; 4) quantity — always phrased as an amount of the asset (e.g. '0.001542 ETH'), never as 'shares'; for orders entered by quantity, the exact amount the user specified (for market and stop_loss label the per-unit price as estimated); for orders entered by dollar_amount, include the per-unit price (for market the response's price — the raw quote, the same price the app displays — with quantity derivation described under dollar_amount; the stop price for stop_loss, the limit price for limit/stop_limit) — label the quantity estimated for market and stop_loss, and exact for limit and stop_limit (derived deterministically from the limit price at placement); 5) limit price (limit and stop_limit orders only); 6) stop price (stop orders only); 7) notional entered (only when the resolved amount differs from what the user asked for); 8) time in force; 9) estimated fee — from estimated_fee, shown even when 0, with the fee_rate value appended verbatim in parentheses when present, e.g. "$1.23 (0.5% maker)" or "$1.23 (0.35%)"; when fee_rate is absent and fee_context is present, append the fee_context value verbatim in parentheses instead, e.g. "$0 (asset not eligible for fee tiers)" — never re-derive, re-label, or reword either parenthetical, and no parenthetical when both are absent; 10) estimated backup withholding — include this row ONLY when the order's tax_withholding is present, from tax_withholding.estimated_withholding_amount (the only amount a preview carries — it has no fills), labeled "Estimated backup withholding", with the tax_withholding.withholding_rate value appended verbatim in parentheses when present, e.g. "$23.88 (24%)"; never raise withholding at all when tax_withholding is absent; 11) estimated total cost or credit — from the order's net_rounded_estimated_notional, which is ALREADY net of both the fee in row 9 and the withholding in row 10, so present it as the bottom line and never subtract either row from it again; if it is absent, omit this row rather than substituting any other field as the total; label it plainly without qualifiers like "(fee included)"; ignore order.rounded_estimated_notional_with_estimated_fee, which is net of the fee only and will overstate a withholding-subject sell; a limit buy's final debit never exceeds it, a market buy's final debit is typically ~it with a worst case up to the collar more, a market sell's credit is typically ~it with a worst case up to the collar less, a stop order's fill notional is typically ~it with a worst case up to the collar worse; mention the collar sizing (see dollar_amount) only when the user asks why it is estimated; 12) routing. Directly below the table, add this line verbatim: "You can switch between Market Maker Routing and Exchange Routing anytime in the Robinhood app under Settings → Crypto → Fee Tiers." — omit it only when the routing row is absent. When tax_withholding is present, add this sentence verbatim directly below the table: "Your order will be subject to backup withholding. Please confirm your tax status at https://robinhood.com/tax-certification." — exactly as written, no rewording; omit it entirely when tax_withholding is absent. Identify the account by the crypto_account_number returned in the response, not by the brokerage account number the tool was called with. A request for a 'stop loss', 'stop order', or 'stop market' order is the stop_loss type — do not ask which stop type (a limit price given alongside the trigger makes it stop_limit); ask only when the phrasing names no type, e.g. a bare 'stop' or 'protect my position'. Then get explicit user confirmation before calling place_crypto_order. No order was created and no id was assigned; the response mirrors an order but is transient. When tax_lots were provided, say the order will sell the specified lots and that lot availability is confirmed only at placement; otherwise do not mention lots.

name: preview_scan
description:
Run a filter set against live market data and return the matching instruments WITHOUT saving a scan. Nothing is persisted and no scan_id is returned. A preview behaves exactly like creating a scan with these filters would — same filters, same default columns, same live evaluation — so it is the way to validate a filter set before create_scan or update_scan_filters.

Expression-based filters run here and save through create_scan (update_scan_filters rejects them). An expression filter sets expression (and omits filter_type): either a value expression with a numeric predicate (expression "dayVolume / volumeAvg(candleCount=30, candlePeriod=\"1d\", session=\"all\")", predicate PREDICATE_GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL, values ["1.5"]), or a boolean screen carrying the whole comparison inside the expression (expression "tradeAllDay.price > closeAvg(candleCount=50, candlePeriod=\"1d\", session=\"all\")", predicate PREDICATE_EQUAL, values ["True"]). An invalid expression comes back as a validation error from the market-data provider instead of failing a later save.

Prefer an enum filter_type whenever one covers the request — enum filters are pre-validated and render as standard, user-editable filters in Legend. Call get_scanner_filter_specs first; build a raw expression only when no enum filter covers the request.

Columns display values, filters screen. To show a datapoint in results without restricting matches, pass it in columns — never fake it with a no-op filter like ">= 0", which pollutes the scan's filter list. A column is a display_name plus an expression, or a standard column's display name alone ({"display_name": "Market cap"}). Scans read best with a few contextual columns supporting the filters (e.g. a put/call screen showing both raw volumes).

Parameters:
- filters (required, non-empty) — the complete filter set to evaluate.
- columns (optional) — extra result columns on top of the filters' own columns and the standard defaults. Note: an expression matching a standard column's canonical form is shown as that standard column, canonical name included.

filter_type.description: Wire-format enum name, e.g. "FILTER_TYPE_RSI". See the scanner-filter-specs resource for valid values. Omit when supplying expression.

predicate.description: Wire-format enum name, e.g. "PREDICATE_GREATER_THAN". See the scanner-filter-specs resource for the predicates supported by each filter.

values.description: Threshold values. Single-element for unary predicates, two-element for BETWEEN, multi-element for IN_LIST/ANY_OF. For a boolean expression screen, exactly ["True"].

interval.description: Time granularity for time-series filters (e.g. "1d"). Use one of the supported_intervals from the filter's scanner-filter-specs entry. Not used with expression — encode granularity inside the expression.

length.description: Lookback length for filters that need one (e.g. RSI period of 14). Use one of the supported_lengths from the filter's scanner-filter-specs entry. Not used with expression.

plot.description: Plot / price-field input for filters that have one (e.g. "open" or "close" for % Change). Use one of the supported_plots from the filter's scanner-filter-specs entry. Not used with expression.

expression.description: Raw market-data expression to screen on, e.g. "dayVolume / volumeAvg(candleCount=30, candlePeriod=\"1d\", session=\"all\")" with a numeric predicate, or a whole comparison like "tradeAllDay.price > closeAvg(candleCount=50, candlePeriod=\"1d\", session=\"all\")" with predicate "=" and values ["True"]. Accepted by preview_scan (validate without saving) and create_scan (save); update_scan_filters rejects expressions — to change an expression filter on a saved scan, call create_scan with that scan's scan_id and the full filter set (a new configuration version is appended; earlier versions are preserved). Omit filter_type when set. Prefer an enum filter_type whenever one covers the request.

display_title.description: Optional short label for an expression filter, shown as the results-column header (e.g. "Relative volume (30D)"). Only used with expression.

filters.description: Filters to evaluate, enum-based and/or expression-based. Enum filter: filter_type from get_scanner_filter_specs plus predicate/values and optional interval/length/plot. Expression filter: expression (omit filter_type) plus predicate/values and an optional display_title. At least one filter is required.

display_name.description: Column header, and the column's identity: matching an existing column's name (case-insensitively) customizes that column instead of adding a duplicate, and two columns cannot share a name. A filter with non-default interval/length names its column with those parameters (e.g. a 5-minute RSI filter's column is "RSI (14, 5M)") — matching it requires that exact name; a bare "RSI" next to it adds a separate, default-parameters RSI column. Without expression, must name a standard column (e.g. "Market cap", "RSI", "Volume") — an unknown name is rejected with the full list of valid ones.

expression.description: Raw market-data expression computing the column's value, built from get_scanner_datapoints (same language as expression filters), e.g. "optionsPutDayVolume / optionsCallDayVolume". Omit to reference a standard column by display_name alone. If the expression equals a standard column's canonical form, the column is saved as that standard column and display_name is REPLACED by its canonical name (e.g. "optionsPutDayVolume" always saves as "Total put volume").

visible.description: Whether the column shows in results. When omitted, a NEW column is visible, but a column customizing an existing filter-created column keeps that column's current visibility (some filter columns are deliberately hidden) — pass an explicit value to change it. A hidden column is still computed and saved.

order.description: Relative ordering among the columns passed in this call: lower comes first, columns without an order go last in the order given. The scan's standard default columns (Symbol, Name, price, Volume, ...) always come before these.

columns.description: Optional result columns to display on top of what the filters and the standard default columns already show. Each column: display_name plus either an expression (raw market-data expression from get_scanner_datapoints) or nothing (a standard column referenced by name, e.g. "Market cap"). Columns display values, filters screen — to show a datapoint without restricting results, add a column here, never a no-op filter (e.g. >= 0).

total_items.description: Total instruments matching the previewed filters right now. May exceed len(results) when the row limit is hit.

ticker.description: Trading symbol (e.g. AAPL). Sourced from the scan's symbol column; empty when the scan has no symbol column visible.

instrument_id.description: Robinhood instrument UUID. Pass to other trading tools that take an instrument_id.

instrument_type.description: Robinhood's own asset classification: EQUITY, OPTION, INDEX, CRYPTO, FUTURES_PRODUCT, FUTURES_CONTRACT, COMBO. NOT the vocabulary the asset-type filter accepts, and not translatable to it: EQUITY covers both stocks and ETFs, which that filter distinguishes. To screen on asset type, use the values listed in the asset-type filter's options from get_scanner_filter_specs, never a value copied from this field.

columns.description: Column display name -> cell value, for every visible column in the scan's configuration. Values are raw numeric strings, not display-formatted: columns whose header contains % hold ratios (multiply by 100 before presenting), large numbers can arrive in scientific notation, and floats carry precision noise. Always format before presenting. An empty string means the datapoint is undefined for that instrument; the row still matched the filters.

results.description: Matched instruments, live at time of execution. Exactly what a scan saved with these filters would return.

sorted_by.description: Sort column + direction applied to the preview results (e.g. "Market cap desc").

filter_type.description: Display label of the column this filter screens on, as shown in Legend (e.g. "RSI", "Market cap"). This is a user-editable label, so it is for describing the filter to the user — do NOT send it back as filter_type when re-applying filters; use filter_type_enum for that.

filter_type_enum.description: Wire-format enum name for this filter (e.g. "FILTER_TYPE_RSI") — the value to pass as a filter's filter_type when re-sending this filter to create_scan or update_scan_filters. FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM is the exception: such a filter is defined by its expression, so re-create it by sending the expression field to create_scan and omitting filter_type. Never send FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM as a filter_type — it would create an empty filter. Empty only when the filter has no recognized type.

values.description: Threshold values for the predicate. Single-element for >/</=, two-element for BETWEEN, multi-element for IN_LIST/ANY_OF.

interval.description: Time granularity for time-series filters (e.g. "1d", "1h"). Empty for snapshot filters.

length.description: Lookback length for filters that need one (e.g. RSI period of 14). Zero/omitted for filters that don't take a length.

plot.description: Plot / price-field input for filters that have one (e.g. % Change uses "open" or "close" to choose changeFromOpen vs changeFromClose). Empty for filters that don't take a plot.

expression.description: Upstream market-data expression this filter screens on. Populated for every filter, standard or custom — an enum filter type is a preset that compiles to an expression upstream. Useful for explaining precisely what the filter measures (which interval, lookback and session it uses). When re-applying a standard filter, send filter_type_enum rather than this; for a FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM filter this expression is exactly what to send, as the expression field of a create_scan filter.

filters_applied.description: The filters as parsed and applied. Expression filters echo back with filter_type_enum FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM and their expression.

result.description: Live market results for the previewed filter set. Nothing was saved: there is no scan_id, and nothing needs cleaning up.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description:
How to interpret the response:
- result.total_items and result.results are exactly what a scan saved with these filters would return right now. Results are live; a later run will differ.
- Nothing was persisted: there is no scan_id, the preview does not appear in get_scans, and there is nothing to clean up.
- result.filters_applied echoes the filters as parsed: enum filters carry their filter_type_enum; expression filters echo FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM with the expression.
- Columns you passed appear as keys in each result row's columns map — under the canonical standard name when an expression matched a standard column's form. An empty cell means the datapoint is undefined for that instrument; the row still matched the filters.

When presenting:
- Render results as a table and state total_items.
- Make clear this was a preview — nothing was saved. If the user is happy with the results, offer create_scan with the same filters, expressions included: create_scan is the tool that saves them (update_scan_filters does not accept expressions).

Error handling:
- "expression cannot be combined with filter_type" / "FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM requires an expression" / "interval/length/plot are not used with an expression" → fix the filter shape and retry; these are local checks, no market-data query was spent.
- A market-data validation error (quotes the rejected expression and the reason, e.g. an unknown function or an out-of-range argument) → fix the expression and preview again. Do not attempt a save until a preview succeeds.
- Each preview costs the same rate-limit budget as run_scan — fix everything you can between attempts rather than iterating one field at a time.

name: review_advanced_order
description:
Simulate an OCO equity order without placing it; returns any pre-trade alert (buying power, instrument halt, etc.). Call this by default before place_advanced_order unless the user very explicitly asked to skip review. Parameters mirror place_advanced_order. Requires an agentic_allowed=true account; non-agentic accounts are rejected — do not call.

OCO rules:
- Both legs use the same symbol, side, and quantity.
- take_profit_limit_price and stop_loss_stop_price are required and must differ.
- For a sell OCO (protecting a long): take_profit_limit_price must be ABOVE stop_loss_stop_price. For a buy OCO (covering a short): stop_loss_stop_price must be ABOVE take_profit_limit_price.
- time_in_force defaults to gtc. market_hours must be regular_hours (the only session OCO supports) — omit it or pass regular_hours explicitly.
- take_profit_limit_price and stop_loss_stop_price must each be at least 0.25% away from the current market price, and at least $0.10 apart from each other, or the order will be rejected — don't propose prices tighter than that.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Must come from the user or be clearly implied — never default from get_accounts. Must be agentic_allowed=true; non-agentic accounts are rejected.

symbol.description: Stock symbol. Both OCO legs are on this symbol.

side.description: 'buy' or 'sell'. Both legs use this side.

quantity.description: Whole-share quantity. Both legs use the same quantity.

time_in_force.description: Can be 'gfd' or 'gtc'.

market_hours.description: 'regular_hours' — the only session OCO supports; extended_hours and all_day_hours are rejected.

take_profit_limit_price.description: Limit price of the take-profit leg.

stop_loss_stop_price.description: Stop trigger price of the stop-loss leg. The stop-loss leg is always a stop-market order — there is no stop-limit option for it.

alert_type.description: Machine alert code in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. 'EQUITY_MAX_NOTIONAL_EXCEEDED'). New codes ship regularly — surface verbatim, do not enumerate.

alert_details.description: Alert-specific detail payload (e.g. the exceeded limit). Shape varies by alert_type; present verbatim.

alert.description: Pre-trade alert. Absent/null means the checks passed with no warnings.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol.

last_trade_price.description: Most recent regular-hours trade (9:30-16:00 ET). Stays frozen at the closing print after the close until the next open; not the official settled close.

last_non_reg_trade_price.description: Most recent pre-market / after-hours / overnight trade. Null during regular hours or when the symbol does not trade in the current session.

venue_last_non_reg_trade_time.description: Timestamp of last_non_reg_trade_price. Reveals which non-regular session the trade came from.

adjusted_previous_close.description: Prior-day close adjusted for splits, dividends, and mergers.

previous_close.description: Raw prior closing print — not corporate-action adjusted and not the official settled close.

previous_close_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD trading date that previous_close corresponds to. Null for symbols that have never had a settled close.

bid_price.description: Highest current buy-order price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

ask_price.description: Lowest current sell-order price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

has_traded.description: False for instruments that have never traded; price fields are meaningless when false.

state.description: Instrument listing state — 'active' is normal; other values (inactive, delisted, unlisted) mean the instrument is not in normal trading state.

quote_data.description: Live market data (single quote) for the shared OCO leg symbol; same shape and semantics as get_equity_quotes results[0].quote.

market_data_disclosure.description: Compliance market-data disclosure string (NBBO bid/ask with sizes + venue codes, last trade, and update time). Display this verbatim to the user. Empty only when live prices were unavailable.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: This tool does NOT place the order — it returns a preview for the user to review. Reaching it means the user opted into review, so present the plan (both legs with symbol, side, quantity, and prices) and get explicit confirmation before place_advanced_order. A null/absent alert means no broker warnings — NOT that confirmation can be skipped. Surface any alert verbatim alongside the preview. You MUST always show the quotes to the user for compliance reasons: whenever market_data_disclosure is present, display it to the user exactly as provided — verbatim and unmodified.

name: review_equity_order
description:
Simulate a stock order without placing it. Returns the current quote plus pre-trade alerts (buying power, PDT, instrument halt, etc.). Call this by default before place_equity_order unless the user has very explicitly asked to skip review. Requires an agentic_allowed=true account; non-agentic accounts are rejected — do not call.

Parameter rules:
- If the user has not specified type, ask. For immediate fills with price protection, prefer a marketable limit at the current ask over a plain market.
- Outside regular hours, only limit orders execute. For an immediate fill during extended or overnight/24-hour sessions, place a limit order (a marketable limit at the current ask) with market_hours set to that session — not a market order. Market and stop orders are regular_hours-only; placed after hours as regular_hours they queue for the next regular open.
- Provide exactly one of quantity or dollar_amount, and take the value from the user — if they did not say how much, ask. Never substitute a default such as 1 share or $100. dollar_amount requires type=market (server computes shares from last_trade_price).
- Fractional shares: only on type=market with market_hours=regular_hours, eligible accounts, up to 6 decimal places, no short sells.
- limit_price required for limit/stop_limit; stop_price required for stop_market/stop_limit.
- Fractional and dollar-based orders only place in regular_hours; the tool rejects them in other sessions.
- tax_lots (specified-lot selling, sell only): to sell specific lots, first call get_equity_tax_lots for the symbol, then pass tax_lots as {open_lot_id, quantity} pairs whose quantities sum to the order quantity. Omit for default (FIFO) cost basis. US accounts only; not allowed with dollar_amount, stop orders, all_day_hours, or fractional limit orders.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Must come from the user or be clearly implied — never default from get_accounts. Must be agentic_allowed=true; non-agentic accounts are rejected.

symbol.description: Stock symbol.

type.description: 'market', 'limit', 'stop_market', or 'stop_limit'.

quantity.description: Number of shares. Decimals (fractional) allowed for market + regular_hours only.

dollar_amount.description: USD notional (e.g. '100.00'). Only valid with type=market.

limit_price.description: Limit price; required for limit or stop_limit.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price; required for stop_market or stop_limit.

time_in_force.description: 'gfd' (good for day) or 'gtc' (good till cancelled). Default: gfd.

market_hours.description: 'regular_hours' (default, 9:30–16:00 ET), 'extended_hours' (pre-/post-market), or 'all_day_hours' (the 24 Hour Market / overnight session). extended_hours and all_day_hours execute limit orders only — market, stop_market, and stop_limit are regular_hours-only and are rejected if tagged to another session.

Updated 1:21 PM ET.'. The update time is rendered in the user's timezone (from the x-timezone-id header, default ET). Display this verbatim to the user. Empty only when live prices were unavailable.

Reaching this tool means the user opted into the review step, so you MUST present the preview to the user (symbol, side, type, quantity or dollar_amount, limit/stop prices, estimated execution) and get explicit confirmation before calling place_equity_order. This holds even when order_checks is empty ({}) — empty means no broker alerts, NOT that confirmation can be skipped; the user asked to review, so let them review. Surface any non-empty alert in order_checks verbatim alongside the preview. In addition, you MUST always show the quotes to the user for compliance reasons: whenever market_data_disclosure is present, display it to the user exactly as provided — verbatim and unmodified — as the required compliance quote disclosure. Market orders: estimate execution from quote_data.last_trade_price (ask for buys, bid for sells when spreads are wide). Limit orders: compare limit_price to quote_data bid/ask so the user knows the distance from market.

name: review_option_order
description:
Simulate an options order without placing it. Returns the current quote plus pre-trade alerts. Call this by default before place_option_order or replace_option_order unless the user has very explicitly asked to skip review.

Capability: single-leg options orders — Level 2 strategies (covered calls, cash-secured puts, long calls and puts). Multi-leg spreads (Level 3 strategies) are supported on option_level_3 accounts.

Account requirements: confirm via get_accounts that the chosen account is agentic_allowed=true AND has option_level_2 or option_level_3. If agentic_allowed=false do NOT call. If option_level is empty or option_level_0, do NOT call; follow the get_accounts guide for how to direct the user to enroll.

Parameter rules:
- legs: option_id (from get_option_instruments), side, position_effect, optional ratio_quantity per leg.
- Multi-leg leg layouts — vertical spread: two legs, same expiration, different strikes, opposite sides. Calendar: two legs, same strike, different expirations. Iron condor: four legs, a put spread plus a call spread. Roll: close the leg you hold (position_effect 'close', side opposite the position) plus open the replacement ('open').
- Get the net price from the user rather than inferring it from individual leg quotes.
- Multi-leg is not available on cash or retirement accounts through this tool.
- type: 'limit' (default), 'market', 'stop_limit', 'stop_market'. If unspecified, ask. price for limit/stop_limit; stop_price for stop_market/stop_limit.
- market, stop_market, and stop_limit are single-leg only. market and stop_market are also GFD, regular_hours only. stop_market is sell-to-close only with stop_price below the current ask. Non-limit-immediate types are blocked in any extended-hours session.
- Surface order_checks alerts verbatim — the detail strings carry the actual time/contract/BP values for the user.

account_number.description: Brokerage account number. Must come from the user or be clearly implied — never default from get_accounts. Must be agentic_allowed=true.

position_effect.description: 'open' (new position) or 'close' (existing position). To close a long use sell; to close a short use buy.

ratio_quantity.description: Contracts for this leg per unit of the order's quantity. Defaults to 1, which is what standard spreads, condors, calendars, and rolls use. Must be 1 on a single-leg order; across legs the ratios must be in lowest terms (1:2, not 2:4).

legs.description: 1 to 4 legs, all on the same underlying and each a different contract. Several legs are filled together as one strategy.

direction.description: Net direction of the whole order: 'debit' (you pay the net premium) or 'credit' (you receive it). Required with 2 or more legs; for one leg it is derived from that leg's side, so omit it.

type.description: 'limit' (default), 'market', 'stop_limit', or 'stop_market'. Only 'limit' is available with 2 or more legs.

quantity.description: Positive integer contract count. With several legs it counts whole strategies — each leg fills quantity × its ratio_quantity contracts.

price.description: Limit price (e.g. '1.50'). Per contract for one leg; with several legs it is the net premium of the whole strategy per unit of quantity, always positive — direction says whether it is paid or received. Required for limit/stop_limit; must be omitted for market/stop_market.

stop_price.description: Stop trigger price per contract. Required for stop_limit/stop_market; must be omitted for limit/market. For sell-side stop_market, must be below the current ask.

time_in_force.description: 'gfd' (default) or 'gtc'. Market orders must be 'gfd'.

market_hours.description: 'regular_hours' (default), 'regular_curb_hours', or 'regular_curb_overnight_hours'. Extended-hours sessions only accept limit+immediate. CURB requires an index chain with extended_hours_state='enabled' (per get_option_chains); rejection surfaces at place time.

chain_symbol.description: Underlying ticker (e.g. 'AAPL', 'SPXW'). Supply alongside underlying_type to include fees and collateral in the response — always do so when known.

underlying_type.description: 'equity' or 'index'. Required alongside chain_symbol to enable the fee + collateral fetch.

account_number.description: Echoed account_number. Mask all but the last 4 digits (e.g. '••••1234') when displaying to the user.

type.description: Echoed user-facing order type (limit / market / stop_limit / stop_market).

direction.description: Net direction the order was reviewed with: 'debit' (the user pays) or 'credit' (the user receives). Derived from the leg's side on a single-leg order.

quantity.description: Echoed contract count. With several legs it counts whole strategies.

price.description: Echoed limit price — per contract for one leg, the net premium of the whole strategy per unit of quantity with several legs. Omitted for market/stop_market.

stop_price.description: Echoed stop trigger price per contract. Omitted for limit/market.

time_in_force.description: Echoed time_in_force.

position_effect.description: 'open' (new position) or 'close' (existing position). To close a long use sell; to close a short use buy.

ratio_quantity.description: Contracts for this leg per unit of the order's quantity. Defaults to 1, which is what standard spreads, condors, calendars, and rolls use. Must be 1 on a single-leg order; across legs the ratios must be in lowest terms (1:2, not 2:4).

legs.description: Echoed request legs[] (option_id, side, position_effect, ratio_quantity per leg) so the response identifies which contract(s) were reviewed.

alertType.description: Identifies the pre-trade-check issue. Surface verbatim to the user along with details.

details.description: Alert-specific structured detail payload. Shape varies by alertType (e.g. deposit_amount, leg list, timing info).

order_checks.description: Pre-trade validation result. An empty object {} means the order is clean and safe to place. Non-empty carries alertType (the issue) plus alert-specific details.

instrument_id.description: UUID of the option contract; the canonical match key against closes[].instrument_id.

ask_price.description: Lowest current sell-side price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

bid_price.description: Highest current buy-side price. Zero when the book is closed or unavailable.

break_even_price.description: Underlying price at which the position breaks even at expiration (strike +/- premium).

adjusted_mark_price.description: Mark adjusted for corporate actions on the underlying. Use against historical cost basis.

mark_price.description: Mid-market fair value — canonical current price for valuation.

high_fill_rate_buy_price.description: Upper bound of the likely fast-fill range for a buy.

low_fill_rate_buy_price.description: Lower bound of the likely fast-fill range for a buy.

high_fill_rate_sell_price.description: Upper bound of the likely fast-fill range for a sell.

low_fill_rate_sell_price.description: Lower bound of the likely fast-fill range for a sell.

previous_close_price.description: Quote-derived prior close — best-effort, not the official settled close.

previous_close_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD trading date that previous_close_price corresponds to.

delta.description: Sensitivity of option price to a $1 move in the underlying.

gamma.description: Rate of change of delta per $1 move in the underlying.

rho.description: Sensitivity to a 1% change in interest rates.

theta.description: Daily time decay ($/day); negative for long positions.

vega.description: Sensitivity to a 1% change in implied volatility.

open_interest.description: Outstanding contracts not yet closed or expired.

chance_of_profit_long.description: Model probability the long side ends in profit at expiration, decimal.

chance_of_profit_short.description: Model probability the short side ends in profit at expiration, decimal.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the quote refresh.

option_quotes.description: Live option quote(s) for the legs; same shape as get_option_quotes quotes[].

fee_rate.description: Rate applied to compute this fee component, as a decimal string.

fee.description: Dollar amount charged for this component, as a decimal string.

fee_saving_rate.description: Rate of the Gold fee discount applied to this order.

fee_total_savings.description: Total dollar savings from Gold pricing on this order. Mention to the user when non-zero.

gold_fee_savings.description: Gold-member fee discount applied to this order. fee_total_savings is zero for non-Gold accounts.

display_name.description: User-facing label for this tax (e.g. 'GST'). Use this when surfacing taxes to the user.

sales_taxes.description: Applicable sales taxes. Empty for most US accounts; surface non-empty entries separately from fee components.

is_gold.description: True when Gold pricing was applied to this calculation.

total_fee.description: All-in fee the user will pay (or save, if negative due to Gold savings). Lead with this when presenting fees.

fees.description: Trading fees breakdown. Present only when chain_symbol and underlying_type were supplied. Lead with total_fee when presenting.

account_number.description: Account the collateral applies to; echoes the request. Mask all but the last 4 digits (e.g. '••••1234') when displaying to the user.

amount.description: Change in dollar collateral if the order fills, as a decimal string — computed against the account's existing positions and working orders, not for this order alone. Zero is a valid answer when existing positions already cover the new legs. null when the position carries infinite risk (infinite=true).

direction.description: 'debit' means buying power is held to cover the position; 'credit' means collateral is released.

infinite.description: True for naked short positions with unlimited risk (e.g. naked calls). Warn the user before they proceed.

cash.description: Change in dollar collateral if the order fills.

instrument_id.description: UUID of the underlying equity. Pass to get_equity_quotes / get_equity_tradability when the agent needs live data on the held equity.

instrument.description: URL of the equity instrument. Prefer instrument_id (the UUID) when calling other tools; the URL is retained for clients that consume hyperlinks.

symbol.description: Equity symbol whose shares are being held as collateral (e.g. 'AAPL').

quantity.description: Number of shares being held.

direction.description: 'debit' means shares are held; 'credit' means shares are released.

uncovered_shares.description: Shares of this symbol that do NOT yet cover the option position. Non-zero means additional cover is required.

equities.description: Share-based collateral required by the strategy (e.g. covered calls). Empty for most orders — only short equity-covered strategies require share collateral.

collateral.description: How this order changes the collateral held on the account, measured against its existing positions and working orders — a credit means collateral is released, and zero means existing positions already cover the new legs. Do NOT describe it as this order's standalone requirement or as unreliable. Present only when chain_symbol and underlying_type were supplied. Warn the user when cash.infinite=true (unlimited-risk position).

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: This tool does NOT place the order — it returns a preview for the user to review. Reaching this tool means the user opted into the review step, so you MUST present the preview to the user (legs, type, quantity, price/stop_price, alerts, fees, collateral, quote) and get explicit confirmation before calling place_option_order (for a new order) or replace_option_order (when modifying an existing order). This holds even when order_checks is empty ({}) — empty means no broker alerts, NOT that confirmation can be skipped; the user asked to review, so let them review. Non-empty order_checks: present alertType + details verbatim and ask the user to confirm before proceeding. On user ack, call place_option_order (or replace_option_order) with the same parameters. With several legs, present each leg (pair it with its option_quotes entry by instrument_id) and then the net direction and price for the order as a whole. Use option_quotes (mark_price, bid/ask, greeks) to help judge cost. When fees is present, lead with total_fee; mention gold_fee_savings when non-zero. When collateral is present, show cash amount/direction; warn on cash.infinite=true (unlimited-risk position) or non-empty equities (share-based collateral). Echo the order type: for market/stop_market remind the user the fill price is unbounded; for stop_limit/stop_market note the order only triggers when the underlying reaches stop_price.

name: run_scan
description:
Execute a saved scanner (also called screener) and return live market results. A scan's filters are evaluated against current market data at request time — results are real-time, not cached.

Returns the scan's title, the total number of matching instruments, a list of instrument rows (with ticker, instrument_id, type, and one cell per visible column), plus the active sort and filters. The agent should present results as a table and mention this is live data.

Parameters:
- scan_id (required) — the scan identifier from get_scans or create_scan. Returns an error if the scan does not exist or does not belong to the calling user.

Use get_scans first to discover available scan_ids if the user has not specified one.

scan_id.description: The scan identifier to execute. Get this from get_scans or create_scan.
Scan identifier. Stable across reads and writes.

total_items.description: Total instruments matching the scan's filters. May exceed len(results) when the scan's frontend_limit is hit.

ticker.description: Trading symbol (e.g. AAPL). Sourced from the scan's symbol column; empty when the scan has no symbol column visible.

instrument_id.description: Robinhood instrument UUID. Pass to other trading tools that take an instrument_id.

instrument_type.description: Robinhood's own asset classification: EQUITY, OPTION, INDEX, CRYPTO, FUTURES_PRODUCT, FUTURES_CONTRACT, COMBO. NOT the vocabulary the asset-type filter accepts, and not translatable to it: EQUITY covers both stocks and ETFs, which that filter distinguishes. To screen on asset type, use the values listed in the asset-type filter's options from get_scanner_filter_specs, never a value copied from this field.

columns.description: Column display name -> cell value, for every visible column in the scan's configuration. Values are raw numeric strings, not display-formatted: columns whose header contains % hold ratios (multiply by 100 before presenting), large numbers can arrive in scientific notation, and floats carry precision noise. Always format before presenting. An empty string means the datapoint is undefined for that instrument; the row still matched the filters.

results.description: Matched instruments, in the scan's current sort order. Live at time of execution.

sorted_by.description: Current sort column + direction in human form (e.g. "Volume desc"). Empty when no sort is configured.

filter_type.description: Display label of the column this filter screens on, as shown in Legend (e.g. "RSI", "Market cap"). This is a user-editable label, so it is for describing the filter to the user — do NOT send it back as filter_type when re-applying filters; use filter_type_enum for that.

filter_type_enum.description: Wire-format enum name for this filter (e.g. "FILTER_TYPE_RSI") — the value to pass as a filter's filter_type when re-sending this filter to create_scan or update_scan_filters. FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM is the exception: such a filter is defined by its expression, so re-create it by sending the expression field to create_scan and omitting filter_type. Never send FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM as a filter_type — it would create an empty filter. Empty only when the filter has no recognized type.

values.description: Threshold values for the predicate. Single-element for >/</=, two-element for BETWEEN, multi-element for IN_LIST/ANY_OF.

interval.description: Time granularity for time-series filters (e.g. "1d", "1h"). Empty for snapshot filters.

length.description: Lookback length for filters that need one (e.g. RSI period of 14). Zero/omitted for filters that don't take a length.

plot.description: Plot / price-field input for filters that have one (e.g. % Change uses "open" or "close" to choose changeFromOpen vs changeFromClose). Empty for filters that don't take a plot.

expression.description: Upstream market-data expression this filter screens on. Populated for every filter, standard or custom — an enum filter type is a preset that compiles to an expression upstream. Useful for explaining precisely what the filter measures (which interval, lookback and session it uses). When re-applying a standard filter, send filter_type_enum rather than this; for a FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM filter this expression is exactly what to send, as the expression field of a create_scan filter.

filters_applied.description: Filters in effect when the scan was run. Always populated on create_scan / update_scan_filters responses; optional on run_scan.

cortex_managed.description: True when this scan was created or modified by Cortex. Read-only via MCP tools.

result.description: Live scan results: matched instruments, total count, and the scan's metadata.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description:
How to interpret the response:
- result.total_items is the total number of instruments matching the scan's filters. result.results may contain fewer entries if the scan's frontend_limit caps the rows — mention this to the user when total_items > len(results).
- result.results is an array of matching instruments. Each entry has:
  - ticker: trading symbol (e.g. "AAPL"). Empty when the scan does not have a Symbol/Ticker column visible — use instrument_id then.
  - instrument_id: Robinhood instrument UUID. Pass this to other trading tools that take an instrument_id.
  - instrument_type: Robinhood's own asset classification (EQUITY, OPTION, INDEX, CRYPTO, FUTURES_PRODUCT, FUTURES_CONTRACT, COMBO). EQUITY covers both stocks and ETFs. This is NOT the vocabulary the asset-type filter accepts and it is not translatable to it: to screen on asset type, use the values listed in the asset-type filter's options from get_scanner_filter_specs, never a value copied from this field.
  - columns: map of column display name -> cell value. Values are RAW numeric strings, not display-formatted; always format them before presenting. In particular: columns whose header contains "%" (e.g. "% Change") hold RATIOS, so multiply by 100 (a cell of "-0.0059" is -0.59%, not -0.0059%); large numbers can arrive in scientific notation ("1.98e+11"); floats carry precision noise ("-0.6800000000000068") and need rounding. An empty string means the datapoint is undefined for that instrument (e.g. Market cap for an ETF); the row still matched the filters.
- result.sorted_by tells you the row order (e.g. "Volume desc"). Mention it when describing the table.
- result.filters_applied lists the filters in effect — useful for confirming "this scan currently filters by RSI > 70".
- result.cortex_managed: true means the scan was created by Cortex inside Legend. Reads are fine, but update_scan_filters / update_scan_config will reject Cortex-managed scans — tell the user that if they ask to modify it.

When presenting results:
- Render as a table with ticker as the leftmost column followed by the most user-relevant columns (% Change, Volume, etc.).
- State total_items so the user knows how big the match set is.
- Note that results are live as of execution time — they will differ if run again later.
- If results is empty: tell the user the scan returned 0 matches right now. Suggest relaxing filters with update_scan_filters if they want broader results.

Error handling:
- "scan does not exist or you do not have access to it" → the scan_id is wrong or the scan belongs to a different user. Suggest get_scans to see available scans.
- Rate-limited or upstream failure → surface the error verbatim, no automatic retry.

name: search
description: Resolve a natural-language query to Robinhood instruments (stocks/ETFs), crypto pairs, or market indexes. Use when the user names an asset by name (or partial name) instead of a ticker/pair/index symbol, or when you need an instrument_id / currency-pair UUID / market-index id for a downstream tool. Defaults to instrument search; pass asset_type="currency_pair" for crypto or asset_type="market_index" for indexes (SPX, NDX, DJI, etc.). Instrument results carry symbol + instrument_id (use with get_equity_quotes / get_equity_tradability / place_equity_order or any instrument_id-based tool). Crypto results carry hyphenated symbol (e.g. BTC-USD) + id — the symbol routes to crypto quote/order tools, the id routes to watchlist tools as currency_pair_ids. Market-index results carry symbol + id — pass id to index quote tools for current values, or in the index_ids array of watchlist tools.

query.description: Natural-language search query: company name, partial name, or ticker (e.g. "apple", "tesla motors", "AAPL"). Required.

asset_type.description: Asset category to search. Supported: "instrument" (US-listed stocks/ETFs), "currency_pair" (crypto pairs like BTC-USD), and "market_index" (e.g. SPX, NDX, DJI). Defaults to "instrument" when omitted. More categories (events, futures) will be added as their corresponding tools land.

limit.description: Max results to return. Defaults to 10; clamped to 20.

instrument_id.description: Robinhood instrument UUID. Pass to tools that take an instrument_id.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL. Pass to tools that take a symbol (get_equity_quotes, get_equity_tradability, place_equity_order).

name.description: Full instrument name, e.g. "Apple Inc. - Common Stock".

simple_name.description: Short product name shown in UI, e.g. "Apple". Omitted when upstream did not return one.

results.description: Matched instruments in upstream relevance order. Empty when no Robinhood-tradable instrument matches the query.

id.description: Currency-pair UUID. Pass in the currency_pair_ids array of watchlist tools, or match against the currency_pair_id field on crypto position rows. (Use the symbol, not this id, with crypto quote/order tools.)

symbol.description: Canonical hyphenated symbol (e.g. 'BTC-USD'). Pass to crypto quote/order tools.

currency_pairs.description: Matched crypto pairs in upstream relevance order. Populated when asset_type=currency_pair; absent for instrument searches. Each entry carries the id (pass in the currency_pair_ids array of watchlist tools) and the hyphenated symbol (e.g. BTC-USD; pass to crypto quote/order tools).

id.description: Market-index UUID. Pass to index quote tools for the current level, or in the index_ids array of watchlist tools.

symbol.description: Index ticker (e.g. 'SPX', 'NDX', 'DJI'). Cross-references the symbol on index snapshot tools.

description.description: Longer human-readable description when upstream provides one. May be empty.

market_indexes.description: Matched market indexes in upstream relevance order. Populated when asset_type=market_index. Each entry carries id + symbol + name (e.g. SPX, NDX, DJI); pass id to index quote tools for live values, or use symbol to cross-reference index snapshot tools.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Exactly one of results[] (instruments), currency_pairs[] (crypto), or market_indexes[] (indexes) is populated, matching the requested asset_type. Instrument entries carry symbol + instrument_id — pass symbol to symbol-based tools (get_equity_quotes, get_equity_tradability, place_equity_order) and instrument_id to id-based tools. Currency-pair entries carry hyphenated symbol (e.g. BTC-USD) + id — the symbol routes to crypto quote/order tools, the id routes to watchlist tools as currency_pair_ids. Market-index entries carry symbol + id — pass id to index quote tools for live values; the symbol cross-references index snapshot tools. Multiple results means the query was ambiguous (e.g. "apple" could match AAPL or APLE; "bitcoin" could match BTC-USD or BCH-USD); ask the user to disambiguate before placing trades. An empty result list means no Robinhood-tradable match — do not invent a symbol.

name: unfollow_watchlist
description: Stop following a Robinhood-curated list. The list itself is unchanged — it just no longer appears in the user's watchlists. Confirm with the user before calling.

list_id.description: UUID of the Robinhood-curated list to unfollow.
UUID of the list that was followed.

user_id.description: UUID of the user that followed the list (always the caller).

owner_type.description: Always 'robinhood' for follow_watchlist — only Robinhood-curated lists are followable.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the user first followed this list. The follower endpoint is idempotent — re-following an already-followed list returns the existing record, so this timestamp may be older than 'just now'.

follower.description: The new or pre-existing follower record. Omitted for unfollow which has no response body.

status.description: 'ok' when the upstream accepted the operation.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: 404 means the user wasn't following that list (already-clean state).

name: update_alert
description:
Change an existing price or indicator alert: enable/disable it, adjust its threshold or indicator settings, or switch its condition within the same family. Confirm the change with the user before calling — this is a real write.

Parameter rules:
- At least one of enabled, condition_type, threshold, or indicator is required; only the fields you send change, the rest keep their stored values.
- condition_type may only change within the alert's current condition family — e.g. price_above -> price_below, or sma_above -> price_above_sma (both sma family). To change the indicator family or the symbol, create a new alert instead.
- threshold/indicator rules per condition family match create_alert; conditions comparing price to an indicator line take no threshold.

alert_id.description: The alert to change — take it from get_alerts or create_alert; never construct one.

enabled.description: Set false to pause the alert or true to re-enable it. Omitted = unchanged.

condition_type.description: New condition for the alert — same vocabulary as create_alert. Omitted = unchanged.

threshold.description: New trigger price or target indicator value, as a decimal string. Omitted = unchanged.

period.description: Lookback window in bars. Required for sma/ema/rsi/boll conditions.

interval_secs.description: Bar size in seconds — one of 300 (5m), 600 (10m), 3600 (1h), 86400 (1d), 604800 (1w), or 2592000 (30d). Required for every indicator condition; vwap conditions support 300 only.

std_dev.description: boll only: number of standard deviations for the bands (commonly 2).

ma_type.description: boll only: which moving average the bands are built on — sma or ema.

indicator.description: New indicator configuration — replaces the stored one wholesale, so send the complete configuration when provided. Omitted = unchanged.

alert_id.description: Opaque identifier for this alert. Pass to update_alert/delete_alert; never construct one.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol. Bare symbol for equities (e.g. AAPL). For crypto this is the base currency code (e.g. BTC), not a trading pair — never BTC-USD.

enabled.description: Whether this alert is on. When false it will not fire until re-enabled; it has not been deleted.

condition_type.description: Which condition this alert uses, e.g. price_above, price_below, price_crosses, sma_above, rsi_below, price_crosses_sma, macd_above_signal. Labels derive from the upstream setting type, so these are examples, not the full set — new condition types may appear beyond them.

target_price.description: Decimal string. Set for plain price-threshold conditions (condition_type price_above/price_below/price_crosses).

target_value.description: Decimal string. Set for plain indicator-value conditions (e.g. condition_type sma_above, rsi_below).

kind.description: Which indicator family this configuration is for: sma, ema, vwap, rsi, macd, or boll.

period.description: Number of bars in the indicator's lookback window. Not set for vwap.

std_dev.description: boll only: number of standard deviations for the bands.

ma_type.description: boll only: which moving average the bands are built on, sma or ema.

indicator.description: Indicator configuration. Present whenever condition_type names a technical indicator.

condition.description: The configured threshold/indicator details for condition_type.

updated_at.description: RFC3339 last-updated time.

alert.description: The alert as stored after the update — the same shape get_alerts returns.

data.description: Tool-specific result payload; see the inner properties for fields.

guide.description: Confirm the new condition from the response, not from the request, and state what changed. Fields you did not send were left as they were. If the alert_id is unknown or no longer exists the call fails rather than creating a new alert — re-read get_alerts and confirm with the user before creating one.

name: update_scan_config
description:
Change the sort order of a saved scan's results table, and/or replace its extra result columns. The scan's filters are always preserved.

Parameters:
- scan_id (required) — the scan to modify.
- sorting_column (required unless columns is provided) — display name of the column to sort by. Must match a column on the scan; the error response lists available columns when no match is found.
- sorting_direction — "asc" or "desc". Required with sorting_column.
- columns (optional) — REPLACE the scan's extra result columns (beyond the filters' own columns and the standard defaults). guide.description:
How to interpret the response:
- result.sorted_by — the sort in effect ("Volume desc" etc.).
- result.columns — the scan's columns after the change (when columns were passed, verify the intended set landed; expression columns matching a standard column adopt its canonical name).
- result.results — live results reflecting the change.
- The change is persisted: subsequent run_scan calls on this scan_id will return rows accordingly.

- Confirm what changed (sort, columns, or both) to the user.
- Render the results as a table. Eyeball-verify a sort change with the user if they care: the top rows should match the requested direction.
- Mention that the change is saved for future runs of the scan.

- "no column named X" → the requested sorting_column does not match any column. The error message lists available columns — relay them to the user and ask which they meant. - "created by Cortex" → the scan is read-only via MCP. Suggest creating a fresh scan via create_scan.
- "scan X does not exist or you do not have access" → bad scan_id. Suggest get_scans.

name: update_scan_filters
description:
Replace the filters on an existing saved scan. The complete filter set provided replaces whatever filters the scan had — this is REPLACE semantics, not merge. To add a single filter to an existing scan, the agent must first read the scan (via get_scans or run_scan), then call this tool with all the existing filters plus the new one.

Parameters:
- scan_id (required) — the scan to modify. Get from get_scans or create_scan.
- filters (required) — the complete new filter set. Send [] to clear all filters. Each filter has filter_type (FILTER_TYPE_... enum), predicate, values, optional interval/length. Call get_scanner_filter_specs for valid combinations.

Restrictions:
- Cortex-managed scans (cortex_managed: true in get_scans) are rejected with a user-friendly error.
- Returns an error and does not apply any change if any filter fails validation.

Returns the scan with its new filters and fresh live results.

guide.description:
How to interpret the response:
- result.filters_applied lists the filters that are now in effect on the scan. Confirm this matches what the user requested.
- result.total_items reflects matches under the new filter set — tighter filters typically lower this count.
- result.results is fresh live data evaluated against the new filters.

When presenting:
- Confirm exactly which filters are now active (filters_applied) — useful especially after add/remove operations where the user wants to know the new total filter set.
- Mention the new total_items so the user sees the impact of the change.
- Render the new results as a table.
- If results is empty: tell the user no instruments match the new filter set. Suggest relaxing one filter (and offer to call update_scan_filters again with the relaxed set).

Columns display values, filters screen: to show a datapoint in the scan's results without restricting matches, do NOT add a filter here (a ">= 0" filter is not a no-op — it silently drops instruments where the datapoint is undefined, and it pollutes the scan's filter list). Use update_scan_config's columns parameter instead; it keeps this scan's filters untouched.

REPLACE-semantics callout:
- If the user said "add a market cap filter" but the request payload only had the new filter (not the existing ones), the existing filters were dropped because update_scan_filters REPLACES the filter set. Surface this if the result's filters_applied is shorter than expected. Recovery: read the scan via get_scans/run_scan, then call again with the full intended set — carry each existing filter over using its filter_type_enum value, since filter_type is a display label and is not accepted here. A filter whose filter_type_enum is FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM cannot be carried over here — it is defined by an expression, which this tool does not accept. To keep it, use create_scan instead with this scan's scan_id and the full intended filter set, passing that filter's expression in the expression field (the scan gets a new configuration version; earlier versions are preserved). Never send FILTER_TYPE_CUSTOM as a filter_type — it creates an empty filter.

- "filter[N]: ..." → validation failure at filter index N. Tell the user which filter and why.
- "created by Cortex" → the scan is read-only via MCP. Suggest creating a fresh scan via create_scan as the alternative.
- "scan X does not exist or you do not have access" → bad scan_id. Suggest get_scans.
